BRCA1 deficiency in ER-negative breast cancer: cell of origin and immune evasion
Extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA) in ER-positive breast cancer

headline: Six papers hand over the cell states this lab works on, and not one of them scores the immune step
summary: The strongest paper of the week is the lab's own question asked in the lab's own model class: Lev et al. argue that BRCA1 triple-negative breast cancer also starts in the basal-myoepithelial compartment, giving the mesenchymal subtype, while the luminal route gives the basal-like subtype, and their within-model transplant of matched sorted fractions is the part worth reading closely. On the ovarian side, Pirttikoski et al. trace the chemoresistant HGSOC state back to a MAPK and NF-kB module that already exists in normal fallopian tube epithelium, and Qian et al. show that in human HGSOC, BRCA deficiency raises interferon and antigen presentation inside a T, NK and dendritic cell region without changing the overall tissue architecture. On the ecDNA side, Hung and colleagues show that damaged ecDNA is swept into a single micronucleus where it stops transcribing, and that cells inheriting it do worse, while Wang et al. separate ecDNA position from copy number with the lamin B receptor as the tether. The common gap is the same in every direction: these papers deliver the cell states, the spatial maps and the molecular handles, and then stop exactly where the lab's model starts. The micronucleus paper is the sharpest case, since it puts oncogenic DNA into the exact compartment the lab's BRCA1 chain begins in and then measures fitness and survival rather than cGAS, interferon, MHC class I or NK surveillance. That gap is the lab's contribution to make.
cross_links: The micronuclear ecDNA paper is the bridge the lab has been waiting for, and it stops one step short. Replication stress sweeps damaged ecDNA into a single micronucleus, which is precisely the cytosolic DNA source the lab's BRCA1 model starts from, yet the paper measures no cGAS, STING, interferon, MHC or NK readout anywhere. Its only immune-shaped item is one hallmark enrichment panel in hydroxyurea treated versus untreated bulk cells, with no direction of change reported and no link to the micronucleated cells themselves, so it cannot be read as an immune result. Worth noting in the other direction: they use Lamin B1 to argue these micronuclei keep an intact inner membrane, which if it holds would make them poor cGAS substrates, so the lab should test rupture directly rather than assume it.

Lev and Mohd use Cre drivers that mark the same compartment. Lev argues that Wap-Cre basal-myoepithelial cells give rise to the mesenchymal TNBC subtype, and Mohd's PARP inhibitor tumors come from K14-Cre, a basal and myoepithelial driver, so Mohd's olaparib sensitivity and resistance maps may be reporting one lineage rather than BRCA1 tumors in general. Reading the two together is the cheapest way to test that.

Pirttikoski puts the MAPK and NF-kB module at the LATE end of the fallopian tube trajectory, which is the opposite orientation to the lab's model, where NF-kB and JAK/STAT favour a progenitor-like, less differentiated state. Their axis is RNA velocity latent time in secretory cells with ciliated cells excluded, so it may not be the lab's differentiation axis at all. Scoring the lab's own markers against their modules E7 and E9 would settle it, and their unused E1 module is the JAK/STAT one.

Qian is the human readout the lab's BRCA1 model predicts, but in the ovary rather than the breast: BRCA deficiency associated with higher interferon alpha and gamma, higher antigen processing and presentation and higher TNF and NF-kB signalling, in a region genuinely enriched for T, NK and dendritic cells. It is corroboration one organ over, not a test of the breast chain, and MHC appears only as an aggregate score with no HLA-C, HLA-E or NKG2A breakout.

Pirttikoski and Qian both carry large stromal and immune compartments that they annotate and then use only as a reference: 18,974 stromal and 80,764 immune cells in the DECIDER cohort, and a fibroblast to lipid-associated macrophage CXCL12 and CXCR4 axis in Qian. Neither paper asks whether estrogen does anything to those cells, which is exactly the lab's question.
actions: Take the micronucleus paper's induction and readout toolkit and run the lab's own immune panel on it: hydroxyurea at 50 to 80 micromolar for 24 hours to 3 days as the replication stress, oncogene FISH with a centromere probe to call micronuclei oncogene-positive, and targeted Cas9 cutting of one ecDNA species as a non-genotoxic way to force an amplicon into a micronucleus. Then score cGAS recruitment, micronuclear rupture, interferon and MHC class I, which is the step they did not take.

Score Lev's tumor basal and fetal-like basal states, and their luminal-derived counterparts, for the lab's interferon and MHC class I panel. Their immunocompetent material is the spontaneous Wap-Cre glands and tumors only, since the transplants went into NSG mice, and the paper's data deposition is not stated in the retrievable text, so it may be worth writing to Lawson.

Take Pirttikoski's modules E7 and E9 and score the lab's progenitor and differentiation markers against them, to decide whether their late NF-kB axis and the lab's progenitor-like NF-kB state are the same axis read in opposite directions. Their E1 module is the JAK/STAT one and they never follow it up.

Borrow Qian's analysis template for the lab's own spatial work: patient-level aggregation of spot scores, join count analysis as a negative control for architecture, and a treatment-adjusted linear model as a sensitivity check.
Decide whether the ecDNA arm wants to test position rather than dose in ER-positive breast models, using the isogenic double minute versus HSR design and the LBR knockout handle from Wang et al.

papers.title: NF-kB-mediated chemoresistance emerges from distorted fallopian tube cell-state trajectory in ovarian cancer
papers.authors: Anna Pirttikoski, Shabnaz Koochakkhani, Laura Gall-Mas, Wojciech Senkowski, David Fontaneda-Arenas, Jun Dai, Matias Marin Falco, Erdogan Pekcan Erkan, Johanna Hynninen, Krister Wennerberg, Anna Vaharautio

bibliographic.title: NF-kB-mediated chemoresistance emerges from distorted fallopian tube cell-state trajectory in ovarian cancer

reading.one_line_takeaway: The chemoresistant, poor prognosis state of high-grade serous ovarian cancer is not a newly invented cancer program but a developmentally late MAPK and NF-kB gene module that already exists in normal fallopian tube epithelium, and inhibiting CCDC6 shifts organoids out of that state and back toward platinum sensitivity.
reading.tldr: The authors asked whether the cell states that make high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma (HGSC) heterogeneous and treatment resistant are new cancer inventions or reused programs of the tissue the cancer comes from, the fallopian tube epithelium (FTE). They built continuous gene co-expression modules from single-cell RNA sequencing of 52 treatment-naive HGSC samples from 50 patients plus normal postmenopausal FTE, instead of carving the cells into discrete clusters. Two of the nine shared epithelial modules sat at opposite ends of an inferred differentiation trajectory and had opposite survival associations: an early oxidative phosphorylation module E7 went with longer survival and with homologous recombination deficiency, while a late MAPK and NF-kB module E9 went with shorter survival and marked a stable state that, unlike its normal FTE counterpart, had lost MHC class II antigen presentation regulators. Using a published genome-scale Perturb-seq screen to pick candidate targets, they then showed in five patient-derived organoid lines that the USP7 inhibitor XL177A, which destabilises CCDC6, lowers phospho-p65 and phospho-ERK and synergises with carboplatin, whereas the SERCA2 activator N106 raises NF-kB signalling and is neutral to antagonistic with carboplatin. Their conclusion is that conserved tissue-of-origin states, not de novo cancer states, drive this heterogeneity in clinical response, and that those states are pharmacologically movable.
reading.research_question: Do the transcriptional cell states that create intratumoral heterogeneity and platinum resistance in high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma arise de novo during tumorigenesis, or are they conserved gene expression programs inherited from the normal fallopian tube epithelium, and can those states be shifted with small molecules to change chemotherapy response?
reading.background: HGSC is usually found late, almost always carries a TP53 mutation, is driven mainly by copy number change rather than recurrent point mutations, and has a five year survival of 43 percent. Survival has improved only for homologous recombination deficient tumours treated with PARP inhibitors. Several lines of evidence point to the fallopian tube epithelium as the tissue of origin: fallopian tube lesions carry the same TP53 mutations as the tumour and this p53 signature can progress through serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma to HGSC, and HGSC transcriptomes resemble FTE more than ovarian surface epithelium. In other cancers, tumour gene modules often turn out to be reused normal tissue programs such as stress response, interferon response and differentiation. The gap the authors state is that earlier single-cell studies of fallopian tube had few postmenopausal donors and that no matched single-cell HGSC tissue data existed, so normal states had to be projected onto bulk tumour RNA-seq rather than compared cell to cell at matched resolution. The authors also argue against the common practice of treating cell states as discrete clusters, since states coexist and are plastic.
reading.study_design: Single-cell RNA sequencing of 52 treatment-naive HGSC samples from 50 patients, collected at laparoscopy or primary debulking from peritoneum, omentum, mesentery, ovary, ascites, adnexa or fallopian tube, all from the DECIDER study (NCT04846933). The dataset combines 16 previously unpublished and 43 previously published samples. Normal controls were 7 fallopian tube or fimbrial samples from postmenopausal women without an HGSC diagnosis, one of whom carried a germline TP53 mutation (Li-Fraumeni syndrome). An external published single-cell dataset of secretory FTE from 7 postmenopausal donors (3,614 secretory cells) was added for differential expression; the abstract reports n = 14 normal FTE samples, which corresponds to these 7 in-house plus 7 external donors, although the text does not state that arithmetic explicitly. After filtering, 131,225 cells were retained: 30,236 malignant epithelial, 1,251 secretory FTE, 80,764 immune and 18,974 stromal. Ciliated cells were excluded from the main analysis but used in trajectory validation. Key comparisons were cancer epithelium versus secretory FTE versus tumour microenvironment (for gene selection), module activity across cells and samples, module activity versus inferred latent time, module activity versus inferCNV subclone identity, and module activity versus overall survival and homologous recombination status in deconvoluted TCGA bulk RNA-seq from 258 HGSC patients. Replication used an independent published HGSC single-cell dataset of 211,624 cells from 41 patients. The functional arm used five patient-derived organoid lines from the same cohort, tested with candidate compounds alone and with carboplatin, read out by viability, bulk RNA-seq (2 organoids) and phospho-protein western blot (all 5 organoids).

key_methods.name: Single-cell RNA sequencing of treatment-naive HGSC and normal fallopian tube
key_methods.plain_explanation: Single-cell RNA sequencing measures which genes are switched on in each individual cell rather than averaging over a whole piece of tissue. Tissue is broken apart into single cells, each cell is captured in its own droplet together with a barcoded bead so that every RNA molecule from that cell carries the same tag, and the tagged RNA is sequenced and reassigned to cells computationally. The result is a table of roughly 20,000 genes by tens of thousands of cells, from which cell types and cell states can be read directly.
key_methods.how_used: 10x Genomics Chromium Single Cell 3-prime v2 chemistry, sequenced on HiSeq4000, HiSeq2500 and NovaSeq6000, aligned with Cell Ranger v3.1.0 to GRCh38 and processed in Seurat v4 with sctransform normalisation, 50 principal components and 30 dimensions for UMAP. Cells with more than 20 percent mitochondrial reads were discarded, doublets were removed where stromal or immune markers such as DCN, LUM or PTPRC co-occurred with the epithelial markers MUC16 and PAX8, and cell-type-specific count thresholds were applied. Cell types were called from canonical markers (MUC16, PAX8, WFDC2 for cancer epithelium, FOXJ1 and PIFO for ciliated, OVGP1 for secretory, COL1A2 and DCN for stromal, CD14, CD3D and PTPRC for immune). Post-thaw viability of the frozen samples ranged from 26.4 to 94.9 percent, median 83.1 percent.
key_methods.why_it_matters: This is what makes a cell-by-cell comparison between tumour epithelium and normal fallopian tube epithelium possible at all, which is the whole premise of the paper. The caveat is that cancer cell yield varied widely between samples and that only 1,251 in-house secretory FTE cells were recovered, so the normal side of the comparison leans heavily on a small number of cells plus one external dataset.

key_methods.name: Pseudobulk differential expression followed by CS-CORE and WGCNA gene module construction
key_methods.plain_explanation: A gene module is a group of genes whose expression rises and falls together across cells, which usually means they serve a common program. To find modules the authors first chose which genes to consider, by summing each sample's cells into one pseudo-bulk profile per cell type and asking which genes differ between cancer epithelium, normal secretory epithelium and the surrounding microenvironment. They then measured how strongly each surviving gene pair co-varies across single cells using CS-CORE, a method that corrects for the technical noise and sequencing-depth differences that otherwise inflate single-cell correlations, and finally grouped the genes by hierarchical clustering of that correlation structure using WGCNA.
key_methods.how_used: Pseudobulk differential expression with edgeR and limma-voom, requiring adjusted p below 0.05, expression in at least 10 percent of cells of the group, at least a two-fold difference, protein-coding genes only, and no ribosomal or mitochondrial genes; samples with fewer than 50 cells of a type were dropped, which excluded 9 tumour and 2 fallopian tube samples. This produced 229 cancer-specific, 257 normal-specific and 598 shared epithelial genes. CS-CORE correlations that were not significant after Benjamini-Hochberg correction were set to zero, then WGCNA with dynamic tree cutting produced 6 cancer-specific modules C1 to C6, 4 normal-specific modules N1 to N4, and 9 shared epithelial modules E1 to E9. Shared epithelial genes were co-expressed separately in cancer and in normal cells and the two correlation matrices averaged.
key_methods.why_it_matters: Building modules from shared epithelial genes is what lets the same program be scored in a tumour cell and in a normal fallopian tube cell, which is how the authors can claim a state is conserved rather than cancer-specific. The caveat the authors themselves raise is that sample-specific effects can mask broadly conserved programs, and that the soft-threshold power, minimum module size and merging settings for WGCNA are not reported.

key_methods.name: Per-cell module and pathway scoring with UCell, PROGENy and decoupleR
key_methods.plain_explanation: Once a gene set is defined you need a number per cell saying how active it is. UCell does this by ranking all genes within each cell and asking how near the top the gene set sits, which makes the score robust to how deeply each cell was sequenced. PROGENy estimates the activity of a signalling pathway not from the pathway's own components but from the downstream genes that respond when the pathway is on, which is a more reliable readout of signalling than the expression of the receptor or kinase itself. decoupleR with the CollecTRI network does the same trick for transcription factors, inferring a factor's activity from the behaviour of the genes it is known to regulate.
key_methods.how_used: Module activity was scored per cell with UCell at default parameters and module-active cells were the top 25 percent by score, with 10 percent, per-sample 25 percent and 50 percent thresholds also tested. Fourteen PROGENy pathway activities were estimated per cell and Spearman-correlated with module scores separately in cancer and normal cells, with non-significant correlations set to zero and cells subsampled to the median per sample count (236 cancer, 151 normal) to stop large samples dominating. MSigDB hallmark gene sets were scored the same way. Transcription factor activity used decoupleR v2.10.0 with a univariate linear model on gene statistics of minus log p times log fold change.
key_methods.why_it_matters: These scores are what turn the modules into interpretable biology: they are how E9 was tied to MAPK and NF-kB and E7 to oxidative phosphorylation, and how NF-kB, RELA, JUN, ATF4 and DDIT3 were named as the transcription factors behind E9. The caveat is that all of this is correlative and computed from the same expression matrix, so pathway activity here means a downstream transcriptional footprint and not a measured phosphorylation event, which is part of why the organoid western blots were needed.

key_methods.name: RNA velocity and latent time ordering (velocyto, scVelo, CellRank)
key_methods.plain_explanation: RNA velocity exploits the fact that a newly transcribed RNA still contains introns while a mature RNA does not. If a gene's unspliced, intron-containing reads are high relative to its spliced reads, that gene is being switched on, and if the ratio is reversed it is being switched off. Summed over many genes this gives each cell an arrow pointing toward the state it is heading for, and from those arrows a program can infer a starting point, an end point and a continuous pseudo-time called latent time that orders cells along a trajectory. Importantly this is inferred from a single snapshot, not measured by following real cells over time.
key_methods.how_used: velocyto v0.17.17 counted spliced and unspliced reads with repeats masked, scVelo v0.2.3 fitted the dynamical model, and CellRank v1.3.1 identified root and terminal states and computed latent time, done separately for each sample with more than 100 cells. Latent time was then Spearman-correlated with each module score within each sample, and only correlations with adjusted p below 0.05 were averaged across samples. Control fallopian tube samples were analysed with ciliated cells included to check the trajectory direction.
key_methods.why_it_matters: This is the step that produces the paper's central and most provocative claim, that the NF-kB state is developmentally late rather than early or stem-like. It is also the weakest link in the chain, because latent time is an inference from splicing ratios in a static snapshot and the authors explicitly list this as a limitation; the direction of the trajectory rests on the external check that secretory cells have lower latent time than ciliated cells in 5 of 6 samples.

key_methods.name: inferCNV subclone reconstruction
key_methods.plain_explanation: Cancer genomes gain and lose chromosomal segments, and a gene sitting in an amplified region tends to be expressed higher simply because there are more copies of it. inferCNV uses this by sliding a window along each chromosome and averaging expression of neighbouring genes in each cell, comparing it with normal reference cells from the same patient. Smooth region-wide shifts reveal copy number changes, and cells sharing the same pattern are grouped into genetic subclones. This lets a genetic family tree be read out of an RNA experiment.
key_methods.how_used: inferCNV v1.7.1 with cutoff 0.1, subcluster analysis mode, denoising, Leiden resolution 0.5 and a hidden Markov model reported per cell, using each patient's own immune and stromal cells as the normal reference. Chi-square tests asked whether E7-high and E9-high cells fell into different subclones, restricted to patients with more than one subclone and subclones with more than 10 cells, covering 10,615 module-active cells, and compared against random module assignments of equal group size.
key_methods.why_it_matters: It addresses the obvious alternative explanation, that these are not plastic states at all but just genetically distinct clones. The answer the authors get is intermediate: module activity is significantly biased across subclones in 22 of 30 patients, so there is genetic structure to the states, but no single genetic driver emerges, so they argue the states are neither purely plastic nor purely clonal.

key_methods.name: Deconvoluted TCGA bulk RNA-seq with ovaHRDscar homologous recombination calling and survival analysis
key_methods.plain_explanation: Bulk RNA-seq of a tumour mixes cancer cells with stroma and immune cells, so a signal from one compartment can be diluted or faked by another. Deconvolution estimates the cancer-cell-only expression profile from the bulk mixture so that an epithelial module can be scored without microenvironment contamination. Homologous recombination deficiency means the cell cannot repair double-strand DNA breaks by copying the intact sister chromosome, which leaves a characteristic scar pattern of structural rearrangements in the genome; ovaHRDscar reads that scar pattern to classify a tumour as deficient or proficient.
key_methods.how_used: Deconvoluted bulk RNA-seq from 258 grade 3 and 4 HGSC patients with overall survival data. Module-high versus module-low groups were split at a threshold optimised with max.stat, and compared by Kaplan-Meier curves and log-rank tests. ovaHRDscar assigned 138 patients as homologous recombination deficient and 111 as proficient for the Fig. 4A comparison. A multivariable Cox model included module activity, homologous recombination status and age. Copy number calls came from cBioPortal GISTIC data for 248 of the 258 patients, limited to driver genes amplified in at least 10 patients.
key_methods.why_it_matters: This is the only place the modules are connected to patient outcome, so it carries the clinical claim. Keeping both modules significant in the Cox model after adjusting for homologous recombination status and age is what lets the authors argue that the E7 survival benefit is not simply a restatement of the known PARP-inhibitor-sensitive, repair-deficient good-prognosis group.

key_methods.name: Perturb-seq based target prioritisation and patient-derived organoid drug testing with Bliss synergy
key_methods.plain_explanation: Perturb-seq is a pooled CRISPR screen read out by single-cell RNA sequencing: thousands of genes are knocked down one per cell and the whole transcriptome is measured, so for every knocked-down gene you get the expression change it causes. The authors used a published screen of this kind as a lookup table, asking which knockdown would push cells away from the bad module and toward the good one. A patient-derived organoid is a three-dimensional mini-tumour grown from a patient's own cancer cells in extracellular matrix, which keeps the patient's genetics and lets drugs be tested directly. Bliss synergy asks whether two drugs together kill more cells than you would expect if each acted independently, scoring above 10 as synergy and below minus 10 as antagonism.
key_methods.how_used: A genome-scale Perturb-seq dataset in RPE1 cells covering 2,394 knockdown genes was Spearman-correlated with the module signatures, looking for knockdowns that lower E9 and raise E7, which put CCDC6 top on both counts and flagged ATP2A2 (encoding the endoplasmic reticulum calcium pump SERCA2) as negatively correlated with E9; LSM12 and USP9X also fitted but were deprioritised because their expression did not separate cancer from normal FTE or microenvironment cells. Two organoid lines were screened first across four tenfold dilutions from 10 nM to 10 uM, alone and with a line-specific carboplatin dose over 7 days, read out with CellTox Green and Hoechst imaging; the two chosen compounds were then tested in five organoid lines in total with CellTiter-Glo 3D viability. XL177A reaches CCDC6 indirectly by inhibiting USP7, the deubiquitinase that stabilises CCDC6, and N106 is a SERCA2 activator.
key_methods.why_it_matters: This is the only causal, interventional part of the paper and it is what lifts the modules above correlation: if pushing CCDC6 down sensitises to carboplatin and pushing SERCA2 up raises NF-kB and removes that benefit, the state is a lever and not just a marker. The authors are candid that the Perturb-seq data came from RPE1 retinal pigment epithelium, a non-cancerous line with no fallopian tube identity and none of the copy number burden of HGSC, so the screen was used only to generate candidates, and that five organoid lines cannot establish generality.

key_concepts.term: Gene module as a continuous cell state
key_concepts.plain_definition: A gene module is a set of genes whose expression levels move up and down together across cells, which normally means the cells are running a shared program such as a metabolic mode, a stress response or a stage of differentiation. Treating a module as continuous means every cell gets a graded score for every module rather than being assigned to exactly one cluster, so a single cell can be partly in one state and partly in another, and can slide between them. This paper rests on that choice: the authors argue that discrete clustering forces plastic, coexisting states into artificial boxes, and that scoring modules continuously is what allowed the same program to be recognised in both a tumour cell and a normal fallopian tube cell.

The authors split genes into three pools before building modules. Cancer-specific genes are higher in tumour epithelium than in both normal secretory epithelium and the surrounding microenvironment, normal-specific genes are higher in normal secretory epithelium than in both of the others, and shared epithelial genes are higher in both epithelial populations than in the microenvironment, so they mark epithelium in general rather than malignancy. Modules were built separately within each pool, giving 6 cancer modules, 4 normal modules and 9 shared epithelial modules. The paper's argument lives in the shared pool: a state built only from shared epithelial genes can be measured identically in cancer and normal tissue, which is the only way to ask whether a cancer state was inherited from the tissue of origin.

key_concepts.term: RNA velocity and latent time (inferred pseudotime)
key_concepts.plain_definition: RNA velocity estimates which direction each cell is moving transcriptionally from a single snapshot, by comparing each gene's newly made intron-containing RNA with its mature spliced RNA. High unspliced relative to spliced means the gene is being turned on, the reverse means it is being turned off, and summing over genes gives a direction of travel per cell. Latent time is the continuous ordering of cells along the resulting trajectory, scaled from 0 at the inferred root to 1 at the inferred endpoint. It is a computational inference about dynamics from static data, not a measurement of real elapsed time, so terms like early and late in this paper mean early and late along an inferred transcriptional trajectory.

key_concepts.term: NF-kB and the TNFalpha signalling via NF-kB program
key_concepts.plain_definition: NF-kB is a family of transcription factors, with RELA (p65) as the main activating subunit, that normally sit inhibited in the cytoplasm and move into the nucleus when the cell receives an inflammatory or stress signal, where they switch on cytokines, survival and anti-apoptotic genes. Because active NF-kB promotes cell survival, chronic NF-kB signalling is a classical route to resistance against DNA-damaging chemotherapy. The MSigDB hallmark set called TNFalpha signalling via NF-kB is the downstream transcriptional footprint of this pathway, so a cell scoring high on it is one whose NF-kB target genes are on, regardless of which upstream ligand turned them on. In this paper that footprint is the defining feature of the E9 module, and its protein-level counterpart was measured as phosphorylation of p65 at serine 536.

Oxidative phosphorylation is the mitochondrial process that extracts most of a cell's usable energy, passing electrons along the respiratory chain complexes in the inner mitochondrial membrane to pump protons and then using that gradient to make ATP. A cell with a high OXPHOS transcriptional program is running mitochondrial respiration heavily rather than relying on glycolysis, which usually signals a metabolically active, relatively unstressed state. Here OXPHOS defines the E7 module, which the authors also find enriched for DNA repair genes, associated with homologous recombination deficiency and with longer survival, and whose transcription factor signature is MYC and PPARGC1A rather than inflammatory factors.

Homologous recombination is the accurate way a cell repairs a double-strand DNA break, by copying the missing sequence from the intact matching chromosome. When the machinery for this fails, most often through BRCA1 or BRCA2 loss, the cell falls back on error-prone repair and accumulates a characteristic pattern of structural rearrangements in its genome that can be scored after the fact as a genomic scar. HRD tumours respond better to platinum chemotherapy and to PARP inhibitors, so they form the known good-prognosis subgroup of HGSC. That is why the authors had to show that the E7 survival benefit remained significant in a Cox model adjusted for HRD status and age: otherwise E7 could simply have been rediscovering HRD.

key_concepts.term: MHC class II antigen presentation and the RFX complex
key_concepts.plain_definition: MHC class II molecules display fragments of proteins on the cell surface to CD4 T helper cells, and unlike MHC class I they are normally restricted to dedicated antigen-presenting cells, although epithelial cells can switch them on under inflammatory conditions. Their transcription requires a specific complex, RFX5 together with RFXAP and RFXANK, which binds the MHC class II promoter and recruits the master regulator CIITA. Losing this axis removes a cell's ability to be recognised by CD4 T cells. In this paper the normal fallopian tube version of the late E9 state has high inferred activity of RFX5, RFXAP and RFXANK, while in the cancer version this axis is lower, which the authors read as loss of a highly antigen-presenting epithelial state during tumorigenesis. Note that this is MHC class II only; MHC class I, HLA-A, HLA-B, HLA-C, HLA-E and B2M are not examined anywhere in the paper.

A patient-derived organoid is a three-dimensional culture grown from a patient's own tumour cells embedded in a basement-membrane-like extracellular matrix, where the cells self-organise into small structures that keep much of the original tumour's genetics and drug response. Unlike a cell line it is specific to one patient and relatively short-lived, and unlike a mouse xenograft it can be dosed directly and read out quickly. The organoids used here were genomically validated and, importantly for interpreting the results, contain cancer cells only, with no stromal or immune cells, so any signalling change seen in them is happening inside the cancer cells without input from the microenvironment.

When two drugs are combined you need a baseline for what their joint effect should be if they do not interact. The Bliss independence model assumes the two act on cells independently, so the expected surviving fraction is simply the product of the two individual surviving fractions. The Bliss score is the gap between the observed and this expected effect, with a score above 10 called synergistic, meaning the combination kills more than independence predicts, and below minus 10 antagonistic, meaning the drugs get in each other's way. Here it is the readout for whether a state-shifting compound genuinely resensitises organoids to carboplatin, which is what separates XL177A from N106.

Perturb-seq is a pooled CRISPR screen whose readout is the whole transcriptome of single cells. Each cell receives a guide RNA that knocks down one gene, the guide identity is captured along with the cell's RNA, and the result is a map from each perturbed gene to the full expression change it causes. That map can be used backwards: given a transcriptional state you want to leave, you can look up which gene knockdown produces the opposite expression shift. The authors used a published genome-scale Perturb-seq dataset in RPE1 cells this way to nominate CCDC6 and ATP2A2, and are explicit that RPE1 is a non-cancerous retinal pigment epithelial line with no fallopian tube identity and none of HGSC's copy number burden, so the predictions were only a way to choose candidates for testing.

figures.label: Fig. 1
figures.title: Identification of epithelial gene modules and their pathway and survival associations in HGSC
figures.question: Can gene co-expression modules be defined that are shared between HGSC and normal fallopian tube epithelium, and do any of them carry prognostic information?
figures.how_to_read: Panel a is the workflow schematic: pseudobulk differential expression splits genes into cancer-specific, normal-FTE-specific and shared epithelial sets using an external fallopian tube secretory dataset, CS-CORE computes confounder-controlled co-expression, and WGCNA hierarchical clustering cuts the result into modules. Panel b is a UMAP of 31,487 epithelial cells, coloured by sample origin (tumour versus fallopian tube) on the left and by patient on the right, so patient-driven separation shows up as patient colours occupying separate territories. Panel c shows violin plots of UCell module activity in cancer versus secretory FTE cells, one violin pair per module. Panel d is a correlation heatmap of module activity against the 14 PROGENy pathway activities computed at single-cell level in 15,948 cancer cells, so each cell of the heatmap is a module-by-pathway Spearman correlation. Panel e shows Kaplan-Meier overall survival curves in the TCGA cohort splitting patients into module-high and module-low, with numbers at risk underneath.
figures.key_result: Six cancer-specific (C1 to C6), four normal-specific (N1 to N4) and nine shared epithelial (E1 to E9) modules were defined. Cancer-specific modules were more active in cancer cells and normal-specific modules in FTE cells (p below 2e-16) while epithelial modules were more evenly active in both. Among PROGENy pathways, E9 correlated most strongly with MAPK and NF-kB and E1 with JAK-STAT, in both cancer and normal cells. In TCGA (n = 258), E7-high tumours had longer overall survival (log-rank p = 0.0025) and E9-high tumours shorter overall survival (log-rank p = 0.0015).

figures.label: Fig. 2
figures.title: Cross-sample consistency of the epithelial modules and the signalling and transcription factor activity that distinguishes E7 from E9
figures.question: Are E7 and E9 reproducible structures across many heterogeneous tumours rather than artefacts of individual samples, and which signalling pathways and transcription factors separate them?
figures.how_to_read: Panels a to c are UMAPs of the same 31,487 epithelial cells after Harmony integration, coloured by sample origin and patient (a), by E7 and E9 UCell activity (b), and by the eight clusters found at resolution 0.3 (c). Harmony was used only for visualisation and clustering; the module scores themselves come from unintegrated data. Panels d and e are violin plots across those eight clusters, showing E7 activity on top and E9 activity below in d, and PROGENy MAPK activity on top and NF-kB activity below in e, so a cluster where the d and e violins rise together is where module and pathway coincide. Panel f is a waterfall plot of inferred transcription factor activity change between the E9 and E7 states, with the top 10 factors up in E9 to one side and the top 10 down to the other.
figures.key_result: E7 activity peaked in cluster 5 and E9 in cluster 7 followed by cluster 4, with MAPK strongly enriched in cluster 7 and NF-kB highest in cluster 4 and also elevated in cluster 7. E9 showed higher inferred activity of NF-kB, RELA, JUN, JUND, ATF4 and DDIT3, while E7 showed higher PPARGC1A, GABPA, MYC, HCFC1 and ZBTB4, which the authors read as a stress and inflammatory state versus a metabolically active low-stress state. In an independent 41-patient HGSC dataset E9 again tracked TGF-beta, MAPK and NF-kB (r = 0.21, 0.19, 0.18) and E7 tracked negatively with NF-kB and TNFalpha (r = minus 0.18, minus 0.17).

figures.label: Fig. 3
figures.title: The poor-prognosis module sits late along the inferred epithelial differentiation trajectory in both cancer and normal fallopian tube
figures.question: Where along an inferred differentiation trajectory does each module sit, and does the normal fallopian tube version of the late state differ from the cancer version?
figures.how_to_read: Panel a shows histograms of per-sample correlations between CellRank latent time and the modules with the strongest average correlations, restricted to correlations with p below 0.05, so a histogram shifted off zero means the association is consistent across samples. Panel b plots the average latent-time correlation for every module, cancer samples on top and fallopian tube samples below, with points coloured by module group, so position left of zero means early and right of zero means late. Panel c shows, for three cancer samples, UMAPs of latent time (scaled 0 early to 1 late) beside UMAPs of E9 activity with velocity arrows overlaid. Panel d uses control sample 1, a normal fallopian tube from a woman with a germline TP53 mutation, coloured by FTE subtype with the top 25 percent of cells for E7 or E9 marked, and by latent time, with box plots comparing latent time between the most E7-high secretory cells, the most E9-high secretory cells and ciliated cells. Panel e is a waterfall plot of transcription factor activity change within the E9 state, cancer versus normal epithelium.
figures.key_result: In cancer samples E2 and E9 correlated positively with latent time (mean r = 0.33 and 0.32) and E3 and E7 negatively (mean r = minus 0.27 and minus 0.26); in the smaller set of normal FTE samples the same pattern was stronger (E2 0.52, E9 0.45, E3 minus 0.46, E7 minus 0.52). Secretory cells had lower latent time than ciliated cells in 5 of 6 samples analysed, and E7-high secretory cells preceded E9-high secretory cells, placing E9 late in epithelial differentiation. Within the E9 state, normal FTE showed higher SRF, ELK4 and ELK1 activity and higher activity of the MHC class II regulators RFXAP, RFXANK and RFX5, which were lower in the cancer version of the same state.

figures.label: Fig. 4
figures.title: Genetic associations of the two prognostic modules with homologous recombination status and subclonal structure
figures.question: Are these continuous states explained by tumour genetics, specifically homologous recombination deficiency or copy number subclones?
figures.how_to_read: Panel a is a box plot of E7 activity in homologous recombination deficient (n = 138) versus proficient (n = 111) TCGA patients, compared by Wilcoxon rank-sum test. Panel b is a histogram of FDR-adjusted p values from chi-square tests asking whether E7-high and E9-high cells distribute differently across inferCNV subclones in 30 patients, with the observed distribution plotted against a null obtained by randomly reassigning modules to groups of the same size; subclones with fewer than 10 cells were excluded. Panel c takes cancer samples 1 and 29 and shows UMAPs coloured by which module is most active on top and by subclone identity below, with stacked bar plots giving the subclone composition of E7-high and E9-high cells.
figures.key_result: E7 activity was higher in homologous recombination deficient tumours (Wilcoxon p = 0.0012) while E9 did not differ (p = 0.78), and in a Cox model including homologous recombination status and age both E7 (p = 0.024) and E9 (p = 0.014) remained associated with overall survival. Genes enriched in BRCA1-mutant COV362 cells were upregulated in E7-high cells (adjusted p = 0.0016, NES = 1.42) and genes enriched in the BRCA1-restored wild-type counterpart were downregulated (adjusted p = 2e-10, NES = minus 3.38). Module activity was significantly associated with subclone identity overall (p = 1.75e-264) and in 22 of 30 individual patients after FDR adjustment, with no association under random assignment. Associations with individual driver amplifications (E9 higher with CCND3 amplification p = 0.02, E7 lower with AKT2 amplification p = 0.045) did not survive multiple-testing correction.

figures.label: Fig. 5
figures.title: Small-molecule targeting of the E9 state in patient-derived organoids
figures.question: Can the late NF-kB-associated state be shifted pharmacologically, and does shifting it change carboplatin response?
figures.how_to_read: Panel a is the schematic: module signature log fold changes are compared with z-normalised expression changes from genetically perturbed cells, candidate compounds are then tested with carboplatin in organoids. Panel b shows box plots (Kruskal-Wallis) of ATP2A2 and CCDC6 expression within the E9 state, averaged per sample, compared across cancer cells, secretory epithelial cells and tumour microenvironment cells. Panel c gives Bliss synergy scores for XL177A and N106 with carboplatin across organoid models, where above 10 is synergistic and below minus 10 antagonistic. Panel d is a bar plot of the top three PROGENy pathways by relative activity in E9 versus E7 together with the drugs' effects on those pathways, asterisks marking pathways still significant after FDR correction. Panel e is a dot plot of the top 20 transcription factors enriched in E9 relative to E7 and their behaviour under drug treatment, colour giving inferred activity score and dot size giving minus log10 p, with factors at p of 0.05 or above drawn without an outline. Panel f quantifies phospho-protein western blots after N106 or XL177A, as log2 fold change versus untreated control normalised to total protein, bars as mean plus or minus SEM, points as individual organoids, grey lines joining matched samples, paired t-tests with FDR adjustment.
figures.key_result: Screening 2,394 knockdown genes from a published RPE1 Perturb-seq dataset put CCDC6 top for both lowering E9 and raising E7 and flagged ATP2A2 as negatively correlated with E9, and both genes were expressed more highly in HGSC cells than in normal FTE or microenvironment cells. XL177A, which destabilises CCDC6 by inhibiting USP7, showed the strongest tendency to synergise with carboplatin and gave recurrent carboplatin sensitisation across five organoid lines, suppressed NF-kB and TNFalpha signalling and inflammatory transcription factors including STAT1 and STAT2, and consistently reduced phospho-p65 at serine 536 and phospho-ERK1/2 relative to N106, with no consistent change in phospho-p38. The SERCA2 activator N106 did the opposite, activating NF-kB signalling and the immediate-early stress factors JUND and ATF4, and was neutral to modestly antagonistic with carboplatin.

key_findings.statement: Inter-patient transcriptional heterogeneity in HGSC is generated during tumorigenesis rather than inherited from a heterogeneous normal tissue: normal secretory fallopian tube cells from different donors mix together, whereas cancer cells segregate by patient.
key_findings.evidence: Fig. 1B and Fig. S1D. Louvain clustering placed on average 96 percent of each fallopian tube sample's secretory cells in one shared cluster, while on average 84 percent of cells within a cancer cluster came from a single patient. Immune and stromal cells also clustered together across patients.

key_findings.statement: Two shared epithelial modules, E7 (oxidative phosphorylation, fatty acid metabolism, DNA repair) and E9 (MAPK, NF-kB, TNFalpha signalling), are mutually antagonistic in cancer cells and have opposite associations with overall survival.
key_findings.evidence: Fig. 1C to 1E, Fig. S3A and S3B. E3, E5 and E7 correlated with the OXPHOS hallmark (cancer r = 0.50 to 0.65, normal r = 0.54 to 0.57); E9 correlated with TNFalpha signalling via NF-kB (r = 0.48 cancer, 0.70 normal), TGF-beta (r = 0.42 cancer) and EMT (r = 0.70 normal). In cancer cells TNFalpha/NF-kB and OXPHOS were inversely related (r = minus 0.73, p = 0.00063), not significant in normal cells (r = minus 0.28, p = 0.24). In TCGA (n = 258) E7-high gave longer and E9-high shorter overall survival (log-rank p = 0.0025 and 0.0015).

key_findings.statement: The E9 state is developmentally late and the E7 state developmentally early along an inferred RNA velocity trajectory, in cancer and in normal fallopian tube alike, so the chemoresistance-associated state is not an early stem-like state.
key_findings.evidence: Fig. 3A to 3D and Fig. S6, S7. Mean per-sample latent-time correlations in cancer were E2 0.33 and E9 0.32 versus E3 minus 0.27 and E7 minus 0.26, with the same ordering and larger magnitudes in normal FTE (E9 0.45, E7 minus 0.52). Trajectory direction was checked by secretory cells having lower latent time than ciliated cells in 5 of 6 samples, and E7-high secretory cells preceding E9-high secretory cells in the germline TP53 control sample.

key_findings.statement: The cancer version of the late E9 state has lost the MHC class II regulatory activity that its normal fallopian tube counterpart retains.
key_findings.evidence: Fig. 3E. Inferred activity of the MHC class II regulators RFXAP, RFXANK and RFX5 was higher in the normal FTE E9 state than in the cancer E9 state, alongside higher SRF, ELK4 and ELK1 in normal. The authors also note that the germline TP53-mutant fallopian tube sample kept normal-like antigen presentation in its late state.

key_findings.statement: The good-prognosis E7 state, not the NF-kB state, is the one associated with homologous recombination deficiency and with a BRCA1-mutant-like transcriptional signature, and both modules predict survival independently of homologous recombination status and age.
key_findings.evidence: Fig. 4A and Fig. S8B. E7 was higher in homologous recombination deficient than proficient TCGA tumours (Wilcoxon p = 0.0012) while E9 did not differ (p = 0.78); in a Cox model with homologous recombination status and age, E7 p = 0.024 and E9 p = 0.014. BRCA1-mutant-enriched genes from the isogenic COV362 pair were up in E7-high cells (adjusted p = 0.0016, NES = 1.42) and BRCA1-wild-type-restored genes were down (adjusted p = 2e-10, NES = minus 3.38).

key_findings.statement: Module activity is partly structured by copy number subclones, so these states are neither purely plastic nor attributable to one genetic driver.
key_findings.evidence: Fig. 4B and 4C. Across all patients, inferCNV subclone groups were associated with module activity (p = 1.75e-264), and 22 of 30 individual patients showed a significant association after FDR adjustment, with no signal under random module assignment; 10,615 module-active cells were analysed. Individual driver amplification associations (CCND3 with E9 p = 0.02, AKT2 with E7 p = 0.045) did not survive multiple-testing correction.

key_findings.statement: Inhibiting USP7 with XL177A, which destabilises CCDC6, pushes organoids out of the NF-kB-active state and resensitises them to carboplatin, while activating SERCA2 with N106 does the reverse.
key_findings.evidence: Fig. 5C to 5F. XL177A gave the strongest synergy tendency with carboplatin in the initial two-organoid screen and recurrent sensitisation across five organoid lines (Bliss above 10 counted as synergy), suppressed NF-kB and TNFalpha signalling and inflammatory transcription factors including STAT1 and STAT2 in bulk RNA-seq of two organoids, and consistently lowered phospho-p65 Ser536 and phospho-ERK1/2 across all five organoids by paired t-test with FDR adjustment, with no consistent phospho-p38 change. N106 activated NF-kB signalling and JUND and ATF4 and was neutral to modestly antagonistic with carboplatin.

key_findings.statement: Both candidate targets are preferentially expressed in cancer cells rather than normal epithelium or microenvironment, which is why they were chosen over other computational hits.
key_findings.evidence: Fig. 5B. CCDC6 and ATP2A2 showed higher expression in HGSC cells than in either normal FTE or tumour microenvironment cells within the E9 state (Kruskal-Wallis), whereas LSM12 and USP9X, which fitted the same perturbation pattern, did not separate these populations and were deprioritised.

limitations: The claim that the E9 state is developmentally late rests entirely on RNA velocity latent time, which is inferred from spliced and unspliced read ratios in a static snapshot and not measured by following cells over time; the authors list this explicitly as a limitation.

The fallopian tube to HGSC relationship is inferred from single-cell data and was never modelled experimentally, and the authors describe the proposed regulatory divergence between normal and cancer versions of the E9 state as hypothesis-generating.

The normal side of the comparison is thin: only 1,251 in-house secretory fallopian tube cells passed filtering, two of the seven control samples were dropped from the pseudobulk analysis for having fewer than 50 cells of a type, and the normal latent-time correlations come from a small number of samples.

All normal controls are postmenopausal women, and the external secretory fallopian tube dataset is also from postmenopausal donors, so hormonal state is uniform and low and no premenopausal normal reference is present.

Harmonising single-cell data across highly heterogeneous tumours is difficult and cancer cell numbers varied widely between samples, so sample-specific effects may still mask broadly conserved programs even after pseudobulk gene selection.

The target prioritisation used a genome-scale Perturb-seq dataset generated in RPE1 cells, a non-cancerous retinal pigment epithelial line with no fallopian tube identity, no HGSC copy number burden and no malignancy, and the correlations were only correlational.

The functional arm uses five patient-derived organoid lines, which the authors say does not allow broad generalisation across HGSC, with magnitude and concentration dependence of the carboplatin effect varying between lines.
The patient-derived organoids contain cancer cells only, so no stromal or immune contribution to the NF-kB state could be tested in the functional experiments.
Bulk RNA-seq of treated organoids was taken at a single time point before carboplatin exposure, which limits any conclusion about when the sensitisation starts or how long it lasts.
The MHC class II result is an inferred transcription factor activity difference (RFX5, RFXAP, RFXANK) rather than a measurement of MHC class II protein, antigen presentation or T cell recognition.

Several analysis parameters are not reported, including the WGCNA soft-threshold power and minimum module size, the Harmony settings, and the max.stat survival cut points, and two reported cell counts differ (30,236 malignant epithelial cells in Methods versus 15,948 cancer cells used for the Fig. 1D correlations, the latter apparently a subsample).

Associations of the modules with individual driver amplifications were nominally significant but did not survive multiple-testing correction, so that genetic link remains inconclusive by the authors' own statement.
open_questions: Where does the NF-kB-activating signal in the E9 state come from in vivo? The paper never separates a cell-intrinsic stress route from ligand input such as TNF from surrounding stromal or myeloid cells, and TNF ligand expression was not measured.

Is the late E9 state the endpoint of normal secretory differentiation, or an aberrant branch off it? Ciliated cells were excluded from the main module analysis and used only to orient the trajectory, so the relationship between E9 and the secretory-to-ciliated differentiation axis is unresolved.

Does the loss of MHC class II regulatory activity in the cancer E9 state actually reduce antigen presentation and CD4 T cell recognition, and is it accompanied by any change in MHC class I? Neither MHC class II protein nor any class I component was measured.

Why is the BRCA1-mutant-like, homologous recombination deficient signature associated with the NF-kB-low E7 state rather than with the inflammatory E9 state, given that BRCA1 loss is widely linked to cytosolic DNA sensing and NF-kB activation elsewhere?

Is the carboplatin sensitisation by XL177A actually caused by the shift out of the E9 state, or by a parallel effect of USP7 inhibition on DNA repair? CCDC6 is a DNA repair regulator and USP7 has many substrates, and the paper does not isolate the state-shift from the repair effect.

Does the subclonal bias in module activity mean some cells are genetically locked into a state? The authors show a bias in 22 of 30 patients but no driver, and they do not test whether a cell can be moved between states and back.
Would the same two modules emerge, and would XL177A still sensitise, in premenopausal fallopian tube and in models where hormonal and stromal context is present rather than in cancer-only organoids?
reading.relevance_to_lab: This paper sits squarely in the lab's fallopian tube and HGSOC origin strand and it puts NF-kB at the centre of the clinically important epithelial state, which is exactly the pathway the lab's own model (Chen, Han et al. 2026 preprint) proposes as the epithelial readout of an inflammatory, estrogen-driven stroma. Three concrete connections are worth working through. First, a direction clash that is genuinely informative rather than a disagreement to wave away: the lab's model has NF-kB and JAK/STAT activation favouring a progenitor-like, less differentiated epithelial state, whereas here the MAPK and NF-kB module E9 sits at the LATE end of the inferred fallopian tube trajectory and the OXPHOS and MYC-high E7 module sits early, and the authors explicitly frame this as a challenge to the cancer stem cell paradigm. Before concluding the two models conflict, note what late means here: it is RNA velocity latent time in secretory cells with ciliated cells excluded from module building, oriented by the observation that secretory cells have lower latent time than ciliated cells, and in normal fallopian tube the E9 module also correlates with the EMT hallmark at r = 0.70. So the honest question is whether the paper's late axis is the same axis the lab calls differentiation at all, and the lab's own secretory-to-ciliated differentiation markers could be scored against E7 and E9 directly to find out. Second, the lab's JAK/STAT arm has a candidate here that the paper does not pursue: module E1 was the one that correlated most strongly with PROGENy JAK-STAT in both cancer and normal cells, and the E1 gene list in Table S3 is a ready-made test set for whether the lab's stromal-ERalpha-driven epithelial signature maps onto a real, reproducible human epithelial module. Third, and most usable, the dataset itself. This is 52 treatment-naive HGSC samples and 7 normal postmenopausal fallopian tube samples from the DECIDER cohort (NCT04846933) with 18,974 stromal and 80,764 immune cells that were annotated and then used only as a reference population, for gene selection and as the inferCNV normal baseline. Nothing stromal or myeloid was analysed as biology. That is precisely the lab's compartment, so reanalysing these stromal and myeloid cells for ESR1 and ERalpha target activity, POSTN, FGF1, FGF2, TNF, IL1 and CCL2, and then asking whether stromal inflammatory tone tracks with epithelial E9 activity in the same tumour, is a well-defined and low-cost project on public data. Be clear about what the paper does not contain, because the overlap is narrower than the NF-kB headline suggests. Estrogen, oestrogen, ESR1 and ERalpha do not appear anywhere in the text; postmenopausal appears only as a sample descriptor, and in fact every normal control is postmenopausal, so the hormonal axis is held flat rather than tested. POSTN, FGF1, FGF2, IL1, IL1B and CCL2 do not appear; TNF appears only as the TNFalpha-via-NF-kB hallmark footprint and as the pathway XL177A suppresses, never as a measured ligand from a specific cell type. Fibroblasts and CAFs are not discussed. Crucially, the paper never establishes where the NF-kB signal originates: the organoids contain cancer cells only, so what they show is that NF-kB tone can be moved cell-intrinsically through ER calcium handling and CCDC6, which is informative but does not exclude stromal input in vivo and certainly does not test it. For the BRCA1-deficient ER-negative breast strand the connection is thinner but one result deserves precise statement. The antigen presentation finding is MHC class II only: inferred activity of the RFX5, RFXAP and RFXANK complex is higher in the normal fallopian tube version of the late E9 state and lower in the cancer version, which the authors read as loss of a highly antigen-presenting epithelial state. MHC class I, HLA-A, HLA-B, HLA-C, HLA-E, B2M, NKG2A, cGAS, STING, IRF3, type I interferon, NK cells and CD8 T cells appear nowhere in the paper, so this cannot be read as support for the lab's HLA-C and HLA-E and NKG2A chain. The conceptual parallel is still real: the authors argue that TP53 loss starts carcinogenesis but that immune evasion is a required further step, and they point to the germline TP53-mutant fallopian tube sample retaining normal-like antigen presentation in its late state, which mirrors the lab's own two-step framing in BRCA1-deficient tissue. One further result cuts against an easy assumption in the lab's breast chain and should be stated plainly: homologous recombination deficiency and a BRCA1-mutant-like COV362 signature associate with E7, the NF-kB-LOW good-prognosis module, not with the inflammatory E9 module. If BRCA1 loss drove NF-kB through cytosolic DNA sensing in this tissue, the naive expectation would have been the opposite, so this is a real tension worth a lab meeting. Finally, two things are directly borrowable: the module-building recipe of pseudobulk gene selection, then CS-CORE for noise-corrected single-cell co-expression, then WGCNA, which would work on the lab's own mouse and human fallopian tube data and avoids forcing plastic states into clusters, and the Perturb-seq lookup trick of asking a published genome-scale screen which knockdown moves a signature in the wanted direction, which the lab could run against its own stromal-ERalpha-induced epithelial signature.
discussion_questions: The paper's late MAPK and NF-kB state is the chemoresistant one, while our model has NF-kB activation favouring a progenitor-like, less differentiated epithelial state. Are these the same state described from opposite ends, or is the paper's RNA velocity latent time not measuring differentiation in the sense we mean? Scoring our secretory and ciliated differentiation markers against E7 and E9 would settle it, and so would asking where our stromal-ERalpha-dependent epithelial signature falls on their trajectory.

Nothing in this paper says where the NF-kB signal comes from: the organoids are cancer cells only, TNF is measured as a downstream hallmark footprint and never as a ligand from a named cell type, and no stromal or myeloid biology is analysed. Their DECIDER data contain 18,974 stromal and 80,764 immune cells that were used only as a reference. Is reanalysing those cells for ESR1 and ERalpha target activity, POSTN, FGF1, FGF2, TNF, IL1 and CCL2, and correlating stromal inflammatory tone with epithelial E9 activity per tumour, the fastest test of our model on human data?

Module E1, not E9, was the one that tracked JAK-STAT most strongly in both cancer and normal cells, and the authors never follow it up. Should we take the E1 gene list from their Table S3 as an independent human test set for the JAK/STAT arm of our model, and check whether E1 and E9 co-occur in the same cells the way our stromal inflammatory state predicts?

Homologous recombination deficiency and a BRCA1-mutant-like signature go with E7, the NF-kB-low module, not with the inflammatory E9 module. How do we reconcile that with our BRCA1, cytosolic DNA, cGAS-STING, NF-kB chain in breast? Is the difference tissue, the fact that this is a transcriptional signature rather than acute BRCA1 loss, or evidence that chronic NF-kB tone and acute DNA-sensing-driven NF-kB are different states?

Their antigen presentation result is MHC class II only, as inferred RFX5, RFXAP and RFXANK activity lost in the cancer version of the late state, with no MHC class I, HLA-C, HLA-E or NK data anywhere. Is it worth scoring MHC class I, B2M and the interferon modules in their public epithelial cells ourselves, to see whether class I loss travels with class II loss in the same fallopian tube state?

Every normal control here is postmenopausal, so the hormonal axis is held flat rather than tested, and the authors call the normal-to-cancer divergence hypothesis-generating and ask for engineered fallopian tube secretory cell and organoid models. Does our estrogen and stromal co-culture system let us test the one experiment they could not do, namely whether raising stromal inflammatory tone pushes fallopian tube epithelium toward the E9 state?

nodes.label: Are HGSC cell states new, or inherited from fallopian tube?
nodes.detail: The paper asks whether the transcriptional states that make HGSC heterogeneous and treatment resistant arise de novo during tumorigenesis or are conserved programs of the tissue of origin.

nodes.label: Fallopian tube epithelium is the origin of HGSC
nodes.detail: Transcriptomic, evolutionary and mouse model evidence point to fallopian tube epithelium; lesions carry the same TP53 mutations and the p53 signature can progress through serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma to HGSC.

nodes.label: Tumours reuse normal programs, but no matched single-cell comparison existed
nodes.detail: Tumour gene modules often turn out to be reused normal programs such as stress, interferon and differentiation, yet earlier fallopian tube studies had few postmenopausal donors and no matched single-cell HGSC data, so normal states had to be projected onto bulk tumour RNA-seq.

nodes.label: Homeostatic fallopian tube modules persist and become tumour heterogeneity
nodes.detail: If homeostatic epithelial gene programs survive oncogenesis, then the clinically important cancer states should be measurable in normal fallopian tube epithelium using the same shared epithelial genes.

nodes.label: Continuous gene modules from scRNA-seq of 52 tumours and normal fallopian tube
nodes.detail: Single-cell RNA sequencing of 52 treatment-naive HGSC samples from 50 patients plus postmenopausal fallopian tube controls and an external secretory dataset, with modules built by pseudobulk gene selection, CS-CORE co-expression and WGCNA instead of discrete clustering.

nodes.label: Inter-patient heterogeneity is created during tumorigenesis
nodes.detail: Normal secretory cells from different donors mix (96 percent of each sample's secretory cells in one shared cluster) while cancer cells segregate by patient (84 percent of cells in a cancer cluster from one patient), and immune and stromal cells also mix across patients.

nodes.label: E7 is an OXPHOS module, E9 a MAPK and NF-kB module, mutually antagonistic
nodes.detail: Of 9 shared epithelial modules, E7 tracks oxidative phosphorylation, fatty acid metabolism and DNA repair while E9 tracks MAPK, NF-kB and TNFalpha signalling; in cancer cells the two hallmarks are inversely related at r = minus 0.73 (p = 0.00063). E1 was the module tracking JAK-STAT.

nodes.label: The two modules predict opposite survival in TCGA
nodes.detail: In 258 TCGA HGSC patients, E7-high tumours had longer overall survival (log-rank p = 0.0025) and E9-high tumours shorter overall survival (log-rank p = 0.0015).

nodes.label: Modules reproduce across tumours with distinct transcription factor signatures
nodes.detail: E7 and E9 recur across integrated epithelial clusters and in an independent 41-patient HGSC dataset; E9 carries higher inferred NF-kB, RELA, JUN, JUND, ATF4 and DDIT3 activity and E7 higher PPARGC1A, GABPA, MYC, HCFC1 and ZBTB4.

nodes.label: E9 sits late and E7 early along inferred latent time, in cancer and normal tissue
nodes.detail: Per-sample RNA velocity latent time correlates positively with E9 (mean r = 0.32 cancer, 0.45 normal) and negatively with E7 (minus 0.26 cancer, minus 0.52 normal); trajectory direction was checked against secretory versus ciliated cells in 5 of 6 samples.

nodes.label: Cancer loses the MHC class II regulators the normal late state keeps
nodes.detail: Within the E9 state, inferred activity of RFX5, RFXAP and RFXANK is higher in normal fallopian tube than in cancer, and the germline TP53-mutant control retained normal-like antigen presentation in its late state.

nodes.label: E7 tracks homologous recombination deficiency; both modules are genetically biased
nodes.detail: E7 is higher in homologous recombination deficient tumours (p = 0.0012) and enriched for a BRCA1-mutant-like signature, both modules stay prognostic after adjusting for homologous recombination status and age, and module activity is biased across copy number subclones in 22 of 30 patients.

nodes.label: Perturb-seq lookup nominates CCDC6 and ATP2A2 as state-shifting targets
nodes.detail: A published genome-scale Perturb-seq dataset in RPE1 cells covering 2,394 knockdowns was searched for perturbations that lower E9 and raise E7, which put CCDC6 top and flagged ATP2A2 (SERCA2); both are expressed higher in HGSC than in normal fallopian tube or microenvironment cells.

nodes.label: XL177A lowers NF-kB and ERK and resensitises organoids to carboplatin; N106 does the reverse
nodes.detail: Across five patient-derived organoid lines the USP7 inhibitor XL177A, which destabilises CCDC6, suppressed NF-kB and TNFalpha signalling, reduced phospho-p65 Ser536 and phospho-ERK1/2 with no consistent phospho-p38 change, and synergised with carboplatin, while the SERCA2 activator N106 activated NF-kB and was neutral to modestly antagonistic.

nodes.label: A conserved developmentally late NF-kB state is the stable chemoresistant state
nodes.detail: The clinically bad state is not a de novo cancer invention but a conserved, developmentally late fallopian tube program, which runs against the expectation that resistance lives in an early stem-like state.

nodes.label: Cell state is a pharmacological lever on platinum response
nodes.detail: Because the state can be moved in both directions in organoids by acting on endoplasmic reticulum calcium handling or on CCDC6, conserved tissue-of-origin states are candidate prognostic markers and candidate targets for resensitising platinum-resistant HGSC.

entities.name: High-grade serous ovarian carcinoma
entities.description: The cancer studied, profiled here in 52 treatment-naive samples from 50 patients of the DECIDER cohort.

entities.name: Fallopian tube epithelium
entities.description: The proposed tissue of origin of HGSC and the normal reference tissue in this paper, sampled from 7 postmenopausal women plus an external 7-donor dataset.

entities.name: Secretory fallopian tube epithelial cell
entities.description: The non-ciliated fallopian tube epithelial cell type used as the normal counterpart of cancer epithelium; 1,251 were recovered in house and 3,614 came from external data.

entities.name: Ciliated fallopian tube epithelial cell
entities.description: Excluded from module building but used to orient the inferred trajectory, since ciliated cells had higher latent time than secretory cells in 5 of 6 samples.

entities.name: E7 module
entities.description: A shared epithelial gene module marking an early, metabolically active oxidative phosphorylation and DNA repair state associated with longer survival.

entities.name: E9 module
entities.description: A shared epithelial gene module marking a developmentally late MAPK and NF-kB stress state associated with chemoresistance and shorter survival.

entities.name: E1 module
entities.description: The shared epithelial module that correlated most strongly with JAK-STAT pathway activity in both cancer and normal cells; not pursued further by the authors.

entities.name: NF-kB signalling
entities.description: The inflammatory and survival transcription factor pathway that defines the E9 state and that the organoid drug experiments move in both directions.

entities.name: MAPK signalling
entities.description: The other pathway defining the E9 state, read out computationally by PROGENy and at protein level as phospho-ERK1/2.

entities.name: Oxidative phosphorylation
entities.description: The mitochondrial energy-producing program that defines the E7 state.

entities.name: TNF
entities.description: Appears only as the TNFalpha signalling via NF-kB hallmark footprint correlated with E9 and as the pathway XL177A suppresses; the ligand itself was never measured in a specific cell type.

entities.name: JAK-STAT signalling
entities.description: The PROGENy pathway most strongly correlated with module E1 in both cancer and normal cells.

entities.name: Epithelial to mesenchymal transition
entities.description: A hallmark program strongly correlated with E9 in normal fallopian tube cells (r = 0.70), which the authors note is enriched in stromal cells generally.

entities.name: RELA
entities.description: The p65 subunit of NF-kB, inferred as more active in the E9 state and measured at protein level as phospho-p65 Ser536 in treated organoids.

entities.name: ATF4
entities.description: A stress-response transcription factor with higher inferred activity in E9, and activated by the SERCA2 activator N106 in organoids.

entities.name: MYC
entities.description: A transcription factor with higher inferred activity in the early E7 state, part of the authors' argument that the early state is metabolically driven rather than inflammatory.

entities.name: PPARGC1A
entities.description: A mitochondrial biogenesis coactivator with the highest inferred activity gain in the E7 state.

entities.name: RFX5
entities.description: Part of the RFX complex that drives MHC class II transcription; inferred more active in the normal fallopian tube version of the late E9 state than in the cancer version, together with RFXAP and RFXANK.

entities.name: MHC class II antigen presentation
entities.description: Display of peptides to CD4 T cells; its regulatory axis is retained in the normal late fallopian tube state and lower in the cancer version, which the authors interpret as immune evasion.

entities.name: TP53
entities.description: Almost universally mutated in HGSC; one normal control carried a germline mutation and showed lower TP53 expression (p = 0.011) while staying transcriptionally close to normal fallopian tube.

entities.name: BRCA1
entities.description: Used through an isogenic COV362 signature: BRCA1-mutant-enriched genes were upregulated in E7-high cells and BRCA1-restored genes downregulated.

entities.name: Homologous recombination deficiency
entities.description: Genomic repair defect called by ovaHRDscar in TCGA; associated with higher E7 activity but not with E9.

entities.name: CCDC6
entities.description: A DNA repair regulator, member of module E2 which correlates tightly with E9, nominated by Perturb-seq as the top knockdown lowering E9 and raising E7, and expressed higher in HGSC than in normal fallopian tube or microenvironment cells.

entities.name: ATP2A2
entities.description: Encodes the endoplasmic reticulum calcium pump SERCA2; negatively correlated with E9 in Perturb-seq and expressed higher in HGSC than in normal fallopian tube or microenvironment cells.

entities.name: USP7
entities.description: The deubiquitinase that stabilises CCDC6, which is how the drug XL177A reaches CCDC6 indirectly.

entities.name: XL177A
entities.description: A USP7 inhibitor used to destabilise CCDC6; it suppressed NF-kB and ERK signalling and synergised with carboplatin in patient-derived organoids.

entities.name: N106
entities.description: A SERCA2 activator used to restrain endoplasmic reticulum stress; it activated NF-kB signalling and was neutral to modestly antagonistic with carboplatin.

entities.name: Carboplatin
entities.description: The platinum chemotherapy against which synergy and antagonism were scored in the organoid experiments.

entities.name: Platinum chemoresistance
entities.description: The clinical phenotype the paper is trying to explain, attributed here to the stable late E9 state.

entities.name: Overall survival
entities.description: The clinical endpoint used in 258 deconvoluted TCGA HGSC bulk RNA-seq profiles to test the modules.

entities.name: ERK1/2 (MAPK3 and MAPK1)
entities.description: The MAPK kinases whose phosphorylation at Thr202 and Tyr204 was measured by western blot in treated organoids as the protein-level MAPK readout.

entities.name: RNA velocity latent time
entities.description: The inferred pseudotime from velocyto, scVelo and CellRank that orders epithelial cells and places E7 early and E9 late.

entities.name: DECIDER HGSC single-cell cohort
entities.description: The single-cell RNA sequencing resource built here: 131,225 cells including 30,236 malignant epithelial, 1,251 secretory fallopian tube, 80,764 immune and 18,974 stromal cells, trial NCT04846933.

entities.name: Patient-derived organoid panel
entities.description: Five genomically validated HGSC organoid lines from the same cohort, containing cancer cells only with no stromal or immune cells, used for all functional tests.

entities.name: RPE1 genome-scale Perturb-seq dataset
entities.description: A published CRISPR knockdown screen with single-cell readout in non-cancerous retinal pigment epithelial cells covering 2,394 genes, used only to nominate candidate targets.

relations.evidence: Fallopian tube epithelium is cited as the tissue of origin of HGSC on transcriptomic, evolutionary and mouse model grounds, with shared TP53 mutations and progression through serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma.
HGSC almost always carries TP53 mutations, and the authors argue TP53 loss initiates carcinogenesis but is not sufficient without further aberrations including immune evasion.
E9 correlated most strongly with PROGENy NF-kB activity in both cancer and normal cells, and with the TNFalpha via NF-kB hallmark at r = 0.48 in cancer and 0.70 in normal cells.
E9 correlated most strongly with PROGENy MAPK activity, which was strongly enriched in the E9-high integrated cluster 7.
The TNFalpha signalling via NF-kB hallmark is the strongest hallmark correlate of E9; the TNF ligand itself was not measured in any cell type.
E3, E5 and E7 correlated with the oxidative phosphorylation hallmark at r = 0.50 to 0.65 in cancer and 0.54 to 0.57 in normal cells, alongside fatty acid metabolism, adipogenesis and DNA repair.

In cancer cells the TNFalpha via NF-kB and oxidative phosphorylation hallmarks were inversely related (r = minus 0.73, p = 0.00063), E3 versus E9 was the strongest negative module pair, and single-cell E7 to E9 correlation in the independent dataset was r = minus 0.15 (p below 2.2e-16); the relation is mutual exclusivity, not a demonstrated mechanism.
Module E1 showed the strongest correlation with PROGENy JAK-STAT activity in both cancer and normal cells.
E9 correlated with the epithelial to mesenchymal transition hallmark at r = 0.70 in normal fallopian tube cells and with TGF-beta signalling at r = 0.42 in cancer.
Inferred transcription factor activity for NF-kB and RELA, along with JUN, JUND, ATF4 and DDIT3, was higher in the E9 state than the E7 state.
ATF4 was among the transcription factors with higher inferred activity in E9, and N106 treatment activated ATF4 along with JUND in organoid RNA-seq.
MYC was among the transcription factors with higher inferred activity in the E7 state, alongside PPARGC1A, GABPA, HCFC1 and ZBTB4.
PPARGC1A showed higher inferred activity in E7 than E9, consistent with E7 being an oxidative phosphorylation state.
E9 activity correlated positively with inferred latent time, mean r = 0.32 across cancer samples and 0.45 across normal fallopian tube samples, placing it late in the trajectory.
E7 activity correlated negatively with inferred latent time, mean r = minus 0.26 across cancer samples and minus 0.52 across normal fallopian tube samples, placing it early.
Ciliated cells had higher latent time than secretory cells in 5 of 6 control samples, which is how the direction of the inferred trajectory was fixed.
RFX5 with RFXAP and RFXANK forms the complex required for MHC class II gene transcription; this is cited background used to interpret the inferred activity difference.
Inferred RFX5, RFXAP and RFXANK activity within the late E9 state was higher in normal fallopian tube epithelium than in cancer.

The MHC class II regulatory axis was lower in the cancer E9 state than in the normal one, which the authors read as loss of a highly antigen-presenting epithelial state during tumorigenesis; MHC class II protein and antigen presentation itself were not measured.
E7 activity was higher in homologous recombination deficient (n = 138) than proficient (n = 111) TCGA tumours by Wilcoxon test, p = 0.0012, while E9 did not differ (p = 0.78).

BRCA1-mutant-enriched genes from the isogenic COV362 pair were upregulated in E7-high cells (adjusted p = 0.0016, NES = 1.42) and BRCA1-wild-type-restored genes downregulated (adjusted p = 2e-10, NES = minus 3.38).

E7-high tumours had longer overall survival in 258 deconvoluted TCGA profiles (log-rank p = 0.0025), and E7 remained significant in a Cox model with homologous recombination status and age (p = 0.024).

E9-high tumours had shorter overall survival in 258 deconvoluted TCGA profiles (log-rank p = 0.0015), and E9 remained significant in a Cox model with homologous recombination status and age (p = 0.014).

E9 marks the stable state the authors call chemoresistant, supported by its poor survival association and by organoid experiments in which raising NF-kB tone removed carboplatin sensitisation and lowering it produced synergy.
Within the E9 state, CCDC6 expression averaged per sample was higher in HGSC cells than in secretory epithelial or tumour microenvironment cells by Kruskal-Wallis test.
Within the E9 state, ATP2A2 expression averaged per sample was higher in HGSC cells than in secretory epithelial or tumour microenvironment cells by Kruskal-Wallis test.

In the RPE1 Perturb-seq screen of 2,394 knockdowns, CCDC6 knockdown was the top perturbation that both lowered the E9 signature and raised E7, which the authors treat as a prediction only, since RPE1 is a non-cancerous line.
USP7 stabilises CCDC6 by deubiquitination, which is the cited basis for using a USP7 inhibitor to lower CCDC6.
XL177A is a USP7 inhibitor, used here as an indirect way to destabilise CCDC6.
