XL177A suppressed NF-kB and TNFalpha signalling in organoid bulk RNA-seq, lowered inferred NFKB and RELA activity along with STAT1 and STAT2, and consistently reduced phospho-p65 Ser536 across five organoid lines.

XL177A consistently reduced phospho-ERK1/2 at Thr202 and Tyr204 relative to N106 across five organoid lines, with no consistent change in phospho-p38, which the authors read as an ERK rather than p38 effect.

XL177A showed the strongest tendency to synergise with carboplatin in the two-line screen (Bliss above 10 counted as synergy) and gave recurrent carboplatin sensitisation across five organoid lines, though magnitude and concentration dependence varied.
N106 is a SERCA2 activator, used to restrain endoplasmic reticulum stress by increasing calcium pumping.

N106 activated NF-kB and TNFalpha signalling in organoid bulk RNA-seq and raised the immediate-early stress factors JUND and ATF4; the authors propose a feedback loop since NF-kB inhibition had previously been reported to reduce SERCA activity.

Carboplatin response and Bliss synergy were scored in five cancer-cell-only patient-derived organoid lines from the same cohort, so no stromal or immune contribution was present in the functional tests.

The modules were derived from the DECIDER single-cell resource of 131,225 cells, in which 18,974 stromal and 80,764 immune cells were annotated but used only as reference populations for gene selection and copy number inference.

CCDC6 and ATP2A2 were nominated from Spearman correlations between module signature log fold changes and perturbation z-scores in the RPE1 genome-scale Perturb-seq dataset, covering 7,190 genes for E7 and 7,229 for E9.
XL177A combined with carboplatin gave Bliss synergy scores above 10 in the initial two-line screen and recurrent sensitisation across five organoid lines.
N106 combined with carboplatin was mostly antagonistic in the initial screen and neutral to modestly antagonistic across the five organoid lines.

Secretory cells are the fallopian tube epithelial population used as the normal counterpart of cancer epithelium; 96 percent of each control sample's secretory cells fell into a single shared cluster.
Ciliated cells are the other main fallopian tube epithelial population, identified by FOXJ1 and PIFO and excluded from module building.

papers.title: Multi-omics analysis of high-grade serous ovarian cancers reveals heterogeneity and distinct immunological patterns based upon clinico-genomic status
papers.authors: Jing Qian, Rania Bassiouni, Yuxin Jin, Seeta Rajpara, Monica Neuman, Varun U. Khetan, Bodour Salhia, David W. Craig, Joseph W. Carlson, Lynda D. Roman, John D. Carpten

bibliographic.title: Multi-omics analysis of high-grade serous ovarian cancers reveals heterogeneity and distinct immunological patterns based upon clinico-genomic status

reading.one_line_takeaway: In high-grade serous ovarian cancer, BRCA status does not change the overall spatial architecture of the tumour, but it changes what the immune niches inside that architecture are doing: BRCA-mutant tumours have a more interferon-driven, antigen-presenting immune region, while a fibroblast-to-macrophage CXCL12/CXCR4 niche is present in both genotypes.
reading.tldr: The authors asked how BRCA1/BRCA2 status shapes the immune microenvironment of high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC), not just its DNA repair phenotype. They combined whole exome sequencing and bulk RNA sequencing on 25 tumours (17 BRCA-mutant, 8 BRCA-wild-type) with Visium spatial transcriptomics on 39 tissue sections from 22 of those patients. Integrated clustering of about 40,000 spatial spots produced seven recurrent spatial regions that were present in both genotypes: tumour, two fibroblast/extracellular matrix regions, a macrophage-rich lipid-associated macrophage region (IC4) and an immune-activated region (IC7). IC7 carried interferon alpha and gamma, complement and inflammatory programmes and was functionally stronger in BRCA-mutant tumours (higher IC7 abundance, interferon gamma score and antigen presentation score, Wilcoxon p = 0.014, 0.036 and 0.011), whereas the IC4 macrophage niche looked the same in both genotypes and received predicted CXCL12 to CXCR4 and MIF signals from the fibroblast region IC3. The conclusion is that genotype tunes immune function within a conserved spatial scaffold rather than rearranging the tissue.
reading.research_question: How does BRCA1/BRCA2 mutation status in high-grade serous ovarian cancer shape the spatial organisation, cellular composition and predicted cell to cell signalling of the tumour immune and stromal microenvironment, beyond its known effect on DNA repair and drug response?
reading.background: HGSOC is the commonest epithelial ovarian cancer and survival remains poor because recurrent disease becomes treatment resistant. Germline BRCA1/BRCA2 mutations occur in roughly 20 to 22 percent of cases and cause homologous recombination (HR) repair deficiency, which is exploited therapeutically by PARP inhibitors such as olaparib through synthetic lethality. TCGA work established that TP53 mutation is nearly universal in HGSOC and that BRCA-mutant tumours carry more somatic mutations and a distinct pattern of genomic instability. Genomic instability is expected to raise tumour immunogenicity, which could in principle change immune infiltration and response to immunotherapy. What was missing was a spatially resolved comparison: bulk sequencing averages over tumour, stromal and immune compartments, so it cannot say whether BRCA-associated immune differences reflect more immune cells overall, a different tissue architecture, or the same niches behaving differently. This paper fills that gap by mapping tumour, immune and stromal regions in situ and comparing them by BRCA genotype.
reading.study_design: Observational, retrospective human tumour study with no animal or in vitro experiments. Cohort: 25 patients with pathologist-confirmed late-stage HGSOC from the USC Keck Gynecological Tissue and Fluid Repositories, each with matched buffy coat or normal tissue, all as OCT-embedded fresh-frozen blocks, roughly evenly split between treatment-naive tumours and tumours that had received neoadjuvant treatment before debulking surgery. BRCA groups: BRCA-mutant (BRCA-MT, n = 17; 10 germline BRCA1, 4 BRCA1 promoter hypermethylation, 1 somatic BRCA1, 2 germline BRCA2) versus BRCA-wild-type (BRCA-WT, n = 8, no BRCA1/2 alteration). Data types per tumour: whole exome sequencing of tumour and matched normal DNA, Illumina MethylationEPIC arrays to call BRCA1/2 promoter methylation, and total RNA sequencing. Spatial arm: 48 Visium sections from 24 patients, of which 39 sections from 22 patients (16 BRCA-MT, 6 BRCA-WT) passed quality control, at roughly 2 to 4 x 10^8 read pairs per sample and a median of about 2,000 to 6,000 genes detected per spot. Key comparisons: BRCA-MT versus BRCA-WT at the genomic level (mutational signatures, copy number, HR deficiency score), at the bulk transcriptome level (differential expression adjusted for treatment, Hallmark pathway enrichment, immune deconvolution, predicted neoantigen load), and at the spatial level (abundance and functional programmes of each integrated spatial cluster, aggregated per patient, with a sensitivity model that includes treatment status as a covariate).

key_methods.name: Whole exome sequencing of tumour with matched normal DNA
key_methods.plain_explanation: Whole exome sequencing reads the roughly 1 to 2 percent of the genome that codes for protein, which is where most interpretable cancer mutations fall. Sequencing the tumour and the same patient's normal tissue side by side lets you subtract inherited variants and keep only the changes the tumour acquired. The same data also give you copy number, that is how many copies of each chromosome segment the tumour carries.
key_methods.how_used: DNA from fresh-frozen OCT tumour blocks and matched buffy coat or normal tissue was sheared on a Covaris E220 to 150 to 200 bp, prepared with the Agilent SureSelect XT Low Input kit, captured with custom SureSelect V6 plus UTR plus OneSeq probes for tumours and SureSelect Human All Exon V6 for germline, and sequenced on a NovaSeq 6000. Reads were aligned with BWA-MEM v0.7.17 to GRCh38, somatic variants called with GATK v4.1.0.0 Mutect2 and annotated with Ensembl VEP, and summarised with maftools. Germline variants were called with FreeBayes v1.3.6 and Strelka2 v2.9.2, annotated with SnpEff/SnpSift v5.1d, filtered to drop variants above 3 percent population allele frequency, and kept only if pathogenic or likely pathogenic and called by both callers.
key_methods.why_it_matters: This is what defined the two comparison groups and confirmed that the cohort behaves like canonical HGSOC, with TP53 mutated in 82 percent of BRCA-MT and 88 percent of BRCA-WT tumours. The caveat is that exome data miss non-coding drivers and structural rearrangements, so BRCA-WT tumours scored as HR deficient could carry a mechanism this assay does not see.

key_methods.name: Mutational signature analysis (SigProfiler against COSMIC SBS signatures)
key_methods.plain_explanation: Every mutational process leaves a characteristic fingerprint in the types of single base change it makes and the bases on either side. Counting mutations in the 96 possible trinucleotide contexts and fitting that profile to a reference catalogue (COSMIC) tells you which processes were active in a tumour's history. Signature SBS3 is the fingerprint of failed homologous recombination repair, so it is a read-out of BRCA-like repair failure that is independent of knowing the genotype.
key_methods.how_used: SigProfiler was run on the 96-channel substitution counts from the somatic exome calls and the resulting profiles were matched to COSMIC v3 reference signatures by cosine similarity, reporting the top three matches per group (Fig 1D). Tumour mutational burden was computed as nonsynonymous somatic mutations per coding megabase.
key_methods.why_it_matters: It provided functional confirmation that the BRCA-MT group really is repair deficient: SBS3 dominated in BRCA-MT tumours and was absent as a top match in BRCA-WT tumours, which instead showed SBS1 and SBS6. This matters because the BRCA-MT group was deliberately heterogeneous, mixing germline mutation, somatic mutation and promoter hypermethylation.

key_methods.name: scarHRD homologous recombination deficiency scoring
key_methods.plain_explanation: When homologous recombination repair fails, the genome accumulates characteristic scars. scarHRD counts three of them from sequencing data: loss of heterozygosity, telomeric allelic imbalance (lopsided chromosome copy numbers near the chromosome ends), and large-scale state transitions (abrupt copy number changes across long stretches). Their sum is a single HR deficiency score, with a conventional cut-off used clinically to decide whether a tumour is HR deficient.
key_methods.how_used: Copy number was first called from paired tumour and normal exomes with Sequenza v3.0.0 using 50 bp windows, then scarHRD computed loss of heterozygosity plus telomeric allelic imbalance plus large-scale state transitions per tumour, with scores of 42 or above called HR deficient (Fig 2D, per-sample values in S3 Table).
key_methods.why_it_matters: It quantified the degree of genomic instability that the paper later treats as the upstream cause of the immune differences. BRCA-MT tumours had a median score of 59.0 (IQR 40.0 to 67.0) versus 33.5 (IQR 11.25 to 35.5) in BRCA-WT, a Hodges-Lehmann shift of 28.0 (95 percent CI 7.0 to 48.0, Wilcoxon p = 0.0015). The caveat the authors raise themselves is that some BRCA-WT tumours still scored above the HR deficiency threshold, so the genotype label and the functional phenotype are not interchangeable.

key_methods.name: Visium spatial transcriptomics with integrated clustering
key_methods.plain_explanation: Visium measures gene expression while keeping the position in the tissue. A tissue section is laid on a slide printed with a grid of spots, each spot about 55 microns across and carrying position-specific barcodes, so after sequencing you know which transcripts came from which location. Each spot is not a single cell: at that size it covers roughly a handful to a few tens of cells, so a spot's profile is a local mixture. Grouping spots by their expression profiles across all patients at once, after correcting for patient-to-patient batch effects, yields recurrent tissue regions rather than per-patient idiosyncrasies.
key_methods.how_used: Thirty-nine quality-passing sections from 22 patients were clustered after integration, giving 17 integrated clusters (IC1 to IC17) across about 40,002 spots; IC1 to IC7 accounted for roughly 97 percent of spots and were present in both genotypes, so analysis focused on those. Clustering resolution was selected with clustree. Cluster markers were defined with Seurat FindAllMarkers (Wilcoxon rank-sum), fibroblast identity was scored with Seurat AddModuleScore, and tumour purity, immune score and stromal score were assigned per spot with ESTIMATE, a method that infers how much of a transcriptome comes from tumour versus immune versus stromal cells from signature gene expression. One tumour (HR5, germline BRCA2) was also analysed alone as a worked example (Fig 4).
key_methods.why_it_matters: This is the core advance over bulk sequencing: it let the authors ask whether BRCA genotype changes the tissue's building blocks or only their behaviour, and the answer was the latter. The limitation is intrinsic to the platform: because spots are mixtures, each integrated cluster is a region enriched for a cell type, not a purified population.

key_methods.name: RCTD reference-based deconvolution
key_methods.plain_explanation: Because a Visium spot contains several cells, you cannot read cell type directly. Deconvolution estimates what proportion of each spot's transcripts came from each cell type, by fitting the spot's profile as a weighted mixture of reference profiles taken from a single-cell dataset of the same tissue. RCTD does this with a statistical model of counts and is designed for spot data where several cell types genuinely overlap.
key_methods.how_used: RCTD was run against the Zhang et al. HGSOC single-cell reference (GEO accession GSE165897) and the inferred cell type fractions were compared between spots inside and outside a cluster within the same patients, using paired Wilcoxon tests with Benjamini-Hochberg correction. This gave a median macrophage fraction of 13.86 percent in IC4 versus 5.34 percent elsewhere (p = 4.30 x 10^-5, q = 3.01 x 10^-4) and a median combined T/NK plus dendritic cell fraction of 7.18 percent in IC7 versus 4.85 percent elsewhere (p = 2.15 x 10^-4, q = 8.81 x 10^-4).
key_methods.why_it_matters: It converted marker gene enrichment into a claim about cell composition, which is what makes IC4 a macrophage niche and IC7 a lymphoid and dendritic cell niche rather than just a set of co-expressed genes. The caveat is that the estimates inherit whatever biases the single-cell reference carries, and the paper treats them as hypothesis generating rather than as a cell count.

key_methods.name: CellChat ligand-receptor communication inference
key_methods.plain_explanation: CellChat predicts which groups of cells might be talking to which, by checking whether a signalling molecule is expressed in one group and its matching receptor in another, then aggregating those pairs into named pathways and scoring the probability of communication. It is purely computational: it infers possible conversations from gene expression and does not measure protein, secretion, binding or any functional consequence.
key_methods.how_used: CellChat was applied to pooled spatial features grouped by integrated cluster, both across the whole cohort (Fig 6C to 6E) and separately on genotype-pooled data (Fig 7D). It identified the fibroblast-rich IC3 and IC5 as dominant signalling sources toward the macrophage region IC4, with MIF, APP and complement pathways enriched in that direction, IC3 as the single largest contributor of recruitment-like signalling into IC4, and CXCL12 in IC3/IC5 paired with CXCR4 in IC4 (Fig 6F, 6G). At genotype level it suggested lower predicted MIF, complement and ICAM activity in BRCA-WT than in BRCA-MT.
key_methods.why_it_matters: It generated the paper's mechanistic hypothesis, that fibroblasts recruit and condition the lipid-associated macrophage niche through a CXCL12/CXCR4 axis. The authors are explicit that this is exploratory and needs mechanistic validation, and pooling spots by genotype rather than by patient means the genotype-level CellChat comparison in Fig 7D is not a patient-level statistical test.

key_methods.name: Bulk differential expression and gene set enrichment, plus immune deconvolution and neoantigen prediction
key_methods.plain_explanation: Bulk RNA sequencing gives one averaged transcriptome per tumour. DESeq2 models the read counts per gene and tests whether a gene differs between groups, with multiple-testing correction. Pre-ranked gene set enrichment analysis then asks whether whole predefined gene programmes, such as the Hallmark sets, sit systematically high or low in that ranking, which is more robust than looking at single genes. CIBERSORTx and xCell estimate how much of each immune cell type the mixed sample contains from signature genes. Neoantigen prediction asks how many of the tumour's mutated proteins would be presented on that patient's own HLA molecules and therefore look foreign to T cells.
key_methods.how_used: DESeq2 v1.44.0 compared BRCA-MT with BRCA-WT with treatment status as a covariate, Wald tests and Benjamini-Hochberg correction at FDR below 0.05 (Fig 3A). Pre-ranked GSEA on the log2 fold changes against MSigDB Hallmark sets gave the programme-level contrast (Fig 3B); for spatial data the authors used single-sample GSEA per spot with rank normalisation, weighting exponent 0.75 and a minimum gene set overlap of 10 genes. CIBERSORTx estimated 22 immune subsets per tumour (Fig 3C) and xCell was used descriptively on cluster-level spatial expression (Fig 5H). Neoantigens were predicted after inferring each patient's HLA class I and II genotype from the exome data with HLA-LA, and counts were compared with a Wilcoxon rank-sum test (p = 0.902, Fig 3D).
key_methods.why_it_matters: The bulk arm set up the paradox the spatial arm resolves. Bulk programmes differed clearly by genotype (proliferative in BRCA-MT, mesenchymal in BRCA-WT) yet bulk immune composition showed no genotype-defined polarisation and predicted neoantigen load did not differ, so any immune difference had to be local rather than a difference in total immune content.

key_concepts.plain_definition: HGSOC is the most common and most aggressive type of epithelial ovarian cancer. It is thought in most cases to arise from the epithelium of the fallopian tube rather than the ovary itself, and it is defined genetically by near-universal mutation of TP53 together with heavy chromosomal copy number change, rather than by a single recurrent driver mutation. It usually presents at an advanced stage, responds initially to platinum chemotherapy, and then recurs in a treatment-resistant form, which is why survival has barely moved. In this paper HGSOC is the single disease context: all 25 tumours were pathologist-confirmed HGSOC at late stage, and the near-universal TP53 mutation in both groups (82 percent and 88 percent) is what establishes that the two BRCA groups are otherwise the same disease.

key_concepts.term: Homologous recombination deficiency and synthetic lethality
key_concepts.plain_definition: Homologous recombination is the accurate way a cell repairs a double-strand break in DNA, using the intact second copy of the chromosome as a template. BRCA1 and BRCA2 are required for it, so losing either leaves the cell dependent on sloppier backup repair routes, which produces characteristic scars across the genome. Synthetic lethality is the therapeutic consequence: PARP inhibitors such as olaparib block one of those backup routes, which a normal cell can tolerate but an HR-deficient tumour cell cannot, so the drug kills the tumour selectively. In this paper HR deficiency is both the group-defining feature and the proposed upstream cause of the immune differences, quantified as a scarHRD score with a cut-off of 42.

A gene can be silenced without being mutated, by chemical methylation of cytosines in the stretch of DNA that controls its transcription. Heavy methylation of the BRCA1 promoter shuts the gene off and produces the same repair deficiency as a BRCA1 mutation, so it is an epigenetic route to a BRCA-like tumour. This matters here because 4 of the 17 BRCA-mutant tumours were defined by promoter hypermethylation rather than by a sequence change, which was called from Illumina MethylationEPIC arrays processed with minfi v1.50.0 using beta values; it also means a clinical germline test would have scored those four patients as BRCA-wild-type.

COSMIC catalogues the characteristic patterns of single base substitution that different mutational processes leave in a genome, numbered SBS1, SBS2 and so on. SBS3 is the pattern produced when homologous recombination repair has failed, so finding it in a tumour is evidence that the repair pathway really was broken, whatever the genotype says. In this paper SBS3 dominated the BRCA-mutant tumours and was not a top match in the BRCA-wild-type tumours, which instead showed SBS1 (the clock-like signature of spontaneous cytosine deamination) and SBS6 (associated with defective mismatch repair).

key_concepts.term: Spatial transcriptomics spot and why it is not a cell
key_concepts.plain_definition: In the Visium platform the tissue sits on a grid of barcoded capture spots, each about 55 microns wide, and the barcode records where in the tissue each transcript came from. A spot of that size typically covers several to a few tens of cells, so its expression profile is a local mixture rather than a single cell's state. Everything downstream inherits this: a cluster of spots is a region enriched for a cell type, not a purified population, and cell type fractions have to be estimated by deconvolution. The authors list this explicitly as a limitation of all their cluster-level claims.

An integrated cluster is a group of spatial spots that share an expression profile after the data from all patients have been batch-corrected and pooled, so the groups are defined once for the whole cohort rather than separately per tumour. That design is what makes the clusters comparable across patients: you can then ask whether the same region exists in every tumour and whether it behaves differently by genotype. Here 17 such clusters were found, IC1 to IC7 covered about 97 percent of spots and appeared in both genotypes, and the two that carry the paper's argument are IC4 (macrophage-rich) and IC7 (immune-activated).

Cancer-associated fibroblasts are the activated connective tissue cells of a tumour. They lay down the extracellular matrix that gives a tumour its stiff, fibrotic texture, and they secrete growth factors and chemokines that can recruit and reprogramme immune cells. They are not malignant themselves, which is why they count as part of the microenvironment rather than the tumour. In this paper the CAF regions are IC3 and IC5, marked by collagen and matrix genes (COL1A1, COL1A2, COL3A1, DCN, LUM, SPARC, FN1) and activated fibroblast genes (THBS2, CCN2), and IC3 is the predicted source of the signals that condition the neighbouring macrophage niche.

Macrophages are tissue-resident phagocytes that can adopt many functional states. Lipid-associated macrophages are a state first described in obese fat tissue, in which the cell takes on a lipid-handling programme, expressing apolipoprotein genes such as APOE, APOC1 and APOC2 alongside GPNMB and complement genes C1QA and C1QB. The same state is now recognised across tissues and in tumours, where it is generally associated with immune suppression rather than immune attack. In this paper the LAM programme defines IC4, which appeared in every section of both genotypes, which is why the authors call it a structural rather than a genotype-driven feature.

key_concepts.term: Interferon response and antigen processing and presentation
key_concepts.plain_definition: Interferons are cytokines a cell releases when it senses danger such as misplaced DNA or virus, and the interferon response is the broad transcriptional programme they trigger in neighbouring cells. One of its main effects is to raise antigen processing and presentation: the cell chops up its own proteins and displays the fragments on MHC class I molecules at the surface, which is how a cytotoxic T cell can tell that a cell is abnormal. A tumour region with high interferon and high antigen presentation is therefore a region where immune recognition is at least switched on. This pair of programmes is the functional difference the paper finds between genotypes inside IC7.

A join count statistic tests whether labels on a spatial map are clustered or mixed, by counting how often neighbouring positions carry the same label and comparing that with what random arrangement would give. Applied to spatial clusters, it asks whether the regions sit next to each other in a particular arrangement more than chance predicts. Here it was used as a negative control on tissue architecture: it found no significant global spatial differences between BRCA-mutant and BRCA-wild-type tumours (S7 Fig), which is the direct evidence for the paper's claim that the scaffold is conserved and only its function changes.

figures.label: Fig 1
figures.title: Mutational landscape of BRCA-mutant versus BRCA-wild-type HGSOC
figures.question: Do the two cohorts differ in which genes are altered and in which mutational processes have been active?
figures.how_to_read: Panel A is a horizontal bar plot of the percentage of cases with an alteration in each homologous recombination pathway gene, split by cohort and coloured by alteration type. Panel B is a lollipop plot of TP53 mutations along the protein, with the y axis giving the number of samples carrying each mutation, shown for both cohorts. Panel C is a per-patient oncoprint of somatic mutations in 20 genes of interest, with a top plot of mutation count and mutation class per tumour. Panel D shows the single base substitution signature analysis for each group, matched to COSMIC v3 reference signatures by cosine similarity, with the top three matches displayed.
figures.key_result: TP53 was altered in 82 percent of BRCA-mutant (14 of 17) and 88 percent of BRCA-wild-type (7 of 8) tumours; 54.5 percent of TP53 variants were missense and 94.7 percent fell between codons 125 and 300, the DNA-binding domain, with codons 220 and 273 most frequent and Y220C, R273H and R273L seen in both cohorts. Alterations in CSMD3, NF1, FAT3, FANCD2 and EMSY were also detected, with no statistically significant difference between groups in other substitutions. Signature analysis separated the groups: SBS3 was the dominant and best-matching signature only in BRCA-mutant tumours, while BRCA-wild-type tumours showed SBS1 and SBS6 enrichment.

figures.label: Fig 2
figures.title: Copy number change and homologous recombination deficiency scores by BRCA status
figures.question: How much more genomically unstable are the BRCA-mutant tumours, and does that instability reach the clinical HR deficiency threshold?
figures.how_to_read: Panels A and B plot copy number across the genome from whole exome sequencing for BRCA-mutant and BRCA-wild-type tumours respectively, with thresholds at minus 0.5 and plus 0.5 marking loss and gain, gains in red and purple and losses in blue and orange. Panel C shows the same style of profile for BRCA-wild-type samples from TCGA as an external comparison. Panel D is a per-patient bar chart of the scarHRD score, with a dashed line at the HR deficiency threshold of 42.
figures.key_result: BRCA-mutant tumours carried a high copy number burden with gains on 1q, 3q, 8q and 20q and losses on 4q, 5q, 13q and 17p, while BRCA-wild-type tumours had fewer large-scale changes, mainly on 4q and 13q; 469 TCGA BRCA-wild-type samples showed the widespread allelic imbalance typical of HGSOC, and TCGA BRCA-mutant samples were excluded for low numbers. scarHRD medians were 59.0 (IQR 40.0 to 67.0) for BRCA-mutant versus 33.5 (IQR 11.25 to 35.5) for BRCA-wild-type, Hodges-Lehmann shift 28.0 (95 percent CI 7.0 to 48.0), Wilcoxon p = 0.0015, although some BRCA-wild-type tumours still scored as HR deficient.

figures.label: Fig 3
figures.title: Bulk transcriptional and immune differences between genotypes
figures.question: What do bulk RNA-seq and bulk immune deconvolution say about genotype, and is there a genotype-defined immune phenotype at the whole-tumour level?
figures.how_to_read: Panel A is a volcano plot of treatment-adjusted differential expression, with log2 fold change (mutant versus wild-type) on the x axis and minus log10 adjusted p value on the y axis, highlighting genes passing both thresholds. Panel B is a dot plot of Hallmark gene set enrichment, with normalised enrichment score on the x axis, dot size scaled to minus log10 FDR and colour showing direction and magnitude. Panel C is a stacked bar chart of CIBERSORTx absolute abundance for 22 immune cell subsets, one bar per sample. Panel D is a boxplot of predicted neoantigen counts by BRCA status with individual samples shown as dots.
figures.key_result: After adjusting for treatment, a clear BRCA-associated expression signal remained, and the programmes diverged by genotype: BRCA-mutant tumours were enriched for E2F targets, MYC targets, G2M checkpoint, oxidative phosphorylation and DNA repair, a proliferative and metabolically active state, while BRCA-wild-type tumours were enriched for epithelial to mesenchymal transition, myogenesis, hypoxia and estrogen response, a mesenchymal and stress-adapted state. Bulk immune composition varied widely between patients within both groups with no mutation-status-defined polarisation, and predicted neoantigen counts did not differ (Wilcoxon p = 0.902).

figures.label: Fig 4
figures.title: Worked single-tumour spatial architecture, sample HR5
figures.question: What does the spatial structure of one HGSOC tumour look like, and do tumour and immune compartments separate cleanly in space?
figures.how_to_read: Panel A maps each spatial spot coloured by one of seven graph-based clusters. Panel B is the same clusters on a UMAP. Panel C is a violin plot of ESTIMATE tumour purity per cluster and panel D puts purity on the UMAP. Panel E maps ESTIMATE tumour purity, immune score and stromal score back onto the tissue. Panel F is a heatmap of the top five differentially expressed genes per cluster, scaled, with spots as columns grouped by cluster. Panel G is a cluster-level Hallmark GSEA dot plot restricted to FDR below 0.05, with dot size scaled to minus log10 FDR and colour to enrichment score. Panel H maps individual marker genes including IGHG1, EPCAM, GPNMB and APOE by normalised expression. Panel I projects selected Hallmark pathway scores onto the tissue.
figures.key_result: In HR5, a germline BRCA2 tumour, seven spatial clusters emerged. Purity was highest in clusters 2, 4 and 7, while cluster 3 had low purity and was immune enriched; stromal scores marked extensive fibrotic areas and purity outlined malignant regions. Tumour-dominated clusters were enriched for E2F targets and G2M checkpoint genes, whereas immune-enriched clusters showed interferon response, complement and antigen processing and presentation signals. EPCAM localised to high-purity tumour areas and GPNMB to immune-rich areas.

figures.label: Fig 5
figures.title: Integrated spatial clustering identifies recurrent tumour, stromal and immune regions
figures.question: Are the same spatial regions found across all patients, and does BRCA genotype change which regions exist or how big they are?
figures.how_to_read: Panel A is a UMAP of all 40,002 integrated spatial features coloured by integrated cluster IC1 to IC17. Panel B maps the integrated clusters onto two example tumour sections. Panel C bars the number of spatial features per cluster split by BRCA-mutant versus BRCA-wild-type, and panel D shows the percentage contribution of each genotype to each cluster. Panel E is a heatmap of top differentially expressed genes across IC1 to IC7, genes as rows and spots as columns grouped by cluster. Panel F gives violin plots of ESTIMATE tumour purity, immune score and stromal score across clusters. Panel G shows CAF module scores per cluster from Seurat AddModuleScore. Panel H shows the relative proportions of inflammatory, alternatively activated and total macrophage signatures across IC1 to IC7 from xCell.
figures.key_result: Seventeen integrated clusters were defined from about 40,002 spots, with IC1 to IC7 accounting for roughly 97 percent of spots and present in both genotypes, while IC8 to IC17 were sparse or restricted to individual samples. IC1 is the dominant highest-purity tumour compartment, marked by CD24, WFDC2 and MUC1 with E2F target and mTORC1 signalling; IC3 and IC5 are matrix-rich stromal regions marked by COL1A1, COL1A2, COL3A1, DCN, LUM, SPARC and FN1 plus activated fibroblast genes THBS2 and CCN2, with the highest CAF module scores; IC4 is macrophage enriched; IC7 is immune activated. Paired sections from the same patient grouped together before integration, confirming that integration was needed.

figures.label: Fig 6
figures.title: A conserved lipid-associated macrophage region and a predicted fibroblast to macrophage CXCL12/CXCR4 axis
figures.question: What is the macrophage-rich region IC4, is it genotype dependent, and where do its recruitment and conditioning signals come from?
figures.how_to_read: Panel A gives violin plots across IC1 to IC7 of canonical macrophage markers CD68, CD163, GPNMB and LYZ and of lipid-associated macrophage markers APOE, APOC1, C1QA and C1QB. Panel B shows GSEA enrichment of a published LAM programme within IC4. Panel C is a CellChat communication network across IC1 to IC7 computed from pooled spatial features, with clusters as nodes and edge thickness as interaction strength. Panel D is a pair of outgoing and incoming signalling heatmaps for selected pathways, with cluster identity bars on top and overall pathway strength bars on the right. Panel E ranks source clusters by aggregated recruitment-like signalling into IC4 using total communication probability. Panels F and G show CXCL12 and CXCR4, first as spatial feature plots on the tissue and then as violin plots across clusters.
figures.key_result: IC4 is a macrophage region with higher CD68, CD163, GPNMB, C1QA, C1QB and LYZ plus the lipid genes APOC1, APOC2 and APOE, matching a lipid-associated macrophage identity, and RCTD estimated a median macrophage fraction of 13.86 percent inside IC4 versus 5.34 percent elsewhere in the same patients (paired Wilcoxon p = 4.30 x 10^-5, q = 3.01 x 10^-4). IC4 was present in all sections of both genotypes with comparable pathway enrichment, so the authors call it largely BRCA independent. CellChat predicted the CAF-enriched IC3 and IC5 as the dominant signalling sources into IC4, with MIF, APP and complement pathways enriched in that direction, IC3 the single largest contributor of recruitment-like signalling, and CXCL12 enriched in IC3 and IC5 while its receptor CXCR4 was preferentially expressed in IC4.

figures.label: Fig 7
figures.title: IC7 is an immune-activated region whose functional state depends on BRCA status
figures.question: Does BRCA genotype change immune function inside a shared immune region, and does it survive adjustment for treatment?
figures.how_to_read: Panel A shows cohort-wide GSEA of IC7 against curated immune signatures, plotting normalised enrichment score for pathways at FDR below 0.05. Panel B is a genotype-stratified Hallmark GSEA of IC7, mutant versus wild-type, with bars giving normalised enrichment score, coloured where FDR is below 0.05 and grey where not. Panel C compares patients directly on three measures, IC7 abundance as a fraction of spots, an interferon gamma score and an antigen presentation or MHC score, with each point a patient and boxes showing median and interquartile range, and two-sided Wilcoxon p values reported. Panel D shows IC7-specific CellChat communication from genotype-pooled data as total predicted communication probability for immune-related pathways.
figures.key_result: IC7 was enriched for interferon alpha and gamma responses, complement and inflammatory signalling at FDR below 0.05, with patient-level single-sample GSEA scores highest in IC7 for interferon gamma, interferon alpha and TNF alpha/NF-kB signalling. Stratifying by genotype, BRCA-mutant IC7 was enriched for interferon alpha and gamma responses, antigen processing and presentation and inflammatory signalling, whereas in BRCA-wild-type tumours these were reduced and epithelial to mesenchymal transition and tissue remodelling programmes were relatively higher. RCTD gave a higher combined T/NK plus dendritic cell fraction in IC7 (median 7.18 versus 4.85 percent, paired Wilcoxon p = 2.15 x 10^-4, q = 8.81 x 10^-4). At patient level, BRCA-mutant tumours scored higher on IC7 abundance (p = 0.014), interferon gamma signature (p = 0.036) and antigen presentation or MHC score (p = 0.011), surviving Benjamini-Hochberg correction and unchanged when sections were weighted equally within patients. In linear models including treatment, the BRCA effect persisted (IC7 abundance p = 0.044, MHC p = 0.011, interferon gamma p = 0.044) while treatment itself was associated only with the MHC score (p = 0.048). CellChat suggested lower predicted MIF, complement and ICAM activity in BRCA-wild-type tumours.

key_findings.statement: The BRCA-mutant cohort is genuinely homologous recombination deficient and markedly more genomically unstable than the BRCA-wild-type cohort, and this holds across germline mutation, somatic mutation and promoter hypermethylation as routes to BRCA loss.
key_findings.evidence: SBS3 as the dominant mutational signature only in BRCA-mutant tumours (Fig 1D); higher copy number burden with gains on 1q, 3q, 8q, 20q and losses on 4q, 5q, 13q, 17p (Fig 2A to 2C); scarHRD median 59.0 versus 33.5, Wilcoxon p = 0.0015 (Fig 2D).

key_findings.statement: At the bulk transcriptome level the genotypes occupy different cell-intrinsic states, proliferative and metabolic in BRCA-mutant tumours and mesenchymal, hypoxic and stress-adapted in BRCA-wild-type tumours, yet bulk immune composition and predicted neoantigen load do not separate them.
key_findings.evidence: Treatment-adjusted differential expression and Hallmark GSEA showing E2F, MYC, G2M, oxidative phosphorylation and DNA repair in mutant versus epithelial to mesenchymal transition, myogenesis, hypoxia and estrogen response in wild-type (Fig 3A, 3B); CIBERSORTx showing patient-level variability without genotype polarisation (Fig 3C); neoantigen counts not different, Wilcoxon p = 0.902 (Fig 3D).

key_findings.statement: HGSOC tumours are built from a small set of recurrent spatial regions that are present regardless of BRCA genotype: a high-purity tumour compartment, two matrix-rich fibroblast regions, a macrophage region and an immune-activated region.
key_findings.evidence: Integrated clustering of about 40,002 spots across 39 sections from 22 patients, in which IC1 to IC7 account for roughly 97 percent of spots and appear in both genotypes, with marker and ESTIMATE score profiles defining each region (Fig 5A to 5H).

key_findings.statement: BRCA genotype does not reorganise tissue architecture; it changes what the immune region does. IC7 in BRCA-mutant tumours carries stronger interferon alpha and gamma, antigen processing and presentation and inflammatory programmes, and BRCA-mutant patients score higher on IC7 abundance, interferon gamma and MHC scores.
key_findings.evidence: Genotype-stratified GSEA of IC7 (Fig 7B); patient-level comparisons with Wilcoxon p = 0.014, 0.036 and 0.011 surviving Benjamini-Hochberg correction and persisting in treatment-adjusted linear models at p = 0.044, 0.044 and 0.011 (Fig 7C, S8 Fig); join count analysis finding no significant global spatial differences between genotypes (S7 Fig).

key_findings.statement: IC7 is a lymphoid and dendritic cell niche rather than simply a region of high immune gene expression, but the immune difference between genotypes is functional rather than a difference in total immune content.
key_findings.evidence: RCTD deconvolution against the GSE165897 HGSOC single-cell reference gives a median T/NK plus dendritic cell fraction of 7.18 percent in IC7 versus 4.85 percent elsewhere in the same patients, paired Wilcoxon p = 2.15 x 10^-4, q = 8.81 x 10^-4 (S5B Fig); the Discussion states there was no significant genotype-associated increase in macrophage or total immune content.

key_findings.statement: A lipid-associated macrophage region (IC4) is a conserved structural feature of HGSOC, present in every section of both genotypes, and it sits adjacent to a fibroblast region that is the predicted source of its recruitment and conditioning signals.
key_findings.evidence: Macrophage and lipid-associated macrophage markers and LAM programme enrichment in IC4 (Fig 6A, 6B); RCTD median macrophage fraction 13.86 versus 5.34 percent, paired Wilcoxon p = 4.30 x 10^-5, q = 3.01 x 10^-4 (S5C Fig); CellChat identifying IC3 and IC5 as dominant sources with MIF, APP and complement enrichment and IC3 the largest recruitment contributor (Fig 6C to 6E).

key_findings.statement: A CXCL12 to CXCR4 axis is proposed as the link between the fibroblast region and the macrophage region, with the ligand in the fibroblast clusters and the receptor in the macrophage cluster.
key_findings.evidence: Spatial feature plots and violin plots showing CXCL12 enriched in IC3 and IC5 and CXCR4 preferentially expressed in IC4 (Fig 6F, 6G), interpreted through CellChat; no protein, secretion or perturbation experiment was performed.

key_findings.statement: The BRCA-associated immune difference is not driven by one class of BRCA alteration and is not explained by prior neoadjuvant treatment.
key_findings.evidence: Descriptive subgroup analysis in which germline BRCA1, germline BRCA2, BRCA1 promoter hypermethylation and somatic BRCA1 subgroups all showed higher median IC7 abundance, MHC and interferon gamma than BRCA-wild-type (S6 Fig); linear models with treatment as a covariate retaining the BRCA effect while treatment was associated only with the MHC score (p = 0.048).

limitations: Small and unbalanced cohort: 17 BRCA-mutant versus 8 BRCA-wild-type for the genomic arm and 16 versus 6 for the spatial arm, so the wild-type comparison group is only six patients for the central IC7 claim.
Retrospective and exploratory design driven by sample availability, with no formal power calculation, which the authors state explicitly.

Visium spots contain mixed-cell transcriptomes, so every integrated cluster is a marker-enriched region and not a purified cell population; single-cell and proteomic work is needed to confirm composition.
Cell type fractions come from reference-based deconvolution (RCTD against GSE165897) and therefore inherit any bias in that reference; the authors treat them as hypothesis generating.

All cell to cell communication claims, including the CXCL12/CXCR4 axis and the MIF, complement and ICAM differences, are CellChat predictions from expression data with no protein, binding or perturbation validation.
The genotype-level CellChat comparison in Fig 7D was computed from genotype-pooled spots rather than per patient, so it is not a patient-level statistical test.
No survival or outcome analysis was possible because the cohort had no censoring events, so none of the immune differences can be tied to prognosis or to PARP inhibitor response.

Treatment status was mixed (roughly half treatment naive, half neoadjuvant treated) and the treatment-stratified subsets were tiny (9 mutant versus 2 wild-type naive, 7 versus 4 neoadjuvant), so the treatment-adjusted conclusion rests on a covariate model rather than on balanced groups.
The study is purely observational human tissue with no functional perturbation, so causality from BRCA loss through genomic instability to interferon signalling is inferred, not tested.

Estrogen and estrogen receptor signalling were not examined; the only estrogen-related observation in the paper is enrichment of the Hallmark estrogen response gene set in bulk BRCA-wild-type tumours (Fig 3B), with no receptor localisation, no hormone measurement and no stromal or myeloid estrogen receptor analysis.
One internal inconsistency is visible in the text: the Methods describe 10 germline BRCA1 tumours while the Results cite n = 9 for that subgroup.
open_questions: Is the interferon and antigen presentation signal inside IC7 produced by the tumour cells, the infiltrating lymphoid and dendritic cells, or the surrounding stroma? Spot-level mixtures cannot resolve this, and the answer determines whether BRCA loss acts cell intrinsically through cytosolic DNA sensing or through a paracrine route.

Does the higher antigen presentation score in BRCA-mutant tumours reflect classical MHC class I that supports cytotoxic killing, or does it include non-classical inhibitory molecules such as HLA-E that would suppress natural killer cells? The paper reports an aggregate MHC score and does not break out individual HLA genes.

Are the T and natural killer cells enriched in IC7 functional or exhausted? Composition was inferred by deconvolution, and no activation, exhaustion or cytotoxicity markers were examined at the cell level.

Does the predicted CXCL12 to CXCR4 axis actually recruit or condition the lipid-associated macrophage niche? This needs protein-level work and a perturbation, for example CXCR4 blockade in an HGSOC model, to move from prediction to mechanism.

Does the lipid-associated macrophage region suppress the adjacent immune-activated region? The two are described separately and their interface was not analysed, so whether IC4 constrains IC7 is untested.

Does the BRCA-wild-type mesenchymal and estrogen response enriched state cause the attenuated immune phenotype, or merely accompany it? The bulk estrogen response enrichment is unexplained and unfollowed in the paper.
Do any of these spatial immune differences predict response to PARP inhibitors or immune checkpoint blockade? The cohort had no outcome events, so the clinical implication is entirely untested.
Does the conserved spatial scaffold already exist in precancerous fallopian tube and ovarian tissue, or does it assemble during tumour growth? The cohort is all late-stage disease.
reading.relevance_to_lab: This paper is useful to the lab mainly as a human spatial map of the ovarian stromal and myeloid microenvironment, and as partial human support for the lab's BRCA1 model, but it is important to be clear that it does not test estrogen at all. Where it connects. First, it provides exactly the kind of human readout the lab's BRCA1-deficient breast cancer model predicts: in human HGSOC, BRCA deficiency is associated with higher interferon alpha and gamma response, higher antigen processing and presentation, and higher TNF alpha/NF-kB signalling in an immune region that is genuinely enriched for T, natural killer and dendritic cells. That is the lab's chain of BRCA1 loss, cytosolic DNA, cGAS-STING, NF-kB and IRF3, type I interferon, raised MHC class I, observed as a correlation in patient tissue rather than in mice, and it is observed in situ rather than in bulk. Second, it is a clean methodological template for the lab's own scRNA-seq and spatial work: integrated clustering across patients before comparing genotypes, RCTD deconvolution against a matched single-cell reference (GSE165897), patient-level aggregation of spot-level scores so that statistics are done on patients and not on spots, join count analysis as an explicit negative control for architecture, and a treatment-adjusted linear model as a sensitivity check. The patient-level aggregation and the join count control are directly borrowable for the BRCA1 project. Third, on the myeloid strand, the paper describes a lipid-associated macrophage region defined by APOE, APOC1, APOC2, GPNMB, C1QA, C1QB, CD68 and CD163 that is present in every tumour of both genotypes and receives predicted CXCL12 to CXCR4, MIF and complement signals from a neighbouring CAF region marked by COL1A1, COL1A2, COL3A1, DCN, LUM, SPARC, FN1, THBS2 and CCN2. That is a concrete human gene set for a stroma to myeloid conditioning axis in ovarian cancer, and the lab's own model of stromal control of the epithelium through ECM genes and cytokines is the same architecture one tissue layer over. Where it does not reach the lab's model. Estrogen and ESR1 are absent: the only estrogen content in the whole paper is enrichment of the Hallmark estrogen response gene set in bulk BRCA-wild-type tumours in Fig 3B, with no estrogen receptor localisation, no stromal or myeloid estrogen receptor analysis, no hormone manipulation and no comment on it in the Discussion. So neither strand of the lab's estrogen topic is tested. On strand 1, the cohort is all late-stage carcinoma, not fallopian tube or ovary before cancer, and POSTN, FGF1, FGF2, IL1 and CCL2 are not reported; TNF and NF-kB appear only as a pathway score in IC7, and the CAF region is characterised by matrix and chemokine genes rather than by the lab's differentiation-supporting programme. On strand 2, macrophage estrogen receptor signalling is not examined, and the lipid-associated macrophage state is explicitly described as BRCA independent, with no hormonal variable in the analysis. On the BRCA1 breast strand, the readout stops at an aggregate MHC score: HLA-C, HLA-E and NKG2A are not reported individually, natural killer cells are pooled with T cells in the deconvolution, and there is no functional assessment of surveillance. The specific gap worth noting is that this paper shows the BRCA-associated interferon and antigen presentation phenotype exists in human ovarian tissue but says nothing about whether the accompanying lymphoid cells are actually killing anything, which is precisely the part of the lab's model that matters.
discussion_questions: The paper reports an aggregate antigen presentation and MHC score, which is higher in BRCA-mutant tumours. If we re-analysed their spatial data at the level of individual genes, would the signal come from classical HLA-A, HLA-B and HLA-C or also from HLA-E, which would recruit NKG2A and suppress natural killer cells rather than enable killing? That is the difference between immune activation and immune evasion in our own BRCA1 model.

Their central claim is that BRCA status changes function inside a conserved spatial scaffold, with a join count analysis as the negative control for architecture. Should we add the same patient-level aggregation and join count control to our scRNA-seq comparison of BRCA1 carrier and non-carrier breast tissue, so we can say whether we are seeing a change in composition or a change in state?

The CAF to lipid-associated macrophage axis they propose, CXCL12 from IC3 and IC5 into CXCR4 on IC4 plus MIF and complement, is the same architecture as our stromal to epithelial model, one layer over. Is it worth checking whether POSTN, FGF1, FGF2, TNF, IL1 and CCL2 are co-located with their CAF clusters in this public dataset, which would tell us whether our stromal programme is present in late-stage HGSOC or is specific to the precancerous fallopian tube and ovary?

Estrogen appears in this paper only as the Hallmark estrogen response set being enriched in bulk BRCA-wild-type tumours, and the authors do not comment on it. Is that an incidental consequence of the mesenchymal and hypoxic state these tumours occupy, or a real hormonal difference worth following, and could we test it in their data by scoring ESR1 and its targets in the CAF and macrophage regions separately?

Their design starts from late-stage carcinoma, so the conserved scaffold could be a product of tumour growth rather than a pre-existing tissue organisation. If we applied their integrated clustering to fallopian tube and ovarian tissue before cancer, would we find the same seven regions, and would the stromal estrogen receptor state we propose map onto their IC3 and IC5?

nodes.label: How does BRCA status shape the HGSOC immune microenvironment?
nodes.detail: BRCA1/2 status is known to govern DNA repair and drug response in high-grade serous ovarian cancer, but its effect on the surrounding immune and stromal tissue is unclear.

nodes.label: BRCA1/2 loss causes instability; bulk data cannot resolve space
nodes.detail: Germline BRCA1/2 mutations occur in roughly 20 to 22 percent of HGSOC, impair homologous recombination repair and are exploited by PARP inhibitors through synthetic lethality; genomic instability is expected to change immunogenicity, but bulk sequencing averages tumour, immune and stromal compartments, so it cannot tell a change in architecture from a change in local function.

nodes.label: BRCA-driven instability reshapes spatial immune niches
nodes.detail: The authors reasoned that BRCA-dependent genomic states would be reflected in the spatial distribution, signalling and functional programmes of tumour, immune and stromal niches.

nodes.label: WES, methylation and bulk RNA-seq on 25 HGSOC tumours
nodes.detail: Twenty-five late-stage HGSOC tumours with matched normal DNA were profiled by whole exome sequencing, MethylationEPIC arrays and total RNA sequencing, giving 17 BRCA-mutant and 8 BRCA-wild-type cases.

nodes.label: Visium spatial transcriptomics on 39 sections from 22 patients
nodes.detail: Thirty-nine quality-passing Visium sections from 22 of the same patients were clustered after cross-patient integration, with ESTIMATE scores, RCTD deconvolution and CellChat inference layered on top.

nodes.label: BRCA-mutant tumours are truly HR deficient and more unstable
nodes.detail: SBS3 dominated only in BRCA-mutant tumours, which also carried a far higher copy number burden and a higher scarHRD score (median 59.0 versus 33.5, Wilcoxon p = 0.0015).

nodes.label: Bulk programmes split proliferative versus mesenchymal
nodes.detail: Treatment-adjusted expression and Hallmark GSEA put BRCA-mutant tumours in a proliferative, metabolic, DNA repair state and BRCA-wild-type tumours in a mesenchymal, hypoxic, estrogen response enriched state.

nodes.label: Bulk immune composition and neoantigen load do not separate genotypes
nodes.detail: CIBERSORTx showed wide patient-to-patient variation without genotype polarisation, and predicted neoantigen counts were indistinguishable (Wilcoxon p = 0.902), so any immune difference had to be local.

nodes.label: Seven recurrent spatial regions appear in both genotypes
nodes.detail: Integrated clustering of about 40,002 spots gave 17 clusters, of which IC1 to IC7 covered roughly 97 percent of spots and were found in both BRCA-mutant and BRCA-wild-type tumours.

nodes.label: IC4 is a lipid-associated macrophage region present in every tumour
nodes.detail: IC4 carried macrophage and lipid-handling markers, enriched for a published LAM programme, and RCTD put its macrophage fraction at 13.86 versus 5.34 percent elsewhere, with comparable enrichment in both genotypes.

nodes.label: CAF region IC3 is the predicted source of CXCL12 signals into IC4
nodes.detail: CellChat ranked the fibroblast clusters IC3 and IC5 as the dominant sources of signalling into IC4 through MIF, APP and complement, with CXCL12 in the fibroblast clusters matching CXCR4 in IC4.

nodes.label: IC7 is interferon driven and functionally stronger in BRCA-mutant tumours
nodes.detail: IC7 carried interferon alpha and gamma, complement and inflammatory programmes and was enriched for T, natural killer and dendritic cells; BRCA-mutant patients scored higher on IC7 abundance, interferon gamma and MHC scores (p = 0.014, 0.036, 0.011), persisting after treatment adjustment.

nodes.label: Tissue architecture itself does not differ by genotype
nodes.detail: Join count analysis found no significant global spatial differences between BRCA-mutant and BRCA-wild-type tumours, and the Discussion notes no genotype-associated increase in macrophage or total immune content.

nodes.label: Genotype tunes immune function within a conserved spatial scaffold
nodes.detail: BRCA status is associated with functional differences inside broadly conserved spatial regions rather than with a different tissue organisation, which reconciles the clear bulk programme difference with the absent bulk immune difference.

nodes.label: The stromal to myeloid niche is a structural, genotype-independent feature
nodes.detail: The CAF to lipid-associated macrophage interface exists in every tumour regardless of BRCA status, so it behaves as part of the tissue scaffold rather than as a consequence of tumour genotype.

nodes.label: Target stromal to myeloid signalling to widen immune-permissive niches
nodes.detail: For BRCA-wild-type or immune-attenuated tumours, the authors propose combining immune-directed therapy with approaches that modify stromal and myeloid interactions, since immune activation appears to be niche limited rather than globally absent.

entities.name: BRCA1
entities.description: Homologous recombination repair gene whose germline mutation, somatic mutation or promoter hypermethylation defined most of the BRCA-mutant group in this cohort.

entities.name: BRCA2
entities.description: Second homologous recombination repair gene; two germline BRCA2 cases were included in the BRCA-mutant group, one of which (HR5) was the worked single-tumour example.

entities.name: TP53
entities.description: Tumour suppressor mutated in 82 percent of BRCA-mutant and 88 percent of BRCA-wild-type tumours here, confirming both groups are canonical HGSOC.

entities.name: High-grade serous ovarian cancer
entities.description: The single disease studied, represented by 25 pathologist-confirmed late-stage tumours with matched normal tissue.

entities.name: Homologous recombination deficiency
entities.description: Failure of accurate double-strand break repair, quantified here by scarHRD and treated as the upstream cause of the genotype-associated immune differences.

entities.name: COSMIC SBS3 signature
entities.description: Mutational fingerprint of failed homologous recombination repair, dominant only in the BRCA-mutant tumours.

entities.name: IC1 tumour region
entities.description: The dominant high-purity malignant spatial compartment, marked by CD24, WFDC2 and MUC1 with E2F target and mTORC1 signalling.

entities.name: IC3 CAF region
entities.description: Matrix-rich fibroblast spatial region with the highest CAF module scores, identified as the main predicted source of signalling into the macrophage region.

entities.name: IC4 lipid-associated macrophage region
entities.description: Macrophage-enriched spatial region carrying a lipid-handling programme, present in all sections of both genotypes and therefore described as BRCA independent.

entities.name: IC7 immune-activated region
entities.description: Low-purity immune spatial region carrying interferon, complement and inflammatory programmes, whose functional state differs by BRCA genotype.

entities.name: Cancer-associated fibroblast
entities.description: Activated stromal cell type populating IC3 and IC5, marked by collagen and matrix genes and by the activated fibroblast genes THBS2 and CCN2.

entities.name: Lipid-associated macrophage
entities.description: Macrophage functional state defined by apolipoprotein and GPNMB expression, originally described in metabolic disease and here enriched in IC4.

entities.name: Macrophage
entities.description: Myeloid cell type whose inferred fraction was 13.86 percent inside IC4 versus 5.34 percent elsewhere in the same patients.

entities.name: T and NK cells
entities.description: Lymphoid populations pooled in the deconvolution; together with dendritic cells they were enriched in IC7 at 7.18 versus 4.85 percent.

entities.name: Dendritic cell
entities.description: Antigen-presenting myeloid cell pooled with T and NK cells in the RCTD estimate for IC7.

entities.name: CXCL12
entities.description: Chemokine enriched in the fibroblast regions IC3 and IC5 and proposed as the recruiting signal toward the macrophage region.

entities.name: CXCR4
entities.description: Receptor for CXCL12, preferentially expressed in the IC4 macrophage region, completing the predicted recruitment axis.

entities.name: MIF
entities.description: Macrophage migration inhibitory factor, one of the pathways CellChat found enriched in signalling from the fibroblast regions into IC4 and lower in BRCA-wild-type tumours.

entities.name: APOE
entities.description: Apolipoprotein marking the lipid-associated macrophage programme in IC4, together with APOC1 and APOC2.

entities.name: GPNMB
entities.description: Lipid-associated macrophage marker mapped to immune-rich regions in the single-tumour analysis and enriched in IC4.

entities.name: CD68
entities.description: Canonical macrophage marker used, with CD163 and LYZ, to identify IC4 as a macrophage region.

entities.name: COL1A1
entities.description: Collagen gene representative of the extracellular matrix signature that defines the stromal regions IC3 and IC5.

entities.name: Interferon alpha and gamma response
entities.description: Transcriptional programme enriched in IC7 across the cohort and significantly stronger in BRCA-mutant tumours.

entities.name: Antigen processing and presentation
entities.description: MHC-linked programme enriched in BRCA-mutant IC7; the patient-level MHC score was the strongest genotype difference reported (p = 0.011).

entities.name: TNF alpha and NF-kB signalling
entities.description: Inflammatory programme that was among the highest scoring pathways in IC7 by patient-level single-sample GSEA.

entities.name: Epithelial to mesenchymal transition
entities.description: Programme enriched in bulk BRCA-wild-type tumours and relatively higher in BRCA-wild-type IC7, where immune programmes were attenuated.

entities.name: Estrogen response
entities.description: Hallmark gene set enriched in bulk BRCA-wild-type tumours; this is the paper's only estrogen-related observation and it is not pursued further.

entities.name: E2F and MYC proliferative programme
entities.description: Cell cycle and growth programmes enriched in bulk BRCA-mutant tumours and in the high-purity tumour regions.

entities.name: PARP inhibitor
entities.description: Class of drug, including olaparib, that kills homologous recombination deficient tumours by synthetic lethality; cited as background motivation rather than tested here.

entities.name: Visium spatial transcriptomics
entities.description: Spot-based platform used on 39 sections from 22 patients to measure expression while keeping tissue position.

entities.name: RCTD deconvolution
entities.description: Reference-based method used to estimate cell type fractions per spot, run against an HGSOC single-cell reference.

entities.name: CellChat
entities.description: Ligand-receptor inference tool used to predict which spatial regions signal to which; all communication claims in the paper rest on it.

entities.name: scarHRD
entities.description: Scoring tool that sums loss of heterozygosity, telomeric allelic imbalance and large-scale state transitions into a single HR deficiency score, with 42 as the threshold.

entities.name: GSE165897 HGSOC single-cell reference
entities.description: Published HGSOC single-cell atlas from Zhang et al. used as the reference for RCTD deconvolution of the spatial spots.

relations.evidence: BRCA1 loss by germline mutation, somatic mutation or promoter hypermethylation impairs homologous recombination repair.
BRCA2 is required for homologous recombination repair, so its germline loss produces the same repair deficiency.
TP53 mutation was near universal across both cohorts, as established for HGSOC by TCGA.
PARP inhibitors such as olaparib kill homologous recombination deficient tumours through synthetic lethality.
SBS3 was the dominant and best-matched mutational signature only in the BRCA-mutant tumours, confirming functional repair failure.
scarHRD scores were markedly higher in BRCA-mutant tumours, median 59.0 versus 33.5, Wilcoxon p = 0.0015.
Bulk BRCA-mutant tumours were enriched for E2F targets, MYC targets, G2M checkpoint, oxidative phosphorylation and DNA repair.
Epithelial to mesenchymal transition, myogenesis and hypoxia were enriched in bulk BRCA-wild-type tumours.
The Hallmark estrogen response set was enriched in bulk BRCA-wild-type tumours; the paper reports this without following it up.
Thirty-nine quality-passing Visium sections from 22 patients provided the spatial measurements underlying all region-level claims.
The high-purity tumour compartment IC1 was enriched for E2F targets and mTORC1 signalling.
COL1A1 with COL1A2, COL3A1, DCN, LUM, SPARC and FN1 defined the matrix-rich stromal regions IC3 and IC5.
CAF module scores were highest in IC3 and IC5, identifying them as fibroblast regions.
CD68 with CD163, LYZ and GPNMB marked IC4 as a macrophage region.
APOE with APOC1 and APOC2 plus C1QA and C1QB defined the lipid-associated macrophage programme.
GPNMB was enriched in IC4 and mapped to immune-rich areas in the single-tumour analysis.
GSEA showed strong enrichment of a published lipid-associated macrophage programme within IC4.
RCTD estimated a median macrophage fraction of 13.86 percent in IC4 versus 5.34 percent elsewhere in the same patients, q = 3.01 x 10^-4.
RCTD deconvolution was run against the Zhang et al. HGSOC single-cell reference GSE165897.
CXCL12 was enriched in the fibroblast regions IC3 and IC5 on both spatial feature plots and violin plots.
CXCR4 was preferentially expressed in the IC4 macrophage region.
CellChat predicted a CXCL12 to CXCR4 recruitment axis from the fibroblast regions into IC4; this is an expression-based prediction with no functional validation.
CellChat ranked IC3 as the largest contributor of aggregated recruitment-like signalling into IC4, with MIF, APP and complement pathways enriched.
MIF was among the pathways enriched in predicted signalling from the fibroblast regions toward IC4.
IC7 showed GSEA enrichment for interferon alpha and gamma responses alongside complement and inflammatory signalling at FDR below 0.05.
Patient-level single-sample GSEA scores were highest in IC7 for interferon gamma, interferon alpha and TNF alpha/NF-kB signalling.
RCTD gave a median combined T/NK plus dendritic cell fraction of 7.18 percent in IC7 versus 4.85 percent elsewhere, q = 8.81 x 10^-4.
Dendritic cells were pooled with T and NK cells in the RCTD estimate showing enrichment inside IC7.
BRCA-mutant tumours showed stronger interferon alpha and gamma enrichment inside IC7 and a higher patient-level interferon gamma score (p = 0.036, p = 0.044 after treatment adjustment).
Antigen processing and presentation was enriched in BRCA-mutant IC7 and the patient-level MHC score was higher in BRCA-mutant tumours (p = 0.011, retained at p = 0.011 after treatment adjustment).
In BRCA-wild-type tumours the immune programmes in IC7 were reduced while epithelial to mesenchymal transition and tissue remodelling programmes were relatively higher.
Predicted MIF, complement and ICAM activity in IC7 was lower in BRCA-wild-type than BRCA-mutant tumours, which the authors describe as exploratory and computed from genotype-pooled spots.
IC4 appeared in every section of both genotypes with comparable pathway enrichment, so the authors treat it as a conserved structural feature of HGSOC tissue.
IC7 was one of the seven recurrent integrated regions present in both genotypes; join count analysis found no significant global spatial difference between genotypes.

papers.title: Cell-of-origin shapes tumor subtype in BRCA1-associated triple-negative breast cancer
papers.authors: Lev T, Samy ALPA, et al.

bibliographic.title: Cell-of-origin shapes tumor subtype in BRCA1-associated triple-negative breast cancer

reading.one_line_takeaway: In BRCA1-mutant mice the basal-myoepithelial compartment, not only the luminal progenitor compartment, gives rise to triple-negative breast cancer, and which compartment a tumor starts in sets which molecular subtype it becomes: basal-myoepithelial origin gives the mesenchymal subtype and luminal origin gives the basal-like 1 subtype.
reading.tldr: The field has largely settled on the view that BRCA1-associated triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) starts in luminal progenitor cells, a conclusion built mainly on the Blg-Cre Brca1/p53 mouse model. Lev and colleagues profiled a less used model, Wap-Cre Brca1/p53, by single-cell RNA sequencing (67,001 cells in total across the study) and reanalyzed the published Blg-Cre data with the same pipeline. Wap-Cre tumors turn out to carry a broad basal program and to classify as the mesenchymal TNBC subtype, while Blg-Cre tumors classify as basal-like 1, and both subtypes occur at similar frequency in human BRCA1 carriers. Single-cell genotyping shows that the Wap-Cre driver recombines both basal-myoepithelial and secretory luminal cells, so the basal phenotype is not an artifact of where the Cre is active, and in a transplantation experiment using matched donors only the sorted basal fraction produced tumors containing basal cells. Along the way the authors show that basal-myoepithelial cells lose their myoepithelial markers and drift into a fetal-like basal state in pre-malignant glands, before any tumor is visible.
reading.research_question: What determines the molecular subtype of a BRCA1-associated triple-negative breast cancer, and in particular does the cell type in which BRCA1 is lost decide which subtype the resulting tumor becomes?
reading.background: Carrying a pathogenic germline BRCA1 variant raises the cumulative risk of breast cancer to as much as 72 percent by age 80, and there is no targeted prevention. BRCA1 protects the genome by enforcing cell-cycle checkpoints and by supporting homologous recombination, the accurate form of double-strand break repair, so losing it drives error-prone repair and copy-number change. The authors argue that genomic instability on its own cannot explain why the cancer risk concentrates in hormone-responsive organs such as breast and ovary. BRCA1 also has an E3 ubiquitin ligase domain that targets hormone receptors for degradation, and hormone receptors in turn direct how mammary epithelial cells differentiate, so BRCA1 loss plausibly acts through a non-genetic, differentiation-based route as well. Separately, bulk transcriptome profiling splits TNBC into four subtypes, basal-like 1 (BL1), basal-like 2 (BL2), mesenchymal (M) and luminal androgen receptor (LAR), which differ in prognosis and drug response, yet what decides a tumor's subtype is unknown and subtype is not used to stratify BRCA1 carriers. On the mouse side, two epithelial sources had been reported: Blg-Cre deletion of Brca1 in luminal progenitors gives invasive ductal-like tumors, and Krt14-Cre deletion in basal cells gives metaplastic-like tumors that are rare in human carriers. The Blg-Cre model has dominated the field, and single-cell work in it showed aberrant luminal differentiation and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition before tumors appear. The gap the authors address is that this one model does not reproduce the full spectrum of human BRCA1 carrier disease, and that the cell of origin of the Wap-Cre Brca1/p53 model was never established.
reading.study_design: The central model is Wap-Cre;Brca1 f10/f10;p53 f5and6/f5and6 on a mixed 129/SvJ and C57BL/6 background, in which loxP sites flank Brca1 exon 10 and p53 exons 5 and 6. Only females were used. Mutant glands show ductal hyperplasia, excess side branching and precocious alveolar formation, and spontaneous tumors appear at about 6 months. Mammary tissue was taken from 4-month-old mutant females with no visible tumor plus wild-type littermates, and tumors were collected across a size range from 1 to 25 mm. Samples were multiplexed and run on droplet single-cell RNA sequencing, leaving 62,195 cells after quality control in the main dataset and 67,001 cells across the whole study. Published Blg-Cre;Brca1 f21-23/f21-23;p53 f/+ single-cell data were reprocessed through the identical pipeline so the two models could be compared directly. Human comparisons used two TNBC cohorts: the Basser-Gray Foundation Repository (BGFR) with 51 TNBC patients, 35 BRCA1 carriers and 16 non-carriers, of which 17 were previously described and 34 are newly reported, and TCGA TNBC with 132 patients, 12 BRCA1 carriers and 120 non-carriers. The decisive causal experiment is a lineage-restricted transplantation: basal and luminal fractions were sorted from pre-tumor mutant donors and implanted into cleared mammary fat pads of immunodeficient NSG recipients, 8 recipients receiving basal on one side and luminal on the other plus 1 receiving basal bilaterally, in two independent experiments with distinct donor pools. Supporting layers are single-cell genotyping of the recombined Trp53 allele, spatial proteomics by CODEX on wild-type glands, mutant glands and small and large tumors, integration with a mouse developmental mammary atlas spanning fetal through involution stages, integration with the Human Breast Cell Atlas, and an experimental metastasis assay in which cells from one late-stage tumor were injected intracardially into 6 NSG mice with 2 orthotopic controls and tissues harvested at 4 weeks.

key_methods.name: Multiplexed droplet single-cell RNA sequencing
key_methods.plain_explanation: Tissue is broken into single cells, and each cell is captured in its own tiny oil droplet together with a bead carrying a unique DNA barcode. Every messenger RNA molecule from that cell picks up the cell's barcode, so after everything is sequenced together the reads can be sorted back to the cell they came from. The result is a table of how much each gene was switched on in each individual cell, which lets you find cell types and cell states instead of averaging the whole tissue. Here the cells from several animals were also tagged with short oligonucleotide labels (CellPlex) so that multiple samples could share one sequencing lane and then be separated computationally.
key_methods.how_used: Run on a 10x Chromium Controller X with Next GEM 3 prime v3.1 chemistry, CellPlex barcoding, up to 30,000 cells per lane and roughly 2,500 cells per tag, sequenced on a NovaSeq 6000 at a target of at least 15,000 read pairs per cell. Processing used Cell Ranger v7.0.1 against the mm10 reference, ambient RNA removal with SoupX, cluster-specific gene and transcript count thresholds, a mitochondrial read cutoff of 5 to 8 percent depending on batch, and doublet removal with DoubletFinder that required three independent signs of a doublet before a cell was discarded. Analysis used Scanpy and Seurat, with highly variable genes chosen by BigSur, 40 principal components, Leiden clustering, and scVI batch correction for the epithelial sub-clustering. Samples covered wild-type glands, pre-tumor mutant glands and tumors from 1 to 25 mm in the Wap-Cre model, with the published Blg-Cre data reprocessed identically.
key_methods.why_it_matters: It is what allows the authors to say that Wap-Cre tumor cells sit on a continuum between basal-myoepithelial and secretory luminal identity while Blg-Cre tumor cells form a discrete luminal cluster, a distinction that bulk sequencing would erase. The caveat is that dissociation and droplet capture can under-sample fragile or tightly attached cell types, and the Blg-Cre comparison is to data generated in another laboratory with a different Cre driver and different floxed alleles.

key_methods.name: Copy-number inference from single-cell transcriptomes (CopyKAT)
key_methods.plain_explanation: Tumor cells usually carry whole chromosome arms gained or lost, which is called aneuploidy. You normally need DNA sequencing to see that, but if a region of a chromosome is duplicated then all of the genes along it tend to be expressed a little more, so the smoothed average expression across a chromosome can be used to infer gains and losses from RNA data alone. CopyKAT does this by comparing each cell's smoothed expression profile along the genome against known normal cells, and then calls each cell aneuploid or diploid. In practice it is how a study separates genuinely transformed cells from the normal cells sitting next to them.
key_methods.how_used: CopyKAT v1.1.0 adapted to the mm10 mouse genome, applied to epithelial cells only and excluding luminal hormone-sensing cells. Normal baselines were FACS-sorted wild-type epithelium from two mice plus a third mouse and a pooled control; one batch tumor was analyzed separately using stromal cells from the same sample as the diploid reference.
key_methods.why_it_matters: It is the tool that identifies the transformed cells inside pre-malignant glands, which is what lets the authors claim that aberrant basal differentiation is already present before any tumor is visible, and it is how they conclude that in the Blg-Cre data only luminal cells are transformed. That last point is also its weakest use: the authors state plainly that because they could not obtain physical Blg-Cre material for genotyping, the claim that only luminal cells transform in that model rests on inference from expression rather than on direct genotype.

key_methods.name: Single-cell genotyping of the recombined allele (MAESTER-based targeted amplification)
key_methods.plain_explanation: In a conditional knockout mouse, Cre recombinase cuts out the loxP-flanked piece of a gene only in the cells where the Cre driver is active. To know which cell types actually experienced that deletion, you need to read the genotype in the same individual cells you profiled. The approach here takes the barcoded full-length complementary DNA already made during single-cell library preparation and amplifies one specific transcript out of it with targeted PCR, keeping the cell barcode attached, so the recombined versus intact sequence can be read per cell and matched to that cell's transcriptome-defined identity.
key_methods.how_used: Brca1 is too large for multiplexed PCR of this kind, so the authors used the Trp53 transcript as a proxy, which is valid because the same Wap-Cre driver recombines both floxed alleles. A first PCR from 20 ng of barcoded cDNA used a Trp53-specific forward primer and a barcoded reverse primer, a second PCR added Illumina adaptors and dual indexes, and the library was sequenced on a MiSeq Micro at 300 base paired-end for about 4 million reads.
key_methods.why_it_matters: This is the control that makes the central claim defensible. If the Wap promoter only fired in secretory luminal cells, a basal phenotype could be dismissed as mislabeling. Instead both basal-myoepithelial and secretory luminal cells in mutant Wap-Cre glands carry recombined alleles, so restricted Cre activity cannot explain why the tumors are basal. The limitation is that it needs physical tissue, so it could not be applied to the published Blg-Cre dataset.

key_methods.name: Lineage-restricted mammary fat pad transplantation
key_methods.plain_explanation: The mammary fat pad of a very young mouse can be surgically emptied of its own epithelium, leaving the fat and connective tissue behind.
