papers.title: MicroRNA spatial profiling for assessing drug efficacy in BRCA1-related triple-negative breast tumors

bibliographic.title: MicroRNA spatial profiling for assessing drug efficacy in BRCA1-related triple-negative breast tumors

reading.one_line_takeaway: In BRCA1/Trp53-null mouse mammary tumors, the spatial arrangement of just two microRNAs, miR-21-5p and let-7a-5p, measured in situ after only 10 days of treatment, separates PARP-inhibitor-sensitive from resistant tumors and separates olaparib alone from olaparib plus alpelisib or poly(I:C), even where bulk microRNA levels and survival curves do not.
reading.tldr: BRCA1-mutant breast cancers respond to PARP inhibitors at first but most eventually progress, and there is no early readout that tells you whether a given tumor is responding. The authors took K14-Cre Brca1 flox/flox Trp53 flox/flox mouse mammary tumors, both treatment-naive (olaparib-sensitive) and tumors made resistant by continuous olaparib, and asked whether adding a PI3K inhibitor (alpelisib) or an innate immune agonist (poly(I:C)) to olaparib helps, and whether a spatial microRNA readout taken 10 days into treatment predicts the outcome. Both combinations roughly doubled time to the 20 mm endpoint in sensitive tumors, and alpelisib but not poly(I:C) gave a significant extension in resistant tumors. Measuring seven microRNAs in situ on tissue sections with a hydrogel nanoliter-well array and then summarising the maps with a topic model (latent Dirichlet allocation) plus principal component analysis, a miR-21-dominated spatial pattern tracked with sensitivity and a let-7a-dominated pattern tracked with resistance, with tumors separating along a single principal component that carried 96 percent of the variance. Overlaying CD45 immunohistochemistry on serial sections and comparing immune-infiltration maps with the microRNA topic maps using the structural similarity index, immune infiltration generally matched the let-7a pattern, except in sensitive tumors given olaparib plus poly(I:C), where it matched the miR-21 pattern.
reading.research_question: Can adding PI3K inhibition or innate immune stimulation to a PARP inhibitor improve control of BRCA1-deficient mouse mammary tumors, including tumors that have already acquired PARP inhibitor resistance, and can the spatial organisation of microRNA expression measured early in treatment, after 10 days, report which tumors are responding and which treatment arm they are in?
reading.background: Breast tumors carrying germline BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutations cannot repair DNA double-strand breaks by homologous recombination, which is why PARP inhibitors are approved for advanced BRCA1/2-related breast cancer: PARP inhibition stalls and collapses DNA replication forks, and a cell that also cannot do homologous recombination dies. The problem the paper starts from is that roughly 40 to 70 percent of patients either do not respond at all or progress on treatment, so the field needs both rational combination partners and early biomarkers of response. For combination partners the authors draw on two prior lines of their own work: PI3K inhibitors are active in breast tumors with and without PIK3CA mutations and PI3K enzymes also feed the DNA damage response, with PIK3CB specifically required for double-strand break sensing because it controls recruitment of NBN to damaged DNA, and separately the authors had reported that PARP inhibitor efficacy depends on the tumor immune microenvironment, with olaparib increasing CD8 positive T cell infiltration and activation and increasing tumor-associated macrophages. That second observation is what motivates poly(I:C), a synthetic double-stranded RNA mimic that activates dendritic cells through receptors including Toll-like receptor 3 and thereby activates CD8 T cells. For the biomarker side, microRNAs are short non-coding RNAs, roughly 20 nucleotides, that are already used as cancer detection markers, and the same group had previously shown that a seven-microRNA panel read out spatially in end-point mouse tumors, that is tumors collected after a full course of treatment, could distinguish PARP-inhibitor-sensitive from resistant tumors. The gap this paper fills is moving that spatial readout from end-point tumors to an early, 10-day timepoint, adding a treatment-arm comparison and acquired-resistance tumors, and connecting the microRNA patterns to where immune cells sit in the tissue.
reading.study_design: All work is in mice. Tumors arose in female K14-Cre Brca1 flox/flox Trp53 flox/flox mice; tumor fragments were then transplanted orthotopically into the mammary fat pad of female FVB/NJ recipients at least 6 weeks old, so every experiment is a syngeneic orthotopic transplant rather than an autochthonous tumor. Olaparib-resistant tumors were generated by growing initially sensitive tumors orthotopically under continuous olaparib until resistance emerged. Two experiment types were run. First, efficacy and survival: mice were randomised when tumors reached about 5 mm and treated until the longest tumor dimension reached 20 mm, which was the endpoint. Arms were olaparib alone (50 mg/kg intraperitoneally daily), alpelisib alone (24 mg/kg orally daily), olaparib plus alpelisib, olaparib plus poly(I:C) (1 mg/kg intratumorally three times weekly), and untreated control, run separately in sensitive and in resistant tumors; group sizes for the survival studies are not reported in the deposit. Second, the spatial study: mice were randomised at about 8 mm, treated for 10 days, and tumors were harvested, formalin fixed and paraffin embedded. That cohort was 21 tumors: 18 treated tumors made up of sensitive and resistant tumors each given olaparib alone, olaparib plus alpelisib, or olaparib plus poly(I:C), with n = 3 per group, plus 3 untreated olaparib-sensitive controls. Seven breast-cancer-associated microRNAs were measured in situ on sections from those tumors, giving 115,248 spatial measurements in total, and CD45 immunohistochemistry was done on the serial section cut immediately below each microRNA section so that immune maps and microRNA maps are spatially registered. The key comparisons are sensitive versus resistant, olaparib alone versus each combination within each sensitivity class, and microRNA topic maps versus immune infiltration maps.

key_methods.name: K14-Cre Brca1 flox/flox Trp53 flox/flox orthotopic transplant model with acquired olaparib resistance
key_methods.plain_explanation: A conditional knockout mouse in which the Brca1 and Trp53 genes are flanked by loxP sites and are deleted only in cells that express Cre recombinase from the Keratin 14 promoter. Those mice develop mammary tumors that are histologically triple negative. Rather than waiting for new tumors to arise in each mouse, the authors cut an existing tumor into fragments and transplanted them into the mammary fat pad of wild-type FVB/NJ mice of the same strain background, so many mice carry genetically identical tumors and the host immune system is intact. A resistant version of the same tumor was made by keeping transplanted tumors on olaparib continuously until they grew through it.
key_methods.how_used: Female FVB/NJ recipients at least 6 weeks old received orthotopic fragments. For survival studies mice were randomised at about 5 mm tumor diameter and treated to a 20 mm endpoint, with tumors calipered every 2 to 3 days and volume computed as length times width squared divided by two. Olaparib was 50 mg/kg intraperitoneally daily, alpelisib 24 mg/kg orally daily, poly(I:C) 1 mg/kg intratumorally three times per week. For the spatial study mice were randomised at about 8 mm and tumors were taken after 10 days of treatment. IACUC protocol 052-2020-23 at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center.
key_methods.why_it_matters: It gives a BRCA1-null, p53-null, immune-competent, syngeneic tumor in which sensitive and acquired-resistant versions of the same tumor can be compared head to head, which is what makes the sensitive-versus-resistant microRNA comparison interpretable. The caveats are that the Cre driver is Keratin 14, which is a basal and myoepithelial keratin rather than a luminal one, that transplantation bypasses the natural initiation and early progression of the tumor, and that only one tumor lineage is used, so tumor-to-tumor genetic diversity is absent.

key_methods.name: Spatially resolved in situ microRNA assay on a hydrogel nanoliter-well array
key_methods.plain_explanation: A way of reading how much of each of several microRNAs is present at each location across a tissue section, instead of grinding the whole piece of tissue up and getting one number per molecule. The device is a plate of nanoliter-sized wells, each well containing small hydrogel posts. Each post carries a DNA capture probe whose sequence is complementary to one target microRNA, and the same post position in every well targets the same microRNA. A tissue section is laid over the array, microRNAs released from the tissue bind their matching probes in the well underneath, and each captured microRNA is turned into a bright fluorescent signal by rolling circle amplification, which is an isothermal reaction in which a short circular DNA template is copied round and round to produce a long concatenated product carrying many copies of a sequence that labelled detection probes can bind. Reading the fluorescence of each post in each well therefore gives a seven-channel microRNA map of the section.
key_methods.how_used: Applied to formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded sections from the 21 day-10 tumors. Seven microRNAs commonly studied in breast cancer were quantified; the deposit names only miR-21-5p, let-7a-5p and miR-19a-3p, with the full panel in a supplementary table that is not in the deposit. Values were on the order of at most 3 to 4 attomoles per well. The resulting maps were masked by hand to the tissue outline so that only in-tissue wells contributed, and each tumor map was handled at a resolution of 28 by 28 positions.
key_methods.why_it_matters: It is the only part of the study that generates spatial microRNA data, and it is what lets the authors claim that information is carried by where microRNAs are rather than how much of them there is in total: the bulk version of exactly the same measurement was almost entirely uninformative. The caveats are that it is a targeted seven-plex, so it can only see microRNAs chosen in advance, the spatial grid is coarse, and the device is a custom academic platform rather than a commercial kit, with well dimensions and section thickness not stated in the deposit.

key_methods.name: Latent Dirichlet allocation topic modelling of the spatial microRNA maps
key_methods.plain_explanation: Latent Dirichlet allocation, usually shortened to LDA, is a statistical model borrowed from text analysis. It assumes every document is a mixture of a small number of hidden themes, called topics, and that each topic is a characteristic mixture of words. Given only the documents, it infers both the topics and each document's mixture of them. Here the words are the seven microRNAs and each small patch of tissue is a document, so LDA discovers a handful of recurring microRNA co-expression signatures and tells you, for every point in the tumor, which signature that point looks most like. The output is therefore a small set of interpretable microRNA mixtures plus a map of the tumor coloured by which mixture dominates where.
key_methods.how_used: A four-topic model was trained in MATLAB on all 10-day-treated tumors together, 115,248 spatial data points, using collapsed Gibbs sampling, with training taking about 21 minutes. Because LDA needs integer counts, microRNA values were multiplied by 10,000 and rounded. Hyperparameters follow the group's prior work and are not listed. Each spatial location was then assigned the topic with the highest weight there, giving topic maps, and the fraction of each tumor section assigned to each topic became that tumor's feature vector. Topic 2 came out dominated by miR-21 and topic 1 dominated by let-7a. A separate three-topic LDA was later trained on the structural similarity maps.
key_methods.why_it_matters: It compresses a seven-channel image per tumor into a handful of numbers that can be compared across tumors, while keeping the mixtures human-readable as word clouds. The caveat is that the number of topics, four here and three for the similarity analysis, was fixed rather than selected by a stated criterion, and the topics are descriptive rather than causal, so a topic is a recurring pattern and not a biological program that has been validated.

key_methods.name: Principal component analysis of per-tumor topic percentages
key_methods.plain_explanation: Principal component analysis takes a table of samples by measurements and finds new composite axes, the principal components, that are weighted combinations of the original measurements chosen so that the first axis captures as much of the variation between samples as possible, the second as much of what is left, and so on. It is a way of placing each sample at a point on a small number of summary axes so that groups can be seen at a glance.
key_methods.how_used: The input was each tumor's percentage of tissue assigned to each LDA topic, with topics as the variables. PC1 scores of treated tumors were compared between those classified as sensitive and those classified as resistant, n = 9 per group, with a two-sided Mann-Whitney U test at a significance threshold of p < 0.05.
key_methods.why_it_matters: It turns the topic composition of a whole tumor into a single number that can be tested statistically, and it reports which topics pull a tumor in which direction. The caveat is that PCA is unsupervised and PC1 explaining 96 percent of the variance with only four topic proportions as input, which are constrained to sum to 100 percent, means the axis is close to a single contrast between two dominant topics rather than a rich multivariate signature.

key_methods.name: Priming-based LDA for stratifying sensitive tumors by treatment arm
key_methods.plain_explanation: A deliberate reweighting of the input data to make a model pay attention to differences it otherwise misses. The authors first trained a second LDA model on the sensitive tumors alone, then for each microRNA took the single highest probability that microRNA reached in any topic of that sensitive-only model and used it as a multiplier. Every sensitive tumor's raw microRNA values were multiplied by the corresponding multiplier, which shrinks the microRNAs that the sensitive-only model considered unimportant more than those it considered important, and the reweighted data were then pushed back through the original all-tumor model and reanalysed exactly as before.
key_methods.how_used: Used only on olaparib-sensitive tumors treated with olaparib alone or with olaparib plus alpelisib or olaparib plus poly(I:C). The multipliers were 0.92 for let-7a and 0.88 for miR-21, with the other five microRNAs lower. Topic assignment, spatial visualisation and PCA were then run identically to the naive pipeline.
key_methods.why_it_matters: It recovered a separation of sensitive tumors by treatment arm that the naive analysis could not see, and it localises the signal: because the let-7a and miR-21 multipliers differ by only about 4 percent, the regions that flipped topic are those where let-7a and miR-21 were already nearly equal, so the treatment effect lives in locally balanced microregions rather than in a global shift. The important caveat, which the authors state themselves, is that the procedure uses prior knowledge that the tumors are sensitive, so it is not a standalone prognostic classifier and cannot be scored as one.

key_methods.name: CD45 immunohistochemistry with QuPath cell classification and immune-to-tumor ratio mapping
key_methods.plain_explanation: Immunohistochemistry stains a tissue section with an antibody against one protein and makes a coloured deposit wherever that protein is. CD45, also called PTPRC, is on essentially all white blood cells, so a CD45 stain marks tumor-infiltrating immune cells of every kind without distinguishing between them. QuPath is open-source digital pathology software that detects individual cells in a scanned slide image and classifies them. Dividing the number of immune cells by the number of tumor cells at each location gives a map of how heavily infiltrated each part of the tumor is.
key_methods.how_used: CD45 immunohistochemistry (rat anti-mouse CD45, clone 30-F11, 1:250, ThermoFisher 14-0451-82, with a goat anti-rat IgG HRP polymer secondary, Abcam ab214882) was performed on the serial section cut immediately below the section used for the microRNA assay, so the two are registered. QuPath classified cells on the haematoxylin and eosin image as tumor or stromal and counted CD45 positive cells on the immunohistochemistry image. A MATLAB script transferred tumor, stromal and immune counts onto the same grid positions as the microRNA wells using the section's overlay position on the device. The immune-to-tumor ratio at each position was then log transformed after adding a small constant, passed through a logistic transform so that 0.5 separates immune-poor from immune-rich, rescaled per tumor to span 0 to 1, clipped at the within-mask median, and rescaled to 0 to 1 again.
key_methods.why_it_matters: This is what connects the microRNA patterns to tissue architecture, and the serial-section design is what makes the registration credible. Two caveats matter. CD45 is pan-leukocyte, so nothing in this paper resolves T cells, NK cells, macrophages or any other subset. And the ratio map passes through log, logistic, rescaling, median clipping and a second rescaling, each defended as necessary to make it comparable to the near-binary topic maps, but together heavy enough that apparent structure could in part be a product of the transformation chain; the governing equations appear only as images in the deposit, so they could not be checked.

key_methods.name: Structural similarity index maps and LDA on those maps (LDA-SSIM)
key_methods.plain_explanation: The structural similarity index, SSIM, is a measure from image processing that compares two images not pixel by pixel but neighbourhood by neighbourhood, asking at every point whether the local brightness, the local contrast, and the local pattern of light and dark agree between the two images. It runs from minus one to one: close to one means the two images are locally organised the same way, zero means no detectable structural relationship, and close to minus one means the structures are inverted relative to each other. Because it is computed locally, you get a whole map of similarity rather than a single number.
key_methods.how_used: MATLAB's built-in SSIM function was applied with a neighbourhood of about 7 by 7 pixels on each 28 by 28 tumor map, comparing the normalised immune-to-tumor ratio map against each of the two dominant microRNA topic maps, the let-7a-dominated topic 1 and the miR-21-dominated topic 2. That produced two per-pixel similarity maps per tumor. A three-topic LDA was then trained on those similarity maps, with topics expressed as mixtures over the two similarity map types; topic 1 of that model came out dominated by the miR-21-to-immune similarity and topic 3 by the let-7a-to-immune similarity, and the composition of its topic 2 is not described in the deposit. Per-tumor percentages of these similarity topics were computed and plotted, with colour intensity showing similarity strength.
key_methods.why_it_matters: It is a general and reusable trick: any two spatially registered maps of the same tissue can be compared this way, and the output is itself a map, so it points to specific microregions rather than giving one correlation per tumor. The caveats are that a 7 by 7 window on a 28 by 28 grid is a very large fraction of the image, so the similarity maps are heavily smoothed; no correlation coefficients, similarity values or p-values are reported for the similarity analysis; and structural similarity is a descriptive image statistic with no mechanistic content.

key_concepts.plain_definition: BRCA1 is a protein that cells need in order to repair a double-strand break in DNA by homologous recombination, which is the accurate repair route that copies the missing sequence from an intact matching chromosome. When both copies of BRCA1 are lost, that route is unavailable and the cell has to fall back on error-prone alternatives, so it accumulates damage and chromosomal rearrangements. In this paper BRCA1 is deleted, together with Trp53, in the mouse mammary epithelium, and that deficiency is the entire reason the tumors are sensitive to PARP inhibition in the first place.

PARP enzymes help repair single-strand DNA damage and help stabilise DNA replication forks. A PARP inhibitor such as olaparib blocks that activity, so replication forks stall and collapse into double-strand breaks. A normal cell repairs those breaks by homologous recombination and survives, but a BRCA1-deficient cell cannot, and dies. Neither defect alone is lethal while the combination is, which is what synthetic lethality means, and it is why PARP inhibitors are approved specifically for BRCA1/2-mutant cancers. In this paper olaparib is the backbone of every treatment arm.

Tumors that shrink on a PARP inhibitor at first and then regrow while still on the drug have acquired resistance. Clinically this happens to a large fraction of patients: the paper cites roughly 40 to 70 percent who either never respond or stop responding. In this study resistance is not a hypothesis about a mechanism but an operational, experimentally produced state: sensitive tumors were kept on continuous olaparib until they grew through it, and those tumors are then compared with their sensitive counterparts. The paper does not test or report which molecular mechanism made them resistant.

A microRNA is a very short RNA, around 20 nucleotides, that is not translated into protein. Instead it pairs with partially matching sequences in messenger RNAs and causes them to be degraded or blocked from being translated, so one microRNA can damp down tens or hundreds of protein-coding genes at once. Because microRNAs are stable, are easy to detect, and shift characteristically in tumors, they have been pursued as cancer biomarkers. This paper treats them purely as a readout rather than manipulating them, and measures seven of them.

These are the two microRNAs that carry essentially the whole result. miR-21 is a well-established oncogenic microRNA, meaning that higher levels of it tend to promote tumor growth and survival, and let-7a is a well-established tumor-suppressive microRNA, meaning that higher levels of it tend to restrain proliferation; the paper cites both of those characterisations in its Results. In this study a miR-21-dominated spatial pattern tracks with PARP inhibitor sensitivity and with combination treatment, and a let-7a-dominated spatial pattern tracks with resistance and with olaparib alone. Note that the directions of those associations are not what the oncogene and tumor suppressor labels would naively predict, and the paper does not attempt to resolve that.

Spatial profiling means measuring molecules while keeping track of where in the intact tissue each measurement came from, rather than homogenising a tissue sample and getting one average value per molecule, which is what bulk profiling does. The point is that tumors are not uniform: a region packed with immune cells, a region of dividing tumor cells and a dying region can all sit within one millimetre of each other, and their signals cancel out in a bulk average. Here the comparison is made directly: the same seven microRNAs read as bulk per-tumor values gave almost nothing, while the same values read as maps separated the treatment groups.

A topic model is a statistical method, developed for analysing collections of text, that assumes a small number of hidden themes underlie the data. Each theme, or topic, is a characteristic mixture of the observed items, and each observation is a mixture of themes. Given only the raw observations the method works out both at once, with no labels supplied. Latent Dirichlet allocation is the standard version. Applied to tissue, each small patch of tumor plays the role of a document and each microRNA plays the role of a word, so the model discovers a handful of recurring microRNA co-expression signatures and reports how much of each tumor is covered by each signature. The appeal is that the signatures stay readable, as mixtures you can print as a word cloud, instead of being opaque features.

A measure of how similarly two images are organised, taken from image quality assessment. Instead of subtracting one image from the other pixel by pixel, it slides a small window across both and at each position compares the average brightness, the amount of local variation, and whether the light and dark areas line up. The result for each position runs from minus one, meaning the two patterns are inverted relative to each other, through zero, meaning no relationship, to one, meaning the local structures match. In this paper it is used to ask, region by region, whether immune infiltration is arranged like the let-7a microRNA pattern or like the miR-21 pattern.

Poly(I:C), polyinosinic-polycytidylic acid, is a synthetic double-stranded RNA. Because long double-stranded RNA is a signature of viral infection, cells have receptors for it, including Toll-like receptor 3, and engaging those receptors sets off an innate antiviral alarm that matures dendritic cells, which in turn prime and activate CD8 T cells. In this paper poly(I:C) is used purely as an immune-stimulating combination partner for olaparib, injected directly into the tumor at 1 mg/kg three times per week. It is worth being clear that this is RNA sensing, a different sensor arm from cytosolic DNA sensing, and the paper does not measure any downstream innate signalling.

key_concepts.term: PI3K inhibition with alpelisib, and the PI3K link to DNA repair
key_concepts.plain_definition: The PI3K pathway is a central growth and survival signalling route that is frequently hyperactive in breast cancer, often through mutation of PIK3CA. Alpelisib is a PI3K inhibitor already used clinically in breast cancer. The reason it is a rational PARP inhibitor partner here is not only growth suppression: the paper notes that PI3K enzymes also participate in the DNA damage response, with PIK3CB specifically required for sensing double-strand breaks because it controls recruitment of NBN, part of the MRE11-RAD50-NBN complex that detects breaks, to damaged DNA. So blocking PI3K can blunt break sensing and deepen the repair defect that the PARP inhibitor exploits.

figures.label: Fig 1
figures.title: Combination therapy extends time to endpoint in olaparib-sensitive and olaparib-resistant BRCA1-null mouse tumors
figures.question: Does adding alpelisib or poly(I:C) to olaparib slow tumor growth, and does the benefit survive in tumors that have already acquired olaparib resistance?
figures.how_to_read: Panel A is the experimental schematic: syngeneic olaparib-sensitive or olaparib-resistant tumors implanted into FVB/NJ mice, treatment started once the tumor reached 5 mm diameter, arms being olaparib alone or olaparib plus alpelisib or olaparib plus poly(I:C). Panel B is four Kaplan-Meier style curves of the time taken for tumors to reach the 20 mm endpoint, so a curve further to the right is better. B.i is sensitive tumors given olaparib, alpelisib, or both; B.ii is sensitive tumors given olaparib with or without poly(I:C); B.iii is resistant tumors given olaparib with or without alpelisib; B.iv is resistant tumors given olaparib with or without poly(I:C). Asterisks mark p < 0.05, p < 0.01 and p < 0.001.
figures.key_result: In sensitive tumors olaparib alone extended median time to 20 mm to 75 to 78 days versus 19 to 23 days for control (p < 0.001), adding alpelisib extended it further to 115 days versus 75 days (p < 0.001), and adding poly(I:C) to 120 days versus 78 days (p < 0.001), which the authors present as the first demonstration that poly(I:C) enhances PARP inhibition, with a benefit comparable to alpelisib. In resistant tumors olaparib gave only 23 to 24 days versus 17 days for control (p = 0.003); adding alpelisib extended this to 39 days versus 23 days (p = 0.018), while adding poly(I:C) gave 30 days versus 24 days and was not significant (p = 0.567). Group sizes for these survival curves are not reported in the deposit.

figures.label: Fig 2
figures.title: Spatial microRNA topics separate olaparib-sensitive from olaparib-resistant tumors after 10 days of treatment
figures.question: After only 10 days of treatment, do spatial microRNA patterns distinguish sensitive from resistant tumors, and do they distinguish olaparib alone from the combinations, in a way that bulk microRNA levels do not?
figures.how_to_read: Panel A schematises the hydrogel nanoliter-well in situ microRNA assay. Panel B shows one representative seven-plex spatial microRNA output, with all samples relegated to Supplementary Figure S2. Panel C is the analysis. C.i gives the LDA topics as word clouds, where font size is each microRNA's relative weight within the topic and orange marks the microRNAs weighted most heavily. C.ii maps the topic assignment across a tumor section, with well colour matching the topic border colour in C.i. C.iii is a stacked bar chart of what percentage of each tissue section fell into each topic, with sample labels starting R for known resistant or S for known sensitive and then O for olaparib only, OA for olaparib plus alpelisib, or OP for olaparib plus poly(I:C). C.iv is the PCA of those topic percentages, with green points known-sensitive tumors, red points known-resistant tumors, and controls labelled in black text.
figures.key_result: Of the seven microRNAs, miR-21-5p, let-7a-5p and miR-19a-3p were the most abundant. In bulk analysis the only difference found was lower let-7a in olaparib plus poly(I:C) tumors compared with olaparib alone, in both sensitive and resistant tumors (both adjusted p = 0.01); the other six microRNAs differed neither by treatment nor by sensitivity status. Spatially, with a four-topic LDA trained on 115,248 data points, topic 2 was dominated by miR-21 and tracked with sensitivity while topic 1 was dominated by let-7a and tracked with resistance. Tumors separated almost entirely along PC1, which explained 96 percent of the variance, with topic 2 loading positively and topic 1 negatively; median PC1 was 0.42 for sensitive and -0.083 for resistant tumors (Mann-Whitney U, p < 0.001, n = 9 per group). Among resistant tumors the olaparib-only group separated from the two combination groups more clearly than the survival curves in Fig 1B did, with the combinations shifting resistant profiles toward the sensitive profile. Among sensitive tumors this naive analysis showed little separation by treatment arm despite the roughly three-fold survival benefit.

figures.label: Fig 3
figures.title: Priming-based LDA separates olaparib-only from combination-treated sensitive tumors in locally balanced let-7a and miR-21 regions
figures.question: Can a reweighted analysis recover the treatment-arm difference among olaparib-sensitive tumors that the naive spatial analysis missed, and where in the tissue does that difference live?
figures.how_to_read: Panel A contrasts the two pipelines: A.i is the naive route, one model trained on all data then visualisation then PCA, and A.ii is the primed route, where the input is first multiplied by microRNA weights learned from an LDA trained on sensitive tumors only, then pushed through the same naive model and analysed identically. Panel B shows the results. B.i displays the topics from the naive model alongside those from the sensitive-only model. B.ii is the spatial map of sensitive tumors after priming, still coloured by naive topic assignment to match the borders in B.i. B.iii is the percentage of each section assigned to each topic. B.iv is the PCA of those percentages, with green marking combination-treated tumors and red marking olaparib-only tumors; here topic 1 loads positively on PC1 and topic 2 negatively.
figures.key_result: Sensitive tumors stratified almost entirely along PC1, with the let-7a-dominated topic 1 more prevalent in olaparib-only tumors and the miR-21-dominated topic 2 more prevalent in combination-treated tumors. Let-7a and miR-21 carried the highest probabilities in both the naive and the sensitive-only models, with top weights of 0.92 for let-7a and 0.88 for miR-21 in the specialised model. Because priming shrinks heavily weighted microRNAs least, and because the let-7a and miR-21 weights differ by only about 4 percent, the regions that switched from topic 2 to topic 1 in olaparib-only samples are precisely those where let-7a and miR-21 levels were already nearly equal, so the treatment separation rests on locally balanced microregions rather than on any global shift. The authors state explicitly that because this pipeline uses prior knowledge that the tumors are sensitive, it is not a standalone prognostic classifier.

figures.label: Fig 4
figures.title: Immune infiltration is spatially organised like the let-7a topic in most tumors but like the miR-21 topic in sensitive poly(I:C)-treated tumors
figures.question: Do the microRNA topic maps line up spatially with where immune cells infiltrate the tumor, and does that alignment differ by treatment arm?
figures.how_to_read: Panel A is the pipeline schematic: A.i the two inputs, spatial microRNA data and spatial cell counts from staining; A.ii the processing, where microRNA data go through the naive LDA pipeline of Fig 2 to give spatial topic allocations while cell counts are converted into a normalised immune-to-tumor ratio; A.iii the output, a heatmap of SSIM maps giving the structural similarity between immune infiltration and the microRNA topic assignments. Panel B shows the results of an LDA trained on those similarity maps. B.i gives that model's topics, built from the two similarity map types, with its topic 1 dominated by the miR-21-to-immune similarity and its topic 3 by the let-7a-to-immune similarity. B.ii is the percentage of each section assigned to each similarity topic. B.iii and B.iv are the spatial maps of similarity topic assignment in resistant and in sensitive samples respectively, with border colour matching B.i and colour intensity showing how strong the dominant similarity is.
figures.key_result: In most tumors, regardless of sensitive or resistant status, immune infiltration was structurally more similar to the let-7a-dominated topic than to the miR-21-dominated topic. The exception was olaparib plus poly(I:C)-treated sensitive tumors, where similarity to the miR-21 topic was greater. Within poly(I:C)-treated tumors, miR-21 similarity was notably higher in sensitive than in resistant tumors even though the treatment was identical and overall immune cell counts were not substantially different. In those sensitive poly(I:C) tumors the strongest miR-21 similarity clustered where miR-21 regions bordered let-7a-associated immune regions. No similarity values, correlation coefficients or p-values are reported for this analysis, and the immune readout is pan-CD45 only.

key_findings.statement: In olaparib-sensitive BRCA1-null, Trp53-null mouse mammary tumors, adding either alpelisib or poly(I:C) to olaparib substantially extends time to the 20 mm endpoint, and the poly(I:C) combination is reported here for the first time.
key_findings.evidence: Fig 1B.i and Fig 1B.ii plus Supplementary Figure S1: olaparib plus alpelisib 115 days versus olaparib alone 75 days (p < 0.001); olaparib plus poly(I:C) 120 days versus olaparib alone 78 days (p < 0.001); olaparib alone 75 to 78 days versus control 19 to 23 days (p < 0.001).

key_findings.statement: In tumors with acquired olaparib resistance, adding alpelisib gives a modest but significant extension while adding poly(I:C) does not, so the immune-agonist combination loses its benefit once resistance has emerged.
key_findings.evidence: Fig 1B.iii and Fig 1B.iv: olaparib plus alpelisib 39 days versus olaparib alone 23 days (p = 0.018); olaparib plus poly(I:C) 30 days versus olaparib alone 24 days (p = 0.567). Olaparib alone in resistant tumors 23 to 24 days versus control 17 days (p = 0.003). Survival group sizes are not reported in the deposit.

key_findings.statement: Read as bulk per-tumor values, the seven-microRNA panel is almost entirely uninformative: only let-7a changes, being lower in poly(I:C)-treated tumors, while the other six microRNAs distinguish neither treatment arm nor sensitivity status.
key_findings.evidence: Bulk comparisons within Fig 2 and supplementary data, two-way ANOVA with Sidak correction: lower let-7a in olaparib plus poly(I:C) versus olaparib alone in both sensitive and resistant tumors, both adjusted p = 0.01; no other differences.

key_findings.statement: Spatial microRNA topics taken at 10 days of treatment separate olaparib-sensitive from olaparib-resistant tumors, with a miR-21-dominated pattern marking sensitivity and a let-7a-dominated pattern marking resistance.
key_findings.evidence: Fig 2C.i to C.iv: four-topic LDA on 115,248 spatial data points, topic 2 miR-21-dominated and topic 1 let-7a-dominated; PCA of topic percentages separates along PC1 which carries 96 percent of variance, median PC1 0.42 sensitive versus -0.083 resistant, Mann-Whitney U p < 0.001, n = 9 per group.

key_findings.statement: Within resistant tumors, the spatial microRNA readout separates olaparib alone from the two combination arms more clearly than the survival curves do, and both combinations shift resistant tumors' spatial profiles toward the sensitive profile.
key_findings.evidence: Fig 2C.iii and Fig 2C.iv compared against the resistant-tumor curves in Fig 1B.iii and 1B.iv, which show only a modest alpelisib effect and no significant poly(I:C) effect.

key_findings.statement: Among sensitive tumors, treatment arm is not visible to the naive analysis but is recovered by priming-based LDA, and the signal lives in microregions where let-7a and miR-21 levels are nearly balanced: the let-7a topic is more prevalent in olaparib-only tumors and the miR-21 topic in combination-treated tumors.
key_findings.evidence: Fig 3B.ii to B.iv, with top priming weights of 0.92 for let-7a and 0.88 for miR-21, about 4 percent apart, so only near-balanced regions flip topic. The authors state this pipeline uses the sensitivity label and so is not a standalone classifier.

key_findings.statement: Immune infiltration is spatially organised like the let-7a topic in most tumors, but like the miR-21 topic in sensitive tumors given olaparib plus poly(I:C), a difference that is spatial rather than quantitative because total immune cell counts were not substantially different.
key_findings.evidence: Fig 4B.i to B.iv: SSIM maps of the normalised CD45-to-tumor-cell ratio against the let-7a and miR-21 topic maps, summarised by a three-topic LDA; strongest miR-21 similarity clusters at borders between miR-21 regions and let-7a-associated immune regions. No similarity values or p-values are reported.

limitations: The spatial cohort is very small: 21 tumors in total, n = 3 per sensitivity-by-treatment group, plus 3 untreated controls, so every spatial comparison rests on three tumors per arm.
Group sizes for the survival and efficacy studies are not reported anywhere in the version available, so the Kaplan-Meier comparisons in Fig 1 cannot be weighed properly.

Everything comes from one tumor lineage in one genotype, propagated as orthotopic fragment transplants, so there is no tumor-to-tumor genetic diversity and no autochthonous tumor initiation; the resistant tumors are the matched descendants of the sensitive ones rather than independent resistant tumors.

The mechanism of acquired olaparib resistance in these tumors is never determined or reported, so the sensitive-versus-resistant microRNA contrast is anchored to an operational growth phenotype rather than to a defined resistance mechanism.

The immune readout is pan-CD45 immunohistochemistry only. No immune subset is resolved: no CD8 or CD4 T cells, no NK cells, no macrophages, no dendritic cells, and no functional or activation markers.

No mechanism is offered or tested for why immune localisation should align with a let-7a or a miR-21 pattern; the structural similarity analysis is descriptive and reports no similarity values, correlation coefficients or p-values.

The microRNA panel is a targeted seven-plex chosen in advance from breast-cancer literature, so the analysis cannot discover an unanticipated microRNA, and only three of the seven are even named in the available version.

The direction of the associations sits awkwardly with the cited biology: miR-21 is described as an oncogene and let-7a as a tumor suppressor, yet the miR-21 pattern marks sensitivity and response while the let-7a pattern marks resistance, and this tension is not addressed.

No formal classifier is built and no performance metric is reported: there is no accuracy, no area under the curve, no cross-validation and no held-out test set. The authors themselves state that the prognostic separations would need to become formal predictive models with explicit performance metrics.

The priming-based LDA used for the sensitive-tumor stratification takes the sensitivity label as input, which the authors acknowledge means it cannot function as a prognostic classifier; as presented it is circular for prediction purposes.

Model selection is not justified: the four-topic microRNA LDA and the three-topic similarity LDA are fixed numbers with no stated selection criterion, and the LDA hyperparameters are inherited from prior work without being listed.
The spatial resolution is coarse. Tumor maps are 28 by 28 positions and SSIM uses a roughly 7 by 7 neighbourhood, so each similarity value is smoothed over a large fraction of the section.

The immune-to-tumor ratio map is pushed through log transformation, a logistic transform, per-tumor rescaling, clipping at the median and a second rescaling in order to make it comparable with the near-binary topic maps, which is a heavy enough chain that some apparent structure could be an artefact of processing; the governing equations appear only as images in the deposit and could not be inspected.
The in situ microRNA assay is a custom academic device, and key specifications including well size, well count and section thickness are not given, which makes independent replication hard.
Poly(I:C) is delivered intratumorally three times per week, which limits direct translation to systemic therapy.

There is no data availability statement and no code availability statement, and no repository, accession number or software link is provided, so none of the spatial data or the analysis code can be obtained for reanalysis.
open_questions: Does the day-10 spatial microRNA signature actually predict outcome prospectively, in tumors whose sensitivity status is not already known, with a locked classifier and a reported accuracy or area under the curve?

Why do the association directions run opposite to the cited biology, with the oncogenic miR-21 pattern marking sensitivity and response and the tumor-suppressive let-7a pattern marking resistance? Is this a change in microRNA biology, a change in which cells occupy those regions, or something about the assay?

Which cells carry the let-7a and miR-21 signals? Because the assay reads a tissue patch, not a cell, it is unresolved whether the patterns reflect tumor cells, stroma, or the infiltrating immune cells themselves, which matters a great deal for how the immune co-localisation should be read.

What immune cell types make up the CD45 positive infiltrate in each pattern, and does the let-7a-aligned infiltrate differ functionally from the miR-21-aligned infiltrate in poly(I:C)-treated sensitive tumors?
What made these tumors olaparib resistant, and does the spatial microRNA pattern track the resistance mechanism or only the growth phenotype?
Is let-7a or miR-21 doing anything causal here, or are both purely correlative markers? No gain or loss of function experiment is attempted.
Why does poly(I:C) help sensitive tumors but not resistant ones, when both received the same immune agonist and neither showed a large difference in total immune cell number?
Does the SSIM plus topic model approach reproduce on higher-resolution spatial platforms and on human tissue, where the registration and resolution problems differ?
reading.relevance_to_lab: This paper sits squarely in the lab's disease space, BRCA1-deficient ER-negative, triple-negative breast cancer in mouse models, and it touches the lab's PARP inhibitor and immune interests, but it does not test the lab's mechanistic chain, and the mouse model it uses speaks to the opposite side of the cell-of-origin debate from the lab's own position. On cell of origin: the driver is K14-Cre, and Keratin 14 is a basal and myoepithelial keratin, so Brca1 and Trp53 are deleted in the basal and myoepithelial compartment of the mammary epithelium, not in the ER-negative luminal progenitors that the lab and others have argued are the actual cell of origin of human BRCA1-associated breast cancer. It is worth being explicit that the paper itself never discusses this: the words cell of origin, basal, luminal and progenitor appear nowhere in the text, and K14 appears only inside the genotype name, so the basal-compartment reading is background knowledge the lab should bring to the paper rather than anything the authors claim. The practical consequence is that these tumors are a pharmacology and biomarker platform for BRCA1-null, p53-null mammary tumors rather than a model of the initiating cell, and any microRNA pattern found in them should not be assumed to transfer to a luminal-progenitor-derived tumor without testing. The transplant design compounds this: tumor fragments are passaged orthotopically into wild-type FVB/NJ hosts, so initiation and early progression are bypassed entirely. On immune evasion: against the lab's model of BRCA1 loss, then cytosolic DNA, then cGAS-STING, then NF-kB and IRF3, then type I interferon, then MHC class I including HLA-C and HLA-E with NKG2A, then suppressed NK and CD8 T cell surveillance, this paper tests essentially none of the intermediate steps. There is no mention anywhere in the text of cGAS, STING, interferon, type I IFN, NK cells, natural killer cells, MHC or HLA. The only immune measurement in the paper is pan-CD45 immunohistochemistry, which counts leukocytes without distinguishing a single subset, so the paper cannot speak to NK or CD8 surveillance even descriptively. CD8 T cells, dendritic cells, Toll-like receptor 3 and tumor-associated macrophages appear only in the Introduction, as cited background from the authors' own earlier work that olaparib raises CD8 infiltration and activation and raises tumor-associated macrophages. The one point of real mechanistic adjacency is poly(I:C), which is a double-stranded RNA mimic and therefore engages the RNA sensing arm of innate immunity, Toll-like receptor 3 and by extension the cytosolic RNA sensors, rather than the cytosolic DNA sensing arm through cGAS-STING. That makes it a useful conceptual counterpart to a STING agonist: if the lab believes BRCA1 loss generates cytosolic DNA and that tumors then suppress the downstream interferon and antigen presentation response, then the finding that an RNA-sensing agonist combined with olaparib helps sensitive tumors but fails in acquired-resistant tumors, with p = 0.567, is a result worth knowing, because it suggests that whatever makes these tumors olaparib resistant also blunts the benefit of innate immune stimulation. The paper offers no explanation, and testing whether the cGAS-STING to interferon to MHC class I axis is what differs between those sensitive and resistant tumors is an obvious experiment the lab is better placed to do than these authors. What can be borrowed: the analysis layer is portable and the assay layer is not. The topic model plus PCA framing, and especially the structural similarity index approach, which asks region by region whether two registered maps of the same tissue are arranged the same way rather than reducing each tumor to one correlation, can be applied immediately to the lab's own data. The lab could run exactly this on registered pairs of maps from its BRCA1 mouse tumors or human samples, for example an MHC class I or HLA-E immunofluorescence map against an NK or CD8 density map, or a STING pathway or interferon-stimulated gene score from spatial transcriptomics against an immune density map, at considerably better resolution than the 28 by 28 grid used here. All of it runs on MATLAB built-ins and standard LDA, so there is nothing proprietary. The microRNA assay itself is a different matter: it is a custom hydrogel nanoliter-well array with rolling circle amplification readout from the Doyle lab, well dimensions and section thickness are not specified, and it is a targeted seven-plex, so adopting it would mean a collaboration rather than buying a kit. Finally, and importantly for reuse: there is no data availability statement and no code availability statement in the version available, no repository, no accession and no software link, so none of the spatial microRNA data, the immune maps or the analysis code can be pulled for independent reanalysis. If the lab wants the data, someone has to write to the authors.
discussion_questions: The driver here is K14-Cre, which deletes Brca1 and Trp53 in the basal and myoepithelial compartment, while our working model puts the origin of BRCA1-associated breast cancer in ER-negative luminal progenitors. How much should that change how we read a biomarker result from these tumors, and would we expect the miR-21 versus let-7a spatial contrast to survive in a luminal-progenitor-driven model such as a Krt8 or Lgr5 or Prom1-based Brca1 deletion?

Poly(I:C) plus olaparib works in sensitive tumors but fails outright in acquired-resistant tumors (p = 0.567) while alpelisib still helps (p = 0.018). If our model is right that BRCA1 loss drives cytosolic DNA sensing and that tumors then suppress the interferon and MHC class I output, is the simplest explanation that acquired olaparib resistance also shuts down innate immune responsiveness downstream of the sensor? What would we measure in these tumors to test that: interferon-stimulated gene score, STING and IRF3 phosphorylation, MHC class I and HLA-E surface levels, or NK and CD8 infiltration?

The entire immune readout in this paper is pan-CD45. If we repeated the structural similarity analysis on our own sections with a real panel, NK cells, CD8 T cells, macrophages, plus MHC class I and HLA-E, which pairing would we compare first, and would we expect the let-7a-aligned and miR-21-aligned regions to differ by subset composition rather than by total immune number, which is what this paper actually found?

The paper's own key caveat is that the sensitive-tumor stratification comes from a priming step that uses the sensitivity label, and that the top let-7a and miR-21 weights differ by only about 4 percent, so the separation rests on microregions where the two microRNAs are nearly equal. Is that a genuine biological signal localised to transition zones, or is it a model artefact from reweighting a four-topic model on three tumors per arm? What would convince us either way?

Independent of the microRNA biology, is the SSIM plus topic model pipeline worth adopting for our own spatial work? It only needs two registered maps of the same tissue and MATLAB built-ins, and it returns a map that points at specific microregions instead of one correlation per sample. What would we run it on first, and at what resolution, given that 28 by 28 with a 7 by 7 window is far coarser than what Visium or Xenium would give us?

nodes.label: Can early spatial microRNA patterns report PARP inhibitor response?
nodes.detail: Can combination partners improve PARP inhibitor efficacy in BRCA1-deficient tumors, including acquired-resistant ones, and can a spatial microRNA readout at day 10 tell which tumors are responding?

nodes.label: BRCA1 loss blocks homologous recombination, so PARP inhibitors work but often fail
nodes.detail: PARP inhibitors are approved for advanced BRCA1/2-related breast cancer because stalled replication forks become lethal without homologous recombination, yet roughly 40 to 70 percent of patients do not respond or acquire resistance.

nodes.label: A seven-microRNA spatial profile separated sensitive from resistant end-point tumors
nodes.detail: The authors had previously shown that spatial profiles of a seven-microRNA panel in mouse tumors collected after a full course of treatment distinguish PARP-inhibitor-sensitive from resistant tumors.

nodes.label: PARP inhibitor efficacy depends on the tumor immune microenvironment
nodes.detail: The authors had reported that olaparib increases CD8 positive T cell infiltration and activation and increases tumor-associated macrophages, which motivates pairing olaparib with an innate immune agonist.

nodes.label: PI3K inhibition or innate immune stimulation will add to olaparib, and spatial microRNA maps will report it early
nodes.detail: Alpelisib is rational because PI3K also feeds the DNA damage response, with PIK3CB required for double-strand break sensing through NBN recruitment; poly(I:C) is rational because it activates dendritic cells and thereby CD8 T cells. Spatial rather than bulk microRNA readout should carry the response information.

nodes.label: Treat sensitive and acquired-resistant K14-Cre Brca1/Trp53 tumors to a 20 mm endpoint
nodes.detail: Orthotopic syngeneic transplants in FVB/NJ hosts, randomised at 5 mm, given olaparib alone, alpelisib alone, olaparib plus alpelisib, or olaparib plus poly(I:C), with resistant tumors generated by continuous olaparib exposure.

nodes.label: Both combinations roughly double time to endpoint in sensitive tumors
nodes.detail: Olaparib plus alpelisib 115 versus 75 days and olaparib plus poly(I:C) 120 versus 78 days, both p < 0.001; the poly(I:C) combination is reported here for the first time.

nodes.label: In resistant tumors alpelisib still helps modestly but poly(I:C) does not
nodes.detail: Olaparib plus alpelisib 39 versus 23 days (p = 0.018), olaparib plus poly(I:C) 30 versus 24 days (p = 0.567), so the immune agonist loses its benefit once resistance has emerged.

nodes.label: Profile seven microRNAs in situ on day-10 tumors, 21 tumors total
nodes.detail: A hydrogel nanoliter-well array with rolling circle amplification readout measured seven breast-cancer microRNAs across sections of 18 treated tumors, n = 3 per sensitivity-by-treatment group, plus 3 untreated controls, chosen at 10 days so remodelling has occurred but necrosis has not.

nodes.label: Bulk microRNA levels are almost uninformative; only let-7a moves
nodes.detail: Let-7a was lower in olaparib plus poly(I:C) tumors than in olaparib alone in both sensitive and resistant tumors, both adjusted p = 0.01, while the other six microRNAs distinguished neither treatment nor sensitivity status.

nodes.label: Spatial topics separate sensitive from resistant: miR-21 topic sensitive, let-7a topic resistant
nodes.detail: A four-topic LDA on 115,248 spatial points gave a miR-21-dominated topic 2 and a let-7a-dominated topic 1; PCA of topic percentages separated tumors along PC1, which carried 96 percent of the variance, median 0.42 versus -0.083, Mann-Whitney U p < 0.001, n = 9 per group.

nodes.label: Combinations shift resistant tumors toward the sensitive spatial profile
nodes.detail: Among resistant tumors the olaparib-only group separated from the two combination groups more clearly in the spatial readout than in the survival curves, but among sensitive tumors the naive analysis saw no treatment separation despite a roughly three-fold survival benefit.

nodes.label: Priming-based LDA recovers treatment arm in sensitive tumors, in near-balanced regions
nodes.detail: Reweighting the input by microRNA probabilities learned from a sensitive-only model made the let-7a topic more prevalent in olaparib-only tumors and the miR-21 topic more prevalent in combination tumors; because the top weights differ by only about 4 percent, only regions where let-7a and miR-21 were already nearly equal switched topic. The authors note this uses the sensitivity label and so is not a standalone classifier.

nodes.label: Immune infiltration is arranged like the let-7a topic, except in sensitive poly(I:C) tumors
nodes.detail: Structural similarity maps between the CD45-to-tumor ratio and each topic map, summarised by a three-topic LDA, showed let-7a-aligned immune structure in most tumors but miR-21-aligned structure in sensitive olaparib plus poly(I:C) tumors, concentrated where miR-21 regions bordered let-7a-associated immune regions, with total immune counts not substantially different.

nodes.label: Early spatial microRNA organisation carries response information absent from bulk levels and survival
nodes.detail: Where a tumor's microRNAs sit, read after only 10 days, separates sensitivity status and treatment arm and aligns with immune localisation, while the same microRNAs averaged over the tumor do not, so the information is in the spatial pattern rather than the amount.

nodes.label: Proof of concept only: needs formal classifiers, larger cohorts and clinical samples
nodes.detail: The authors frame the work as a proof-of-concept framework whose topics and stratifications must be tested in larger preclinical studies and in clinical BRCA1/2-mutant breast cancer, turned into predictive models with explicit performance metrics, and extended to other spatially resolved readouts such as cell markers and mRNA.

entities.name: BRCA1
entities.description: Homologous recombination repair gene; deleted together with Trp53 in the mouse mammary tumors studied here, and the reason those tumors respond to PARP inhibition.

entities.name: TP53
entities.description: Tumor suppressor; its mouse orthologue Trp53 is conditionally deleted alongside Brca1 in the tumor model used throughout the paper.

entities.name: Homologous recombination repair
entities.description: The accurate route for repairing DNA double-strand breaks, which is unavailable in these BRCA1-null tumors and is the basis of their PARP inhibitor sensitivity.

entities.name: PARP1
entities.description: DNA damage repair enzyme and the target of olaparib; inhibiting it stalls and collapses replication forks.

entities.name: Olaparib
entities.description: PARP inhibitor used as the backbone of every treatment arm, 50 mg/kg intraperitoneally daily, and also used continuously to generate the resistant tumors.

entities.name: Alpelisib
entities.description: PI3K inhibitor combined with olaparib, 24 mg/kg orally daily; the combination partner that retained benefit in acquired-resistant tumors.

entities.name: Poly(I:C)
entities.description: Synthetic double-stranded RNA innate immune agonist given intratumorally at 1 mg/kg three times weekly; helped in sensitive tumors but not in resistant ones.

entities.name: PI3K signaling
entities.description: Growth and survival pathway inhibited by alpelisib, which the paper notes also contributes to the DNA damage response.

entities.name: PIK3CB
entities.description: PI3K catalytic subunit cited as required for double-strand break sensing because it controls recruitment of NBN to damaged DNA, which is the mechanistic rationale for combining a PI3K inhibitor with a PARP inhibitor.

entities.name: NBN
entities.description: Nibrin, part of the double-strand break sensing complex; its recruitment to damaged DNA is said to depend on PIK3CB.

entities.name: PIK3CA
entities.description: Most commonly mutated PI3K subunit in breast cancer, cited as background for why PI3K inhibitors are used, including in tumors with wild-type PIK3CA.

entities.name: TLR3
entities.description: Toll-like receptor 3, a double-stranded RNA sensor named in the Introduction as a receptor through which poly(I:C) activates dendritic cells.

entities.name: Dendritic cell
entities.description: Antigen-presenting cell activated by poly(I:C) through receptors including Toll-like receptor 3, cited as the route to CD8 T cell activation; not measured in this paper.

entities.name: CD8-positive T cell
entities.description: Cytotoxic T cell reported in the authors' earlier work to be increased in infiltration and activation by olaparib; cited as background only and not measured here.

entities.name: Tumor-associated macrophage
entities.description: Myeloid cell population reported in the authors' earlier work to be increased by olaparib; cited as background only and not measured here.

entities.name: Tumor-infiltrating immune cells
entities.description: The pan-CD45-positive leukocyte population mapped spatially in this paper, with no subset resolution; its spatial arrangement is compared with the microRNA topic maps.

entities.name: PTPRC
entities.description: Encodes CD45, the pan-leukocyte marker used by immunohistochemistry to identify tumor-infiltrating immune cells on the serial section below each microRNA section.

entities.name: MIR21
entities.description: Encodes miR-21-5p, one of the three most abundant microRNAs in these tumors and the dominant microRNA of the spatial topic that tracks with olaparib sensitivity and combination treatment; cited in the paper as an oncogenic microRNA.

entities.name: MIRLET7A1
entities.description: Encodes let-7a-5p, one of the three most abundant microRNAs here and the dominant microRNA of the spatial topic that tracks with olaparib resistance and olaparib monotherapy; cited in the paper as a tumor-suppressive microRNA.

entities.name: MIR19A
entities.description: Encodes miR-19a-3p, named as one of the three most abundant microRNAs measured, but not a driver of any of the reported topic separations.

entities.name: miR-21-dominated spatial topic (topic 2)
entities.description: An LDA topic, a recurring microRNA mixture weighted toward miR-21, whose spatial coverage loads positively on PC1 and marks olaparib-sensitive and combination-treated tumors.

entities.name: let-7a-dominated spatial topic (topic 1)
entities.description: An LDA topic weighted toward let-7a, whose spatial coverage marks olaparib-resistant tumors and, after priming, olaparib-monotherapy sensitive tumors.

entities.name: Olaparib sensitivity
entities.description: The treatment-naive responsive state of these tumors, with olaparib extending time to a 20 mm endpoint to 75 to 78 days; the class that the miR-21-dominated spatial topic marks.

entities.name: Acquired PARP inhibitor resistance
entities.description: The state of tumors grown through continuous olaparib, with time to endpoint falling to 23 to 24 days; its underlying mechanism is never determined in this paper.

entities.name: Tumor growth to 20 mm endpoint
entities.description: The efficacy readout of the survival studies, measured as time for the longest tumor dimension to reach 20 mm.

entities.name: Triple-negative breast cancer
entities.description: The disease context: BRCA1-related triple-negative breast cancer, modelled here by BRCA1-null, p53-null mouse mammary tumors.

entities.name: K14-Cre Brca1 flox/flox Trp53 flox/flox mouse mammary tumor model
entities.description: The only model system in the paper: conditional Brca1 and Trp53 deletion driven by a Keratin 14 promoter, with tumor fragments transplanted orthotopically into FVB/NJ hosts as sensitive or olaparib-resistant lines.

entities.name: KRT14
entities.description: Keratin 14, whose promoter drives the Cre recombinase in this model; as background biology it is a basal and myoepithelial keratin of the mammary epithelium, a point the paper itself never discusses.

entities.name: Mammary basal and myoepithelial cell
entities.description: The mammary compartment that expresses Keratin 14 and is therefore targeted by the K14-Cre driver; relevant as background for interpreting the tumor cell of origin, and not addressed anywhere in the paper.

entities.name: Mammary gland
entities.description: Site of tumor origin and of orthotopic transplantation into the mammary fat pad.

entities.name: Hydrogel nanoliter-well in situ microRNA assay
entities.description: The spatial measurement platform: an array of nanoliter wells containing hydrogel posts with DNA capture probes, one post position per target microRNA, read out after rolling circle amplification; it produced the seven-plex spatial microRNA maps.

entities.name: Rolling circle amplification
entities.description: Isothermal DNA amplification that converts each captured microRNA into a long repeated product carrying many labelling sites, which is how the assay turns a bound microRNA into a measurable fluorescent signal.

entities.name: Latent Dirichlet allocation
entities.description: Topic model that treats each tissue patch as a document and each microRNA as a word, learning a small number of recurring microRNA mixtures and mapping which mixture dominates where; run with four topics on the microRNA data and three topics on the similarity maps.

entities.name: Principal component analysis
entities.description: Dimensionality reduction applied to per-tumor topic percentages, producing the PC1 axis on which sensitive and resistant tumors separated with 96 percent of the variance.

entities.name: Structural similarity index measure
entities.description: Local image comparison statistic, run with a roughly 7 by 7 neighbourhood on 28 by 28 tumor maps, used to ask region by region whether the immune infiltration map is arranged like the let-7a or the miR-21 topic map.

relations.evidence: BRCA1 is required for homologous recombination repair of DNA double-strand breaks, so its loss leaves the accurate repair route unavailable.
Germline BRCA1/2 mutation defines the subset of triple-negative breast cancer that the paper addresses.
Olaparib is a PARP inhibitor; blocking PARP stalls and collapses replication forks, which is lethal without homologous recombination.
Roughly 40 to 70 percent of patients with BRCA1/2-related breast cancer fail to respond to PARP inhibitors or develop resistance over time.
Alpelisib is a PI3K inhibitor, active in tumors with mutant and with wild-type PIK3CA.
PIK3CA is the PI3K catalytic subunit most often mutated in breast cancer and is cited as the usual target rationale for PI3K inhibitors.
PIK3CB is cited as required for double-strand break sensing because it regulates recruitment of NBN to damaged DNA.
PIK3CB is a PI3K catalytic subunit, which is how PI3K inhibition is linked to the DNA damage response.
Poly(I:C) is a double-stranded RNA mimic that engages receptors including Toll-like receptor 3.
Poly(I:C) activates dendritic cells through surface receptors such as Toll-like receptor 3.
Activated dendritic cells in turn activate CD8-positive T cells, which is the cited rationale for pairing poly(I:C) with olaparib.
The authors' earlier work reported that olaparib increased CD8-positive T cell infiltration and activation; cited background, not measured in this paper.
The authors' earlier work reported that olaparib increased tumor-associated macrophages; cited background, not measured in this paper.

Keratin 14 is a basal and myoepithelial keratin of the mammary epithelium, so the K14-Cre driver targets that compartment. This is background biology; the paper never discusses basal or luminal compartments or cell of origin.
The Keratin 14 promoter drives Cre recombinase in the K14-Cre Brca1 flox/flox Trp53 flox/flox model, which is what restricts Brca1 and Trp53 deletion to K14-expressing cells.
The model carries floxed Brca1 alleles that are deleted by K14-Cre.
The model carries floxed Trp53 alleles deleted alongside Brca1 by K14-Cre.
Tumors arise in the mammary gland and transplanted fragments are implanted orthotopically into the mammary fat pad of FVB/NJ recipients.
The model is used throughout as a mouse model of BRCA1-related triple-negative breast cancer.

Olaparib extended median time to the 20 mm endpoint to 75 to 78 days versus 19 to 23 days for control in sensitive tumors (p < 0.001), and to 23 to 24 days versus 17 days in resistant tumors (p = 0.003).
Adding alpelisib to olaparib extended time to endpoint from 75 to 115 days in sensitive tumors (p < 0.001) and from 23 to 39 days in acquired-resistant tumors (p = 0.018).

Adding poly(I:C) to olaparib extended time to endpoint from 78 to 120 days in sensitive tumors (p < 0.001), the first such demonstration, but gave only 30 versus 24 days in resistant tumors (p = 0.567, not significant).

In bulk per-tumor analysis, let-7a was lower in olaparib plus poly(I:C) tumors than in olaparib alone, in both sensitive and resistant tumors, both adjusted p = 0.01; the only bulk microRNA difference found.
miR-21-5p was among the three most abundant of the seven measured microRNAs in these tumors, with let-7a-5p and miR-19a-3p.
let-7a-5p was among the three most abundant of the seven measured microRNAs in these tumors.
miR-19a-3p was among the three most abundant of the seven measured microRNAs in these tumors.
miR-21 is cited in the Results as an oncogenic microRNA in breast cancer, which is the stated reason for examining immune infiltration alongside the topics.
let-7a is cited in the Results as a tumor-suppressive microRNA, alongside miR-21 as an oncogene.
Topic 2 of the four-topic LDA is dominated by miR-21, with a top probability of about 0.88 in the sensitive-only model.
Topic 1 of the four-topic LDA is dominated by let-7a, with a top probability of about 0.92 in the sensitive-only model.

Tumor coverage by the miR-21-dominated topic loaded positively on PC1, and sensitive tumors sat at positive PC1 with median 0.42 versus -0.083 for resistant tumors (Mann-Whitney U p < 0.001, n = 9 per group).
Tumor coverage by the let-7a-dominated topic loaded negatively on PC1, where acquired-resistant tumors sat.

After priming, the regions that switched between the two topics were those where let-7a and miR-21 levels were already nearly equal, since the top weights differ by only about 4 percent, so the treatment separation rests on locally balanced microregions.
Structural similarity mapping showed that in most tumors, sensitive or resistant, the immune infiltration map was arranged more like the let-7a-dominated topic map than the miR-21-dominated one.

The exception was olaparib plus poly(I:C)-treated sensitive tumors, where immune infiltration structure matched the miR-21-dominated topic, concentrated where miR-21 regions bordered let-7a-associated immune regions, with total immune counts not substantially different.
CD45, encoded by PTPRC, is the pan-leukocyte marker stained by immunohistochemistry and counted in QuPath to define tumor-infiltrating immune cells; no subset is resolved.
miR-21-5p is one of seven microRNAs quantified in situ by the hydrogel nanoliter-well array; this is the paper's measurement route rather than a biological finding.
let-7a-5p is quantified in situ by the same hydrogel nanoliter-well array on formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded sections.
Captured microRNA and DNA probe complexes are amplified by rolling circle amplification and fluorescently labelled, which is how the array generates signal.
The spatial topics are the output of a four-topic latent Dirichlet allocation model trained in MATLAB by collapsed Gibbs sampling on 115,248 spatial data points.
The let-7a-dominated topic is likewise an output of the same latent Dirichlet allocation model.
Sensitivity status was separated by principal component analysis of per-tumor topic percentages, with PC1 carrying 96 percent of the variance and tested by two-sided Mann-Whitney U.
The spatial relationship between immune infiltration and each microRNA topic map was quantified with MATLAB's structural similarity index, using a roughly 7 by 7 neighbourhood on 28 by 28 tumor maps.

papers.title: Micronuclear ecDNA constrains tumor cell fitness and is associated with favorable patient survival
papers.authors: Lotte Bruckner, Robin Xu, Jun Tang, et al.

bibliographic.title: Micronuclear ecDNA constrains tumor cell fitness and is associated with favorable patient survival

reading.one_line_takeaway: When extrachromosomal DNA is damaged by replication stress it detaches from chromosomes as a cluster, is trapped en masse in a single micronucleus where it loses H3K27ac and stops transcribing its oncogene, and the cell that inherits that micronucleus divides more slowly and dies more often, which at the patient level tracks with better survival in MYCN-amplified neuroblastoma.
reading.tldr: ecDNA is acentric and normally rides along with chromosomes during mitosis by tethering to them, so how it ends up in micronuclei and what that costs the tumor was unknown. Using matched ecDNA versus HSR cell line pairs, oncogene FISH on 275 patient biopsies, live-cell imaging of fluorescently tagged MYC ecDNA, laser microdissection sequencing of single micronuclei, ChIP-seq, RNA-seq and a retrospective neuroblastoma cohort, the authors show that ecDNA is the dominant source of micronuclei in ecDNA-positive cancers and that hydroxyurea-induced replication stress makes damaged ecDNAs coalesce into one cluster, partly via MDC1-CIP2A-TOPBP1, and segregate into a single micronucleus in one daughter cell. Micronuclear ecDNA loses H3K27ac, loses RNA polymerase II serine 5 phosphorylation and largely stops transcribing its oncogene. Daughter cells that inherit a large ecDNA-containing micronucleus take longer to divide again and die more often, and in 86 children with MYCN-amplified neuroblastoma a higher fraction of ecDNA-positive micronuclei at diagnosis was associated with longer overall and event-free survival. The paper stops at fitness and survival and does not measure cGAS, STING, interferon protein or any immune cell readout.
reading.research_question: How do micronuclei arise in ecDNA-driven tumors, what is actually inside those micronuclei, and does sequestering oncogene-bearing ecDNA into a micronucleus change cancer cell fitness and patient outcome?
reading.background: ecDNA is circular, chromatinized, roughly 1 to 2 megabases of DNA that carries oncogenes and their enhancers, and across cancer types its presence tracks with worse outcome than linear chromosomal amplification. Because ecDNA almost certainly has no centromere, it cannot be pulled apart by the mitotic spindle in the normal way and instead depends on tethering to chromosomes to be passed on, which produces uneven, non-Mendelian inheritance and fuels heterogeneity. Separately, micronuclei are small membrane-bound bodies that form at the end of mitosis around chromatin that was left out of the main nucleus; chromatin inside them is known to be epigenetically and transcriptionally silenced and prone to chromothripsis. Earlier work had hinted at a link, since treating ecDNA-bearing cells with hydroxyurea or other DNA-damaging agents raises micronucleus frequency and lowers oncogene levels, and micronuclei can act as intermediates in ecDNA generation. What was missing was a direct account of how micronuclei are generated in ecDNA-positive tumors, what genomic material they actually contain, and whether this helps or hurts the tumor. This paper fills that gap.
reading.study_design: Three layers of evidence. (1) Cell lines: near-isogenic pairs in which the same oncogene sits either on ecDNA or in a chromosomally integrated homogeneously staining region (HSR), namely COLO 320DM versus COLO 320HSR (colorectal, MYC), GBM39EC versus GBM39HSR (glioblastoma, EGFRvIII) and PC3DM versus PC3-HSR (prostate, MYC); plus neuroblastoma lines CHP-212, TR-14, STA-NB10DM, UKF-NB6, Lan5 and SMS-KAN, and small-cell lung line DMS273 which carries MYC and MYCL on separate ecDNA species. COLO 320DM-Tg19 carries TetO-tagged MYC ecDNA visualized with TetR-mNeonGreen plus H2B-emiRFP670 for live imaging. (2) A genetic control for oncogene dose: mouse adult neural stem cells from Trp53 floxed, Myc extrachromosomal-allele mice that form Myc ecDNA after Cre, compared with Trp53 floxed cells overexpressing chromosomally integrated Myc at matched MYC protein levels. (3) Patients: 275 FISH-scored tumor biopsies across neuroblastoma (MYCN, n = 177), breast cancer (ERBB2, n = 58), non-small cell lung cancer (MET n = 29, KRAS n = 8) and liposarcoma (MDM2, n = 3), of which 236 entered the micronucleus frequency comparison and 148 the copy-number stratification; and a separate survival cohort of 86 children with MYCN-amplified, ecDNA-positive neuroblastoma selected from 387 diagnostic biopsies, all sampled before treatment and enrolled in German GPOH trials NB97 (n = 2), NB2004 (n = 67) and the NB2016 registry (n = 17), with median follow-up 6.8 years. The main perturbation throughout is hydroxyurea at 50 to 80 micromolar, with doxycycline-inducible shRNA knockdown of CIP2A, TOPBP1 and MDC1, the CIP2A-lowering compound TD19, CRISPR-Cas9 cutting of ecDNA, and nucleotide transfection as a rescue. Key comparisons are always ecDNA versus HSR, micronucleus versus matched primary nucleus, and hydroxyurea versus untreated.

key_methods.name: Oncogene-specific DNA FISH with Hoechst or DAPI counterstain
key_methods.plain_explanation: Fluorescence in situ hybridization uses a fluorescently labelled DNA probe that sticks only to one specific stretch of the genome, for example the MYC or MYCN gene. Under the microscope that stretch shows up as a coloured dot. A separate dye (Hoechst or DAPI) stains all DNA, so you can see the main nucleus and any small extra DNA-containing bodies beside it. By asking whether a micronucleus contains the oncogene dot, you can label each micronucleus as oncogene-positive or oncogene-negative.
key_methods.how_used: Applied to the three isogenic ecDNA versus HSR cell line pairs, to seven neuroblastoma lines, to mouse adult neural stem cells with Myc probes, and to 275 patient biopsies with probes against MYCN, ERBB2, KRAS, MET or MDM2. Probes were commercial Vysis and ZytoLight dual-colour sets; ecDNA copy number per cell was estimated by counting FISH foci with the Find Maxima function in FIJI. A chromosome 2 centromere probe was used alongside MYCN so that true ecDNA foci could be told apart from whole chromosomes. Triple FISH for CDK4, MYCN and MDM2 was used in TR-14 to test whether different ecDNA species share a micronucleus.
key_methods.why_it_matters: This is the backbone readout of the whole paper, and it is the one assay that could be run on archival patient material. The caveat is that it is a single optical section of a fixed cell, scored partly by hand, so micronucleus counts depend on thresholding and on the plane imaged, and the authors state that the images were not analysed blinded.

key_methods.name: Hydroxyurea-induced replication stress
key_methods.plain_explanation: Replication stress means that DNA replication forks, the moving machines that copy DNA, slow down or stall, which leaves stretches of unreplicated or broken DNA behind when the cell enters mitosis. Hydroxyurea produces this by blocking ribonucleotide reductase and so starving the cell of the nucleotide building blocks that replication needs. It is a controlled, reversible way to create DNA damage that is concentrated at hard-to-replicate regions.
