key_methods.how_used: Cells were treated with 50 to 80 micromolar hydroxyurea for 24 hours up to 3 days, then scored for anaphase DNA clusters, gammaH2AX, micronucleus frequency, micronuclear oncogene content, histone marks and transcription. Nanopore sequencing with EdU and BrdU labelling (DNAscent and forkSense) was used to measure replication fork speed separately on circular ecDNA reads and on linear chromosomal reads, both untreated and after hydroxyurea. Transfection of free nucleotides was used as a rescue to prove that nucleotide depletion, and not some off-target effect of the drug, drove micronucleus formation.
key_methods.why_it_matters: It converts a correlation (ecDNA is damaged, ecDNA is in micronuclei) into a manipulable axis: add stress, get more ecDNA micronuclei. The caveat is that hydroxyurea hits the whole cell, so every downstream hydroxyurea versus control comparison, including the RNA-seq in Fig. 4k, carries general drug effects as well as micronucleation.

key_methods.name: Live-cell imaging of fluorescently tagged ecDNA
key_methods.plain_explanation: An array of TetO DNA sequences was engineered into the MYC ecDNA of COLO 320DM cells; a TetR protein fused to the green fluorescent protein mNeonGreen binds that array, so every copy of the ecDNA glows green in a living cell. Histone H2B fused to the far-red protein emiRFP670 marks all chromatin. The cells are then filmed through mitosis, so you can watch where the ecDNA goes rather than inferring it from fixed snapshots.
key_methods.how_used: COLO 320DM-Tg19 cells in 96-well glass-bottom plates were imaged on a Leica DMi8 widefield microscope with a 63x objective for 60 to 72 hours, in the presence or absence of 50 micromolar hydroxyurea, with z-stacks and deconvolution. Daughter and granddaughter cells were tracked manually after a division in which at least one daughter had a micronucleus, and each was scored as divided, undivided or dead over a 72 hour window (n = 143 individual cells). Micronucleus size was recorded as larger or smaller than 2 micrometres and ecDNA content inside the micronucleus was called high or low relative to the median.
key_methods.why_it_matters: This is the only experiment that links a specific micronucleus to the later fate of the specific cell that inherited it, which is what turns a correlation into a fitness claim. The caveats are that it is one engineered cell line, the imaging is 72 hours (so it measures short-term proliferation and death, not clonal outgrowth), and scoring was manual and unblinded.

key_methods.name: Laser microdissection sequencing of single micronuclei
key_methods.plain_explanation: A laser is used under the microscope to cut a single micronucleus, or its matched primary nucleus, out of a fixed cell grown on a thin membrane slide, and to drop it into a tube. The tiny amount of DNA is then amplified across the whole genome and sequenced. Comparing read coverage over the known ecDNA amplicon coordinates against coverage over the rest of the genome tells you what fraction of the DNA in that one micronucleus is circular ecDNA versus linear chromosome fragments.
key_methods.how_used: TR-14 neuroblastoma cells, which carry three distinct ecDNA species encoding MYCN, MDM2 and CDK4, were treated with 80 micromolar hydroxyurea and dissected on a Leica LMD7 or LMD7000 onto PEN membrane slides. Whole-genome amplification followed the ImmunoGAM protocol, with NEBNext Ultra II libraries sequenced on NextSeq 2000 or NovaSeq X. 18 primary nuclei, 27 single micronuclei and 6 pooled micronucleus samples (5 to 10 micronuclei each) were sequenced, with coverage computed in 25 kb bins over the amplicon coordinates and 100 kb flanks.
key_methods.why_it_matters: It is the only direct molecular inventory of what a micronucleus contains, and it produced the paper's cleanest surprise: 24 of 26 ecDNA-positive micronuclei (92.3 per cent) had no detectable linear chromatin fragment. The caveat is small n, one cell line, and a whole-genome amplification step that can introduce coverage bias on single-cell-scale input.

key_methods.name: Combined immunofluorescence with FISH (ImmunoFISH) on anaphase and interphase cells
key_methods.plain_explanation: Antibodies against a protein or a histone modification are used to stain fixed cells, and in the same cells a DNA FISH probe marks the oncogene. This lets you ask whether a specific protein sits on the specific piece of DNA you care about, rather than just in the cell. Here the antibodies were against gammaH2AX (phosphorylated histone H2AX, a marker of DNA double-strand breaks), phosphorylated RPA2 serine 33 (a marker of replication stress), CIP2A, TOPBP1, MDC1, H3K27ac (a mark of active chromatin), H3K27me3 (a mark of repressed chromatin), Lamin B1 (an inner nuclear membrane protein) and RNA polymerase II phosphorylated on serine 5 of its tail (a marker of transcription initiation).
key_methods.how_used: Applied to fixed COLO 320DM and COLO 320HSR cells, CHP-212, TR-14 and other lines in anaphase and interphase, with and without hydroxyurea, to show that detached DNA clusters in anaphase are gammaH2AX-positive and ecDNA-rich, that CIP2A and TOPBP1 sit on those clusters, that Lamin B1 is higher on oncogene-positive micronuclei, and that H3K27ac and pRNAPII-S5 drop specifically on ecDNA once it is inside a micronucleus. Signal was quantified as Hoechst-normalized corrected total cell fluorescence.
key_methods.why_it_matters: This is what lets the authors say which protein is on which DNA at which stage of mitosis, and it is the evidence that micronuclear ecDNA is epigenetically remodelled rather than simply diluted. The caveat is that fluorescence intensity ratios in small, bright micronuclei are sensitive to focus, background and the chosen normalization.

key_methods.name: Chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing, intron RNA FISH and bulk RNA sequencing
key_methods.plain_explanation: ChIP-seq pulls down DNA bound by a chosen histone modification using an antibody and sequences it, giving a genome-wide map of where that mark sits. Intron RNA FISH uses probes against the intron sequences of a gene; introns are spliced out and destroyed quickly, so an intron signal means the gene is being actively transcribed right now at that spot rather than that old mRNA is lying around. Bulk RNA sequencing counts all mRNA in a population of cells, so you can see which genes and which gene programs go up or down.
key_methods.how_used: H3K27ac and H3K27me3 ChIP-seq was done in COLO 320DM cells treated with hydroxyurea versus untreated (one biological and one technical replicate per condition, NovaSeq X, reads aligned to GRCh38), showing reduced H3K27ac over the MYC ecDNA locus. Intron RNA FISH for MYC was scored in COLO 320DM (n = 102 micronuclei), GBM39EC (n = 109) and PC3DM (n = 104) to classify each micronucleus as transcribing or non-transcribing. RNA-seq compared hydroxyurea-treated with DMSO-treated COLO 320DM cells in three replicates, analysed with DESeq2 and GSEA against the MSigDB hallmark collection.
key_methods.why_it_matters: Together these supply the mechanism offered for the fitness penalty: ecDNA inside a micronucleus is epigenetically shut down and stops producing oncogene mRNA. Two caveats matter. The ChIP-seq is a single biological replicate per condition. And the RNA-seq is a whole-population hydroxyurea versus DMSO comparison, so the hallmark gene sets it returns cannot be attributed to micronucleated cells specifically.

key_concepts.plain_definition: ecDNA is a circular piece of DNA, typically about one to two million base pairs long, that sits in the nucleus of a cancer cell separately from the normal chromosomes. It is packaged into chromatin like a chromosome, and it usually carries one or more oncogenes together with the enhancer sequences that drive them, so a cell can end up with tens or hundreds of copies of an oncogene. Because ecDNA appears to lack a centromere, the structure that the mitotic spindle grabs to pull chromosomes apart, it cannot be divided evenly between daughter cells; it is instead thought to hitch a ride by sticking to chromosomes. In this paper ecDNA is both the object of study and the thing that ends up inside micronuclei.

A micronucleus is a small, separate, membrane-wrapped body of DNA that sits in the cytoplasm next to the main nucleus. It forms at the end of mitosis when a chromosome or a chromosome fragment fails to make it into the reforming main nucleus and instead gets its own small nuclear envelope. Micronuclei are a classic sign of chromosomal instability. The chromatin inside them is handled badly by the cell: it replicates poorly, it is often damaged, it can be shattered and stitched back together (chromothripsis), and it is usually epigenetically silenced. In this paper micronuclei are shown to be, in ecDNA-positive cancers, mostly containers of ecDNA rather than of chromosome fragments.

An HSR is an oncogene amplification that has been re-inserted into a chromosome, producing a long tandem array of copies that stains uniformly along one stretch of a chromosome arm. Functionally it is the linear counterpart of ecDNA: the same oncogene at high copy number, but attached to a centromere-bearing chromosome and therefore inherited evenly at mitosis. Cell line pairs that differ only in whether the amplification is ecDNA or HSR, such as COLO 320DM versus COLO 320HSR, are the key control in this paper, because they let the authors separate effects of high oncogene dose from effects of the DNA being extrachromosomal.

During S phase a cell copies its DNA using replication forks, moving protein machines that unwind the double helix and synthesize new strands. Replication stress is the condition in which these forks slow down, stall or collapse, for example because the cell has run out of nucleotide building blocks, because the DNA is hard to copy, or because transcription machinery is in the way. The consequence is incompletely replicated and broken DNA that the cell carries into mitosis. Hydroxyurea is the classic way to induce it in the laboratory because it blocks the enzyme that makes the deoxynucleotides. In this paper replication stress is the switch that converts occasional ecDNA mis-segregation into frequent, clustered micronucleation.

Since ecDNA has no centromere of its own, the leading model for how it is still passed to daughter cells is that it sticks to the surface of normal chromosomes during mitosis and is carried along with them. Several molecular mechanisms for this hitchhiking have been described, including chromatin acetylation readers, non-coding RNA bridges and sequence elements on the ecDNA itself. The practical consequence is that inheritance is uneven but not random, and that anything which breaks the tether (such as DNA damage on the ecDNA) throws the ecDNA out of the dividing nucleus. This paper shows that broken tethering is what feeds ecDNA into micronuclei.

Rather than each ecDNA molecule going its own way, this paper finds that damaged ecDNAs stick to each other and come off the chromosomes as one lump during anaphase, and that this lump is then wrapped in a single nuclear envelope in just one of the two daughter cells. The practical signature is that a cell with dozens of ecDNA copies ends up with roughly one micronucleus rather than dozens, and that micronucleus is very rich in ecDNA. The authors show this holds even when a cell carries several structurally different ecDNA species, which all end up in the same micronucleus together.

These three proteins form a complex that binds damaged DNA in mitosis and holds broken, acentric fragments together so that they travel as a unit rather than scattering. MDC1 is a DNA damage mediator recruited to gammaH2AX, TOPBP1 is a scaffold for DNA damage signalling, and CIP2A partners with TOPBP1 on mitotic chromatin. The complex is known from work on chromothripsis, where it keeps shattered chromosome pieces together. In this paper it is shown to be at least partly responsible for keeping damaged ecDNAs clustered in anaphase, which is what commits them to one shared micronucleus.

These are chemical tags on the tail of histone H3, the protein that DNA wraps around. Acetylation of lysine 27 (H3K27ac) marks active enhancers and promoters, so it is a signature of DNA that is being transcribed. Trimethylation of the same lysine (H3K27me3) is placed by Polycomb and marks repressed chromatin. ecDNA normally carries high H3K27ac and low H3K27me3, which is part of why its oncogenes are so highly expressed. The paper's result is that once ecDNA ends up in a micronucleus it loses H3K27ac while keeping its low H3K27me3, a combination that the authors suggest distinguishes micronuclear ecDNA from micronuclear linear chromatin fragments.

RNA polymerase II is the enzyme that transcribes protein-coding genes. It has a repetitive tail whose phosphorylation state reports what the enzyme is doing: phosphorylation of serine 5 marks polymerase that has just initiated transcription at a promoter. Staining for pRNAPII-S5 is therefore a way to ask whether a given piece of chromatin is actively starting transcription. In this paper micronuclei have much lower pRNAPII-S5 than matched primary nuclei, which is the protein-level evidence that micronuclear DNA, including ecDNA, is transcriptionally shut down.

CTCF is a simple quantification used throughout the imaging in this paper: for a region of interest drawn around a nucleus or micronucleus, you take the integrated fluorescence intensity and subtract the background expected for that area. Here it is further normalized to the Hoechst DNA signal so that a bright micronucleus is not called positive just because it is dense. Note that in this paper CTCF means corrected total cell fluorescence and has nothing to do with the CTCF chromatin insulator protein, which is a common source of confusion.

key_concepts.term: Event-free and overall survival, and the hazard ratio
key_concepts.plain_definition: Overall survival is the time from diagnosis to death from any cause; event-free survival is the time to disease progression, relapse or death, whichever comes first. A Cox proportional hazards model estimates a hazard ratio, which is the relative instantaneous risk of the event in one group compared to another, or per unit increase of a continuous variable. A hazard ratio below 1 means lower risk. In this paper the hazard ratio for overall survival per one percentage point more ecDNA-positive micronuclei is 0.951, which the authors translate as a 4.9 per cent lower risk of death for each extra percentage point.

For ordinary chromosomes, each daughter cell gets exactly one copy of each, which is Mendelian segregation. ecDNA instead distributes roughly at random because it has no centromere, so a cell with 100 copies might give 60 to one daughter and 40 to the other. This randomness is normally described as the engine of ecDNA-driven heterogeneity and rapid adaptation. This paper argues that micronucleation adds a second, non-random layer on top: when ecDNA is damaged it goes en masse into a single micronucleus in one daughter cell, which makes inheritance markedly asymmetric rather than merely noisy.

figures.label: Fig. 1
figures.title: Cancer cells and tumors with ecDNA have more micronuclei than those with chromosomal amplifications
figures.question: Is ecDNA, rather than general chromosomal instability or high oncogene dose, what drives micronucleus formation in ecDNA-positive cancers?
figures.how_to_read: Panels a and d are schematics of the cell line and patient designs. Panel b plots the percentage of cells with a micronucleus, split into oncogene-negative micronuclei (left block) and oncogene-positive micronuclei (right block), for three ecDNA versus HSR pairs; each dot is an experimental replicate. Panel c shows, for each isogenic pair, the percentage of all micronuclei that contain the oncogene, with lines joining the HSR and ecDNA member of each pair. Panel e repeats the b layout in 236 primary tumors grouped as not amplified, chromosomally amplified or ecDNA-positive, one dot per patient. Panel f shows the oncogene-positive fraction of micronuclei per oncogene cohort. Panel g shows example micrographs with Hoechst in grey, oncogene FISH in magenta and a chromosome 2 centromere probe in yellow; arrowheads mark micronuclei. Panels h and i compare cells in the bottom 30 per cent versus top 30 per cent of ecDNA copy number, in cell lines and in tumors. Panel j bins ecDNA copy number into deciles and plots micronucleation frequency against it. Panel k is the mouse neural stem cell design plus a MYC immunoblot showing matched MYC protein in Myc-ecDNA and Myc-overexpressing cells, and panel l is the micronucleus readout in those mouse cells.
figures.key_result: ecDNA-positive lines have significantly more oncogene-positive micronuclei than their HSR counterparts (P < 0.01 to P < 0.0001) while oncogene-negative micronucleus frequency is unchanged, so the excess is ecDNA-specific and not generic chromosomal instability. The same pattern holds in primary tumors. Micronucleation scales with ecDNA copy number: panel j gives y = 0.117x + 2.782, R squared = 0.835, P = 1.81 x 10 to the minus 8, over 148 tumors and 7 cell lines. Critically, mouse neural stem cells with Myc on ecDNA have elevated micronuclei while cells overexpressing chromosomally integrated Myc at the same MYC protein level do not (P < 0.001), ruling out oncogene dose as the cause. A binomial model elsewhere in the text puts the per-division ecDNA mis-segregation rate at 1.7 per cent (range 0 to 7.8 per cent).

figures.label: Fig. 2
figures.title: Replication stress drives clustered ecDNA detachment and micronucleation via MDC1-CIP2A-TOPBP1
figures.question: What mechanism puts ecDNA into micronuclei, and does DNA damage on the ecDNA trigger it?
figures.how_to_read: Panel a is the experimental schematic (live imaging plus ImmunoFISH, with hydroxyurea, Cas9 double-strand breaks and clustering as the perturbations). Panel b is a time series of a living COLO 320DM-Tg19 cell with MYC ecDNA in green and chromatin in magenta, through mitosis, with dotted outlines marking micronuclei. Panels c and d show CHP-212 anaphases with or without a detached ecDNA cluster and the ecDNA copy number in each class (n = 52 anaphases). Panels e to g compare ecDNA and HSR lines, untreated (UT) versus hydroxyurea (HU), for the fraction of anaphases with a detached cluster and for the fraction of those clusters that are gammaH2AX-positive. Panels h to j show micronucleus frequency and MYC FISH signal inside micronuclei in COLO 320DM versus COLO 320HSR with and without hydroxyurea. Panels k and l show that CRISPR-Cas9 cutting of MYC ecDNA increases the detached ecDNA fraction. Panels m to o show CIP2A and TOPBP1 on the detached cluster, and the loss of clustering when CIP2A, TOPBP1 or MDC1 is knocked down with doxycycline-inducible shRNA.
figures.key_result: ecDNA detaches from chromatids as clusters during mitosis and is packaged into a single micronucleus; cells with detached clusters have higher ecDNA copy number (P < 0.0001). Hydroxyurea strongly increases untethered gammaH2AX-positive ecDNA clusters in anaphase in ecDNA lines but not in HSR lines, and increases oncogene-positive micronucleus frequency and the MYC FISH signal within micronuclei only in COLO 320DM (P < 0.0001). Even in cells with many ecDNA copies, each daughter typically receives a single micronucleus (mean 1.03 per cell in CHP-212 and 1.19 in COLO 320DM). Targeted Cas9 cutting of MYC ecDNA alone raises the detached ecDNA fraction (P < 0.05). Knockdown of CIP2A, TOPBP1 or MDC1 reduces anaphase chromatin clustering in the presence but not the absence of hydroxyurea, without changing overall detachment frequency.

figures.label: Fig. 3
figures.title: Collective entrapment of structurally distinct ecDNAs in the same micronucleus
figures.question: What is physically inside a single micronucleus in a cell that carries several different ecDNA species, and does linear chromosomal DNA come along for the ride?
figures.how_to_read: Panel a is the laser microdissection and single-micronucleus sequencing design. Panel b is a TR-14 metaphase spread with CDK4 in blue, MYCN in yellow and MDM2 in red on separate ecDNA species. Panel c is a heatmap of log2 counts per million read coverage in 25 kb bins across the three amplicons and their flanks, with rows grouped as primary nuclei (n = 18), single micronuclei (n = 27) and pooled micronuclei (n = 6); red means high coverage. Panel d plots the log2 ratio of circular to linear read coverage for each of those three sample classes. Panel e plots, for each micronucleus, cumulative ecDNA length against cumulative linear chromosome fragment length, with the inset pie giving the fraction of ecDNA-positive micronuclei that contained ecDNA only. Panel f compares the amplicon-size normalized fraction of circular reads mapping to each ecDNA species in primary nuclei versus micronuclei. Panel g is a triple-FISH micrograph of one micronucleus. Panels h to j are scatter plots correlating the fluorescence of pairs of oncogenes within the same micronucleus. Panel k counts micronuclei per cell in DMS273 cells after Cas9 cutting of MYC, classified by whether they contain MYC, MYC plus MYCL, MYCL alone, or no amplicon.
figures.key_result: After hydroxyurea, 70 per cent of micronuclei were strongly enriched for all three ecDNA species at once. Micronuclei were markedly enriched for circular over linear DNA compared with their own primary nuclei. 24 of 26 ecDNA-positive micronuclei (92.3 per cent) had no detectable linear chromatin fragment, with only 2 of 26 (7.7 per cent) containing both. Oncogene signals within a micronucleus correlated tightly with each other: CDK4 with MDM2 R = 0.65 (P = 9.6 x 10 to the minus 5), CDK4 with MYCN R = 0.73 (P = 5.6 x 10 to the minus 6), MDM2 with MYCN R = 0.81 (P = 2.4 x 10 to the minus 8). In DMS273 cells, cutting only MYC ecDNA increased micronuclei containing MYC and also dragged the untargeted MYCL ecDNA into the same micronucleus (P < 0.01).

figures.label: Fig. 4
figures.title: ecDNA inside micronuclei loses H3K27ac and largely stops transcribing its oncogene
figures.question: Once ecDNA is trapped in a micronucleus, is it still chromatin-active and still producing oncogene mRNA?
figures.how_to_read: Panel a is the schematic separating anaphase and interphase readouts. Panels b and c show H3K27ac and H3K27me3 immunofluorescence on ecDNA versus chromosomes in anaphase, quantified as Hoechst-normalized CTCF. Panels d and e repeat this for micronuclei versus primary nuclei after hydroxyurea. Panel f is a ChIP-seq difference track (hydroxyurea minus DMSO, delta counts per million) over the MYC locus, showing loss of H3K27ac. Panels g and h show pRNAPII-S5 immunofluorescence and its quantification in micronuclei versus primary nuclei. Panel i shows MYC intron RNA FISH images plus a stacked bar chart of transcribing versus non-transcribing micronuclei in COLO 320DM (n = 102), GBM39EC (n = 109) and PC3DM (n = 104). Panel j plots MYC mRNA z-score in DMSO versus hydroxyurea bulk RNA-seq. Panel k is a dot plot of significantly enriched MSigDB hallmark gene sets between hydroxyurea-treated and DMSO-treated COLO 320DM cells, with dot size for gene count and colour for adjusted P value. Panel l is the GSEA running enrichment plot for MYC TARGETS V2.
figures.key_result: In mitosis ecDNA keeps high H3K27ac and low H3K27me3 unlike bulk chromosomes, but once inside a micronucleus H3K27ac drops significantly (P < 0.0001) while H3K27me3 stays low, and ChIP-seq confirms reduced H3K27ac at the MYC ecDNA locus. Micronuclei have significantly less pRNAPII-S5 than matched primary nuclei (P < 0.001), and in all three cell lines the large majority of micronuclei show no MYC intron RNA FISH signal, meaning no active transcription. Bulk RNA-seq shows reduced MYC mRNA after hydroxyurea (P < 0.0001) and negative enrichment of MYC TARGETS V2 (adjusted P = 4.84 x 10 to the minus 9). Note for the lab: panel k also lists INFLAMMATORY RESPONSE, INTERFERON ALPHA RESPONSE, INTERFERON GAMMA RESPONSE, TNFA SIGNALING VIA NFKB, IL6 JAK STAT3 SIGNALING, COMPLEMENT and ALLOGRAFT REJECTION among the enriched hallmark sets, but the legend and main text give no direction of change for them, do not discuss them, and this is a bulk hydroxyurea versus DMSO comparison of whole cell populations, not a measurement attributable to micronucleated cells.

figures.label: Fig. 5
figures.title: ecDNA-containing micronuclei reduce cell fitness and track with better neuroblastoma survival
figures.question: Does inheriting an ecDNA-containing micronucleus cost the daughter cell, and does that cost show up as better outcome in patients?
figures.how_to_read: Panel a is the live imaging design: 24 hours of 50 micromolar hydroxyurea, then 72 hours of imaging, tracking a parent cell P to daughters F1 and granddaughters F2, with each cell scored as divided, undivided or dead. Panel b is a representative movie montage with chromatin in magenta and MYC ecDNA in green, with dotted circles marking micronuclei, ending in a nuclear fragmentation event at 57 hours. Panel c is a stacked bar chart of cell fates (orange divided, blue cell death, green undivided) for cells with no micronuclei, with low ecDNA micronuclei and with high ecDNA micronuclei (n = 143 cells). Panel d is the clinical design: 86 MYCN-amplified, ecDNA-positive neuroblastoma biopsies at initial diagnosis, FISH-scored for the percentage of cells with any micronucleus and the percentage with an ecDNA-positive micronucleus, then followed through standard GPOH care. Panel e is a Kaplan-Meier overall survival plot with three curves: no micronuclei (n = 46), ecDNA-positive micronuclei at or below the median of 8.3 per cent (n = 21), and above the median (n = 19). Panel f is the summary cartoon contrasting high and low ecDNA retention.
figures.key_result: Daughter cells inheriting a large (over 2 micrometres) ecDNA-containing micronucleus took longer to reach the next division and died more often than their sister cell without a micronucleus, with the effect strongest for high-ecDNA-content micronuclei and independent of ecDNA copy number in the primary nucleus. In patients, neither total primary-nucleus ecDNA copy number nor overall micronucleus frequency correlated with survival, but a high fraction of ecDNA-positive micronuclei was associated with longer overall survival (log-rank P = 0.032) and event-free survival. Modelled continuously, overall survival hazard ratio 0.951 (95 per cent CI 0.914 to 0.990, P = 0.015) and event-free survival hazard ratio 0.956 (95 per cent CI 0.923 to 0.990, P = 0.012), which the authors describe as a 4.9 per cent reduction in risk of death per 1 per cent increase in ecDNA-positive micronuclei. Median follow-up was 6.8 years (range 0.14 to 15.9) for 36 survivors.

key_findings.statement: In ecDNA-positive cancers, micronuclei are predominantly made of ecDNA rather than of chromosome fragments, and the excess micronucleation is caused by the DNA being extrachromosomal rather than by high oncogene dose or by general chromosomal instability.
key_findings.evidence: Fig. 1b and 1c (three isogenic ecDNA versus HSR pairs: oncogene-positive micronuclei elevated, oncogene-negative micronuclei unchanged); Fig. 1e and 1f (236 primary tumors across five oncogene cohorts); Fig. 1k and 1l (mouse Myc-ecDNA versus Myc-overexpressing neural stem cells at matched MYC protein, micronuclei elevated only with ecDNA, P < 0.001); Fig. 3e (24 of 26 ecDNA-positive micronuclei contained no detectable linear chromatin).

key_findings.statement: Replication stress, induced by hydroxyurea or by targeted Cas9 cutting of the ecDNA itself, causes damaged ecDNAs to detach from chromosomes as a single cluster in anaphase and be packaged into one micronucleus in one daughter cell.
key_findings.evidence: Fig. 2e to 2g (gammaH2AX-positive detached clusters rise with hydroxyurea in ecDNA but not HSR lines); Fig. 2h to 2j (oncogene-positive micronuclei and micronuclear MYC signal rise only in COLO 320DM); Fig. 2k and 2l (Cas9 cutting of MYC ecDNA alone raises detached ecDNA, P < 0.05); main text mean of 1.03 and 1.19 micronuclei per cell in CHP-212 and COLO 320DM; nucleotide transfection rescue in Supplementary Fig. 6c,d.

key_findings.statement: The MDC1-CIP2A-TOPBP1 complex is at least partly required for damaged ecDNAs to coalesce into a single cluster, although it does not control detachment itself.
key_findings.evidence: Fig. 2m (CIP2A and TOPBP1 colocalize with detached clusters); Fig. 2n and 2o (doxycycline-inducible shRNA against CIP2A, TOPBP1 or MDC1 reduces clustered chromatin in the presence but not the absence of hydroxyurea, without changing overall detachment frequency); TD19-mediated CIP2A reduction disperses clusters in Supplementary Fig. 8c to 8f.

key_findings.statement: Structurally distinct ecDNA species in the same cell are collectively trapped in the same micronucleus, so damaging one species drags the others in with it.
key_findings.evidence: Fig. 3c (single-micronucleus sequencing of TR-14, 70 per cent of micronuclei enriched for all three species); Fig. 3f (species proportions inside a micronucleus mirror the primary nucleus); Fig. 3h to 3j (pairwise FISH correlations R = 0.65, 0.73 and 0.81); Fig. 3k (Cas9 cutting of MYC in DMS273 co-enriches untargeted MYCL in the same micronucleus, P < 0.01).

key_findings.statement: ecDNA inside a micronucleus is epigenetically remodelled, losing H3K27ac while keeping low H3K27me3, and is transcriptionally silenced, so its oncogene output falls.
key_findings.evidence: Fig. 4d and 4e (reduced H3K27ac in micronuclei versus primary nuclei, P < 0.0001); Fig. 4f (ChIP-seq loss of H3K27ac over MYC); Fig. 4g and 4h (reduced pRNAPII-S5, P < 0.001); Fig. 4i (most micronuclei lack MYC intron RNA FISH signal in COLO 320DM, GBM39EC and PC3DM); Fig. 4j to 4l (reduced MYC mRNA and negative enrichment of MYC TARGETS V2, adjusted P = 4.84 x 10 to the minus 9).

key_findings.statement: A daughter cell that inherits a large ecDNA-containing micronucleus has a measurable fitness penalty: it takes longer to divide again and is more likely to die, independent of how much ecDNA remains in its primary nucleus.
key_findings.evidence: Fig. 5b and 5c (live-cell tracking of 143 COLO 320DM-Tg19 cells over 72 hours after hydroxyurea; higher death and undivided fractions for high-ecDNA micronuclei); Supplementary Fig. 13a to 13d (independence from primary-nucleus copy number).

key_findings.statement: In children with MYCN-amplified, ecDNA-positive neuroblastoma, a higher fraction of ecDNA-positive micronuclei at diagnosis is associated with longer overall and event-free survival, whereas neither total ecDNA copy number nor overall micronucleus frequency is prognostic.
key_findings.evidence: Fig. 5e (Kaplan-Meier, n = 86 split into 46 with no micronuclei, 21 at or below the 8.3 per cent median and 19 above, log-rank P = 0.032); Cox model overall survival hazard ratio 0.951 (95 per cent CI 0.914 to 0.990, P = 0.015) and event-free survival hazard ratio 0.956 (95 per cent CI 0.923 to 0.990, P = 0.012); null results for copy number and total micronuclei in Supplementary Fig. 14b to 14g.

limitations: The paper measures fitness and survival only. It never measures cGAS, STING, type I interferon protein or transcript as a dedicated readout, NF-kB or IRF3 activation, MHC class I, or any immune cell. The one immune-adjacent item is a list of hallmark gene set names in Fig. 4k (inflammatory response, interferon alpha and gamma response, TNFA signaling via NFKB, complement, allograft rejection, IL6 JAK STAT3), and the legend and text give no direction of change and never discuss them.

That Fig. 4k RNA-seq is a bulk comparison of hydroxyurea-treated versus DMSO-treated COLO 320DM cells. Hydroxyurea itself activates DNA damage and stress signalling in every cell, so nothing in that panel can be attributed specifically to micronucleated cells or to micronuclear ecDNA.

No breast cancer cell line or model is used anywhere, and nothing in the paper is ER-positive. Breast cancer appears only as a 58-sample ERBB2 FISH cohort inside the 275-biopsy descriptive analysis. ESR1, CCNE1, BRCA1, estrogen and endocrine or CDK4/6 inhibitor resistance do not appear in the paper at all.

Micronucleus rupture is never assayed. Lamin B1 staining is used only to argue that oncogene-positive micronuclei have an intact inner nuclear membrane (Supplementary Fig. 2a to 2c), and there is no cGAS recruitment, no envelope collapse time course and no measure of how long these micronuclei stay intact.

The survival cohort is small and retrospective: 86 children selected from 387 biopsies, split 46 / 21 / 19, drawn from trials and a registry spanning 1991 to 2022 with different treatment eras. The PDF states that the frequency of ecDNA-positive micronuclei 'remained independently prognostic' but does not name the covariates in the Cox model, and the Nature Portfolio reporting summary marks 'a description of all covariates tested' as not applicable. Standard neuroblastoma risk factors such as age at diagnosis, stage, 1p and 11q status and ALK are not reported as adjusted for. MYCN amplification is held constant by design since all cases are MYCN-amplified.

The association is also direction-ambiguous as published: a tumor with many ecDNA-positive micronuclei may be a tumor that is losing its ecDNA, and the clinical data cannot distinguish a causal fitness penalty from micronucleus count acting as a marker of something else, for example baseline replication stress or proliferation rate.

Mechanistic depth is uneven. The ChIP-seq is one biological replicate per condition (per the reporting summary), single-micronucleus sequencing is n = 27 single micronuclei from one cell line (TR-14), and the whole-genome amplification step on single-micronucleus input can bias coverage.

Imaging scoring was manual and explicitly not blinded (per the reporting summary), micronucleus identification is threshold-dependent, and the authors themselves note that some bodies they call micronuclei may be exclusomes, a distinct cytoplasmic DNA container.

Cause and effect at the level of the micronucleus is still inferential. Hydroxyurea raises micronucleation and lowers fitness, but no experiment selectively removes a micronucleus or selectively re-silences ecDNA without replication stress, so the authors are careful to say that ecDNA silencing probably is not the only mechanism by which ecDNA-positive micronuclei affect cells.

Several key quantities (the per-division mis-segregation rate of 1.7 per cent, the replication fork and nanopore data, the nucleotide rescue, the segregation-asymmetry modelling, the TD19 experiments, the exact P values) live in supplementary figures, tables and the Supplementary Note that are not part of this PDF, so they could not be checked here.
open_questions: Do these ecDNA-rich micronuclei rupture, and if so does cGAS bind the exposed ecDNA? Micronuclear rupture is the step that would connect this entire paper to innate immune sensing, and the paper does not test it. The Lamin B1 result suggesting intact envelopes on oncogene-positive micronuclei could even mean ecDNA micronuclei rupture less than chromosome-fragment micronuclei, which would be the opposite of what an immune model would predict.

Is the survival benefit immune-mediated at all, or purely a cell-intrinsic fitness penalty? Distinguishing these would need immune infiltrate, interferon signature or MHC class I staining on the same neuroblastoma biopsies, none of which was done.

Does ecDNA micronucleation behave the same way in ER-positive breast cancer, where the amplicons of interest are CCNE1, CDK4, MDM2, ERBB2 and ESR1 rather than MYCN, and where the relevant stress is endocrine therapy and CDK4/6 inhibition rather than hydroxyurea?

Is micronuclear ecDNA silencing permanent, or can the ecDNA be reabsorbed into a nucleus and reactivated in a later division? The 72 hour imaging window cannot answer this, and reactivation would change the therapeutic logic entirely.

Can ecDNA mis-segregation be induced pharmacologically at a dose that spares normal cells? The paper proposes targeting mitotic ecDNA retention as a vulnerability, but the only tools shown are hydroxyurea, Cas9 cutting and CIP2A, TOPBP1 or MDC1 knockdown, none of which is ecDNA-selective.

Does the MDC1-CIP2A-TOPBP1 requirement for clustering mean that inhibiting the complex would disperse ecDNA into many small micronuclei, and would that be better or worse for the tumor than one large one?
reading.relevance_to_lab: This paper sits squarely on the bridge between the lab's ecDNA direction and its BRCA1 cytosolic DNA direction, but it only builds the first half of that bridge, so it should be read as mechanism and method rather than as support for the immune chain. What it delivers for the ecDNA direction is direct and usable. It establishes, with the cleanest possible control (isogenic ecDNA versus HSR pairs, plus mouse cells matched for MYC protein level), that extrachromosomal location itself drives micronucleation, and it supplies a working recipe for inducing and scoring micronuclear ecDNA: hydroxyurea at 50 to 80 micromolar for 24 hours to 3 days, oncogene FISH plus Hoechst to classify micronuclei as oncogene-positive or oncogene-negative, a chromosome centromere probe alongside to separate ecDNA foci from whole chromosomes, gammaH2AX and phospho-RPA2-S33 ImmunoFISH to read damage and replication stress on the ecDNA specifically, Lamin B1 to assess micronuclear envelope integrity, H3K27ac and H3K27me3 to read micronuclear chromatin state, pRNAPII-S5 and intron RNA FISH to read whether the oncogene in a micronucleus is still being transcribed, and laser microdissection plus whole-genome amplification to sequence a single micronucleus. Several of these are directly transplantable to the lab's ER-positive breast models, and the oncogene set the paper touches overlaps the lab's list: MDM2 and CDK4 are two of the three ecDNA species in TR-14, ERBB2 appears as a 58-sample breast FISH cohort, and MYC is the main workhorse. The CRISPR-Cas9 cut of one ecDNA species is a particularly clean tool: cutting MYC alone pulled untargeted MYCL into the same micronucleus, which is a way to force ecDNA into the cytosolic compartment without a general genotoxin. For the BRCA1 and cGAS-STING direction, be strict about what is here. The paper measures cGAS nowhere. It measures STING nowhere. It has no interferon protein or transcript readout designed as such, no NF-kB or IRF3 assay, no MHC class I, HLA-C, HLA-E or NKG2A, and no NK or CD8 T cell experiment. It never tests micronuclear rupture. The only immune-shaped item in the entire paper is panel 4k, a dot plot of significantly enriched MSigDB hallmark gene sets in bulk RNA-seq of hydroxyurea-treated versus DMSO-treated COLO 320DM cells, which happens to list inflammatory response, interferon alpha response, interferon gamma response, TNFA signaling via NFKB, IL6 JAK STAT3 signaling, complement and allograft rejection; the paper gives no direction of change for any of them, never mentions them in the text, and the comparison is confounded by hydroxyurea acting on every cell. It would be wrong to cite this paper as evidence that micronuclear ecDNA activates interferon. On models: no breast cancer cell line is used, nothing is ER-positive, and ESR1, CCNE1, BRCA1 and estrogen do not appear anywhere in the paper; breast enters only as FISH-scored archival ERBB2 tumors. The patient survival claim also needs care in lab meeting. The cohort is 86 children with MYCN-amplified neuroblastoma selected from 387 diagnostic biopsies, all pre-treatment, enrolled across GPOH trials NB97, NB2004 and the NB2016 registry spanning 1991 to 2022, split into 46 with no micronuclei, 21 at or below the 8.3 per cent median of ecDNA-positive micronuclei and 19 above. What was correlated was the percentage of tumor cells whose micronuclei contained MYCN ecDNA, scored by FISH on one diagnostic section, against overall and event-free survival. Total ecDNA copy number and overall micronucleus frequency were both null, which is reassuring in that the signal is specific, but the Cox model's covariates are not named in this PDF and the reporting summary marks covariates tested as not applicable, so 'independently prognostic' is not something the reader can verify; MYCN amplification is at least held constant by design. The authors acknowledge the retrospective design and note that they restricted to pre-therapy samples specifically to avoid treatment-induced changes in tumor genetics. Score 4: the mechanism, the assay toolkit and the ecDNA oncogene set are immediately relevant and partly borrowable for direction (1), and this is the best available description of how oncogenic DNA gets from an ecDNA into a cytosolic compartment, which is exactly the upstream step the lab's direction (2) model assumes; it falls short of 5 because there is no breast or ER-positive model, no estrogen or endocrine resistance angle, and no immune measurement of any kind, so it informs the lab's hypothesis without testing it.
discussion_questions: The lab's model starts with cytosolic DNA sensed by cGAS. This paper puts large amounts of ecDNA into micronuclei but never asks whether those micronuclei rupture, and its Lamin B1 data suggest oncogene-positive micronuclei have an intact inner nuclear membrane. Is micronuclear ecDNA actually available to cGAS, or is an ecDNA-rich micronucleus a sealed container that keeps DNA away from the cytosol? Could we test this directly in an ER-positive line by co-staining cGAS, Lamin B1 and oncogene FISH after hydroxyurea?

If ecDNA micronucleation really constrains tumor fitness the way the paper argues, does it also explain part of what we see in BRCA1-deficient cells, where replication stress is chronic? Are the micronuclei in our BRCA1 models made of chromosome fragments, of ecDNA, or of both, and does the composition change which immune readout we should expect?

The paper's survival result inverts the usual ecDNA story: ecDNA presence predicts worse outcome, but ecDNA in micronuclei predicts better outcome. If we were to score ecDNA-positive micronuclei in ER-positive breast tumors with CCNE1 or CDK4 amplification, would we expect the same direction, and would the confounding be worse given that endocrine therapy and CDK4/6 inhibitors are themselves replication stressors applied after the biopsy?

The DMS273 experiment, where cutting MYC ecDNA with Cas9 dragged untargeted MYCL ecDNA into the same micronucleus, is a way to force a specific amplicon into a micronucleus without a general genotoxin. Is that a cleaner entry point than hydroxyurea for asking whether micronuclear ecDNA triggers interferon signalling in our hands, since it avoids the drug confound that undermines panel 4k?

The authors propose targeting mitotic ecDNA retention as a therapeutic vulnerability, and show that knocking down CIP2A, TOPBP1 or MDC1 disperses damaged ecDNA clusters. If dispersal produces many small micronuclei instead of one large one, does that increase the chance of rupture and immune sensing, or does it just produce more silenced ecDNA? Which outcome would we actually want in an ER-positive, endocrine-resistant setting?

Fig. 4k lists interferon alpha, interferon gamma, inflammatory response and TNFA via NFKB among the hallmark sets enriched between hydroxyurea and DMSO, with no stated direction. How much weight, if any, should we give that panel, and what is the minimum experiment that would turn it into a real immune result rather than a drug effect?

nodes.label: ecDNA is acentric and rides on chromosomes to be inherited
nodes.detail: Because ecDNA has no centromere it cannot be partitioned by the spindle and instead depends on tethering to chromosomes, which makes its inheritance uneven and non-Mendelian.

nodes.label: Chromatin trapped in micronuclei is damaged and silenced
nodes.detail: Prior work shows micronuclear chromatin undergoes chromothripsis and epigenetic remodelling and is transcriptionally repressed, and that DNA-damaging agents raise micronucleus frequency in ecDNA-bearing cells.

nodes.label: How do micronuclei form in ecDNA-driven tumors and what does it cost?
nodes.detail: The mechanism of micronucleus generation in ecDNA-positive tumors, the molecular content of those micronuclei and their functional consequences were unknown.

nodes.label: Damaged ecDNA detaches in mitosis and is sequestered in micronuclei
nodes.detail: If DNA damage breaks the tether that carries ecDNA through mitosis, ecDNA should be mis-segregated into micronuclei, and this should be specific to extrachromosomal rather than chromosomal amplification.

nodes.label: Score oncogene-positive micronuclei in isogenic lines and 275 tumors
nodes.detail: Oncogene FISH plus Hoechst in three matched ecDNA versus HSR cell line pairs, seven neuroblastoma lines, mouse Myc-ecDNA versus Myc-overexpressing neural stem cells, and 275 FISH-scored patient biopsies across five oncogene cohorts.

nodes.label: ecDNA, not oncogene dose, drives micronucleation and scales with copy number
nodes.detail: ecDNA lines and ecDNA-positive tumors have more oncogene-positive micronuclei while oncogene-negative micronuclei are unchanged, micronucleation rises with ecDNA copy number (R squared 0.835), and mouse cells overexpressing chromosomal Myc at matched protein level show no increase.

nodes.label: Apply replication stress and watch ecDNA through mitosis
nodes.detail: Live imaging of fluorescently tagged MYC ecDNA plus ImmunoFISH for gammaH2AX, CIP2A, TOPBP1 and MDC1 in anaphase, with hydroxyurea, targeted Cas9 cutting of ecDNA and inducible shRNA knockdowns.

nodes.label: Replication stress makes ecDNA detach as one cluster into one micronucleus
nodes.detail: Hydroxyurea raises untethered gammaH2AX-positive ecDNA clusters in anaphase in ecDNA but not HSR lines, and each daughter cell typically receives a single ecDNA-rich micronucleus (mean 1.03 to 1.19 per cell).

nodes.label: MDC1-CIP2A-TOPBP1 holds damaged ecDNA together as a cluster
nodes.detail: CIP2A and TOPBP1 colocalize with detached clusters, and knocking down CIP2A, TOPBP1 or MDC1 reduces anaphase clustering under hydroxyurea without changing detachment frequency.

nodes.label: Distinct ecDNA species are collectively trapped in the same micronucleus
nodes.detail: Laser microdissection sequencing of single TR-14 micronuclei shows 70 per cent enriched for all three ecDNA species and 92.3 per cent with no detectable linear chromatin, and cutting MYC ecDNA in DMS273 drags untargeted MYCL into the same micronucleus.

nodes.label: Micronuclear ecDNA loses H3K27ac and stops transcribing its oncogene
nodes.detail: ecDNA in micronuclei has significantly reduced H3K27ac with persistently low H3K27me3, reduced pRNAPII-S5, and almost no MYC intron RNA FISH signal, with bulk RNA-seq showing lower MYC and negative enrichment of MYC TARGETS V2.

nodes.label: Cells inheriting ecDNA-rich micronuclei divide less and die more
nodes.detail: Live tracking of 143 cells over 72 hours after hydroxyurea shows delayed next division and higher death in daughters that inherited a large ecDNA-containing micronucleus, independent of primary-nucleus ecDNA copy number.

nodes.label: More ecDNA-positive micronuclei at diagnosis tracks with better survival
nodes.detail: In 86 children with MYCN-amplified neuroblastoma, a high fraction of ecDNA-positive micronuclei was associated with longer overall survival (log-rank P = 0.032; overall survival hazard ratio 0.951) while total ecDNA copy number and overall micronucleus frequency were not prognostic.

nodes.label: ecDNA micronucleation is a fitness penalty, not a neutral accident
nodes.detail: Failure to retain ecDNA during mitosis sequesters and silences the oncogene amplicon, reduces oncogene output and attenuates cancer cell aggressiveness, both in culture and at the patient level.

nodes.label: Forcing ecDNA mis-segregation is a candidate therapeutic strategy
nodes.detail: If mitotic ecDNA retention is what keeps the oncogene expressed, then deliberately damaging ecDNA or breaking its tethering could disarm ecDNA-driven tumors, though no ecDNA-selective agent is demonstrated here.

nodes.label: ecDNA-positive micronucleus fraction is a candidate prognostic biomarker
nodes.detail: The readout is a single FISH stain on an archival diagnostic section, which makes it practical, but the cohort is small and retrospective and the adjusted model's covariates are not reported in the paper.

entities.name: extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA)
entities.description: Circular, chromatinized, roughly 1 to 2 Mb oncogene-bearing DNA outside the chromosomes; the central object of the paper and the main content of micronuclei in ecDNA-positive cancers.

entities.name: micronucleus
entities.description: A small membrane-bound DNA body formed beside the main nucleus at the end of mitosis; shown here to be mostly filled with ecDNA rather than chromosome fragments.

entities.name: homogeneously staining region (HSR)
entities.description: Chromosomally integrated tandem oncogene amplification used throughout as the isogenic control for ecDNA.

entities.name: replication stress
entities.description: Slowed or stalled DNA replication forks, induced here with hydroxyurea; the trigger that converts occasional ecDNA mis-segregation into frequent clustered micronucleation.

entities.name: hydroxyurea
entities.description: Ribonucleotide reductase inhibitor used at 50 to 80 micromolar to deplete nucleotides and induce replication stress in essentially every experiment.

entities.name: TD19
entities.description: Compound used to pharmacologically reduce CIP2A, which dispersed detached ecDNA clusters into individual foci and increased the number of small micronuclei.

entities.name: MYC
entities.description: Oncogene carried on ecDNA in COLO 320DM, PC3DM and DMS273 and on an HSR in the matched control lines; the main amplicon tracked by FISH, ChIP-seq and RNA-seq.

entities.name: MYCN
entities.description: Oncogene amplified on ecDNA in neuroblastoma lines and in the 86-patient survival cohort, scored by FISH in micronuclei.

entities.name: MYCL
entities.description: Second, separate ecDNA species in DMS273 cells; it was co-enriched in micronuclei when only MYC ecDNA was cut with Cas9.

entities.name: EGFR
entities.description: Carried as EGFRvIII on ecDNA in GBM39EC and as an HSR in GBM39HSR, one of the three isogenic pairs.

entities.name: MDM2
entities.description: One of three distinct ecDNA species in TR-14 cells and the amplicon scored in the liposarcoma biopsy cohort.

entities.name: CDK4
entities.description: Another of the three distinct ecDNA species in TR-14 cells, used in the triple-FISH and single-micronucleus sequencing experiments.

entities.name: ERBB2
entities.description: Amplicon scored by FISH in the 58-sample breast cancer biopsy cohort within the 275-tumor descriptive analysis; the only breast cancer material in the paper.

entities.name: CIP2A
entities.description: Component of the mitotic damage complex that colocalizes with detached ecDNA clusters; its knockdown or TD19-mediated reduction disperses those clusters.

entities.name: TOPBP1
entities.description: Scaffold partner of CIP2A on detached ecDNA clusters; knockdown reduces clustering under hydroxyurea.

entities.name: MDC1
entities.description: DNA damage mediator in the same complex; knockdown reduces anaphase chromatin clustering under hydroxyurea without changing detachment frequency.

entities.name: LMNB1 (Lamin B1)
entities.description: Inner nuclear membrane protein stained to assess micronuclear envelope integrity; higher on oncogene-positive than oncogene-negative micronuclei.

entities.name: gammaH2AX (phosphorylated H2AX)
entities.description: Double-strand break marker used to show that detached ecDNA clusters in anaphase are damaged, and that Cas9 cutting produces the same signature.

entities.name: H3K27ac
entities.description: Active chromatin mark; retained on ecDNA in mitosis but significantly lost once ecDNA is inside a micronucleus, confirmed by ChIP-seq over the MYC locus.

entities.name: H3K27me3
entities.description: Repressive Polycomb mark; stays low on ecDNA both in mitosis and in micronuclei, which the authors suggest distinguishes micronuclear ecDNA from micronuclear linear fragments.

entities.name: RNA polymerase II phospho-serine 5 (pRNAPII-S5)
entities.description: Transcription initiation marker, significantly lower in micronuclei than in matched primary nuclei.

entities.name: MYC target gene program
entities.description: MSigDB hallmark MYC TARGETS V2 set, negatively enriched in hydroxyurea-treated COLO 320DM cells (adjusted P = 4.84 x 10 to the minus 9).

entities.name: tumor cell fitness
entities.description: Measured as time to the next division and probability of cell death in live-tracked daughter cells; reduced in cells inheriting large ecDNA-containing micronuclei.

entities.name: overall survival
entities.description: Clinical endpoint in the neuroblastoma cohort, longer in patients whose diagnostic biopsy had a high fraction of ecDNA-positive micronuclei.

entities.name: neuroblastoma
entities.description: The disease of the survival cohort and of several ecDNA cell lines used here; all survival cases were MYCN-amplified and ecDNA-positive.

entities.name: COLO 320DM and COLO 320HSR
entities.description: Near-isogenic colorectal cancer line pair carrying MYC on ecDNA or as an HSR; the main workhorse for imaging, ChIP-seq and RNA-seq.

entities.name: TR-14
entities.description: Neuroblastoma line carrying three distinct ecDNA species (MYCN, MDM2, CDK4), used for single-micronucleus sequencing and triple FISH.

entities.name: DMS273
entities.description: Small cell lung cancer line with separate MYC and MYCL ecDNA species, used to test whether damaging one species drags in the other.

entities.name: mouse adult neural stem cells (Trp53 floxed, Myc ecDNA)
entities.description: Engineered mouse cells in which Myc sits on ecDNA or is chromosomally overexpressed at matched MYC protein level; the control that rules out oncogene dose.

entities.name: oncogene-specific DNA FISH
entities.description: The core readout used to classify each micronucleus as oncogene-positive or oncogene-negative in cell lines, mouse cells and archival patient biopsies.

entities.name: single-micronucleus laser microdissection sequencing
entities.description: Method developed here to cut out one micronucleus or its matched primary nucleus, amplify the genome and sequence it (18 primary nuclei, 27 single micronuclei, 6 pools).

entities.name: live-cell ecDNA imaging (COLO 320DM-Tg19)
entities.description: TetO-tagged MYC ecDNA with TetR-mNeonGreen plus H2B-emiRFP670, used to watch detachment, micronucleation and the fate of each daughter cell over 72 hours.

entities.name: GPOH MYCN-amplified neuroblastoma cohort
entities.description: 86 pre-treatment diagnostic biopsies selected from 387, from trials NB97, NB2004 and the NB2016 registry, with overall and event-free survival follow-up (median 6.8 years).

relations.evidence: ecDNA-positive cells and tumors have significantly more oncogene-positive micronuclei than matched HSR cells and tumors, while oncogene-negative micronuclei are unchanged.

Single-micronucleus sequencing shows circular ecDNA reads strongly enriched over linear reads in micronuclei relative to matched primary nuclei; 24 of 26 ecDNA-positive micronuclei had no detectable linear chromatin.
Hydroxyurea depletes nucleotides and increased markers of replication stress and DNA damage, preferentially on ecDNA; transfecting nucleotides rescued the resulting micronucleus increase.
Hydroxyurea raised the frequency of untethered gammaH2AX-positive ecDNA clusters in anaphase and of oncogene-positive micronuclei in ecDNA lines but not HSR lines.
Nanopore fork analysis showed reduced nucleotide incorporation and disproportionate fork slowing on ecDNA compared with HSRs, both untreated and after hydroxyurea.
Detached ecDNA clusters in anaphase stain positive for gammaH2AX, and Cas9 cutting of MYC ecDNA increases gammaH2AX foci on that amplicon.
CIP2A colocalizes with detached ecDNA clusters in unperturbed cells and more so after hydroxyurea; TD19-mediated CIP2A reduction disperses the clusters.
TOPBP1 immunofluorescence marks the detached anaphase DNA cluster alongside CIP2A.
Inducible shRNA knockdown of MDC1, like CIP2A or TOPBP1 knockdown, reduced clustered chromatin in anaphase under hydroxyurea without changing overall detachment frequency.
Lamin B1 staining intensity was higher in oncogene-positive than oncogene-negative micronuclei, suggesting an intact inner nuclear membrane.
ecDNA in micronuclei had significantly reduced H3K27ac compared with ecDNA in mitosis and in primary nuclei after hydroxyurea, confirmed by ChIP-seq over the MYC locus.
H3K27me3 stayed low on ecDNA both during mitosis and inside micronuclei, unlike bulk chromosomal DNA.
Micronuclei had significantly lower pRNAPII-S5 immunofluorescence than matched primary nuclei.
Intron RNA FISH showed most micronuclei in COLO 320DM, GBM39EC and PC3DM lack detectable nascent oncogene transcription, and bulk RNA-seq showed reduced MYC mRNA after hydroxyurea.
MYC drives the hallmark MYC target program, which is negatively enriched when micronucleation reduces MYC output after hydroxyurea.
Daughter cells inheriting a large ecDNA-containing micronucleus showed delayed progression to the next division and higher death rates than their sister cell without a micronucleus.
A fraction of ecDNA-positive micronuclei above the 8.3 per cent median was associated with longer overall survival (log-rank P = 0.032; hazard ratio 0.951, 95 per cent CI 0.914 to 0.990).
Total ecDNA copy number in the primary nucleus did not correlate with survival in this cohort, in contrast to the published association of ecDNA presence with poor outcome across cancers.
All 86 survival-cohort tumors were MYCN-amplified neuroblastoma with ecDNA identified by FISH before treatment.
Cas9 cutting of MYC ecDNA in DMS273 cells promoted MYC presence in micronuclei while also enriching the untargeted MYCL ecDNA in the same micronucleus.
MDM2 and CDK4 ecDNA fluorescence within the same micronucleus correlated positively (R = 0.65, P = 9.6 x 10 to the minus 5), as did each with MYCN.
HSR lines showed no increase in oncogene-positive micronuclei, and hydroxyurea raised their overall micronucleus rate without putting oncogene sequences into those micronuclei.
Mouse neural stem cells with Myc on ecDNA had elevated Myc-positive micronuclei while Myc-overexpressing cells with chromosomal Myc at matched protein level did not, ruling out oncogene dose.
Oncogene FISH with Hoechst or DAPI counterstain was the primary assay for classifying micronuclei in every cell and tissue experiment.
Laser microdissection of single micronuclei followed by whole-genome amplification and paired-end sequencing quantified circular versus linear DNA content per micronucleus.
Live imaging of tagged MYC ecDNA over 72 hours tracked each daughter cell and scored it as divided, undivided or dead.
Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards analysis of overall and event-free survival in 86 pre-treatment GPOH neuroblastoma biopsies.
In the 58-sample breast cancer biopsy cohort, ERBB2-amplified ecDNA-positive tumors contributed to the higher oncogene-positive micronucleus fraction seen across ecDNA-positive tumors.
TD19 was used for pharmacological reduction of CIP2A expression, which dispersed Hoechst-stained ecDNA clusters and increased small micronuclei per cell.
COLO 320DM carries MYC on ecDNA while its near-isogenic partner COLO 320HSR carries the same amplification integrated as an HSR.
TR-14 carries MYCN, MDM2 and CDK4 on three structurally distinct ecDNA species, confirmed by metaphase FISH and prior sequence reconstruction.
DMS273 carries MYC and MYCL on two separate ecDNA species.
GBM39EC cells, which carry EGFRvIII on ecDNA, had significantly more oncogene-positive micronuclei than GBM39HSR.

papers.source_note: Read from the publisher PDF supplied by the lab (Nature Genetics, 21 pages: article pages 1 to 15 plus a 6-page Nature Portfolio Reporting Summary), covering the full text, all five main figure graphics and legends, the Methods, the data and code availability statements and the reporting summary; there are no Extended Data figures in this file, and the Supplementary Figures 1 to 14, Supplementary Tables 1 to 4, Supplementary Videos 1 to 6, the Supplementary Note (cell culture details, metaphase spread and FISH preparation, microscopy, nanopore fork analysis, single-MN sequencing analysis and the ecDNA segregation model) and the deposited datasets (ArrayExpress E-MTAB-16933 and E-MTAB-16944, ENA PRJEB112294 and PRJEB111610) were not available, so every claim attributed to a supplementary item here is reported only as the main text describes it and the exact P values in Supplementary Table 3 could not be checked.

papers.title: Inverted logic of ecDNA localization converts nuclear periphery into oncogenic transcription hubs in cancer
papers.authors: Y. Wang, X. Yan, N. E. Weiser, et al.

bibliographic.title: Inverted logic of ecDNA localization converts nuclear periphery into oncogenic transcription hubs in cancer

reading.one_line_takeaway: Extrachromosomal DNA carries H3K9me3 that recruits HP1 and docks it onto the lamin B receptor at the nuclear periphery, and instead of being silenced there it clusters into large hubs that raise the transcription of the oncogenes it carries.
reading.tldr: In normal nuclei the shell just inside the nuclear envelope is where silenced, late replicating heterochromatin sits, while active genes move inward. This preprint asks why extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA), which carries highly expressed oncogenes, is nonetheless found at that periphery. Using DNA FISH across six cancer cell lines and several patient tumor types, plus two new single molecule long read assays that write chemical tags onto DNA to record both its nuclear position and its chromatin state on the same molecule, the authors show that peripheral ecDNA keeps open promoters and well positioned nucleosomes, carries the repressive mark H3K9me3 and the active mark H3K27ac at the same time, and is tethered by the lamin B receptor (LBR) through HP1. Removing LBR, or blocking H3K9me3 deposition with chaetocin, pulls ecDNA inward. Peripheral ecDNA replicates late, is CpG hypomethylated over long stretches, and forms the largest ecDNA hubs, and LBR knockout shrinks those hubs and selectively lowers expression of ecDNA encoded genes without changing ecDNA copy number. The authors propose that lamina anchoring turns a three dimensional search into a two dimensional one, so ecDNA molecules find each other more often and amplify each other's transcription.
reading.research_question: How is ecDNA spatially organized inside the cancer cell nucleus, what molecular mechanism puts it where it is, and does that position change how much the oncogenes it carries are transcribed?
reading.background: Chromosomal DNA is organized radially. Lamina associated domains, the parts of the genome that touch the nuclear lamina just inside the nuclear envelope, are gene poor, enriched for the repressive histone mark H3K9me3, replicate late in S phase, and are transcriptionally quiet, while active genes are generally found in the nuclear interior. ecDNA is circular, megabase scale, centromere free DNA that carries amplified oncogenes, segregates unequally at mitosis, and drives tumor evolution, intratumor heterogeneity and therapy resistance. ecDNA was known to be very highly transcribed and to cluster into hubs, and earlier work had noticed peripheral positioning, but the field did not know whether the periphery was incidental, what held ecDNA there, or whether position was functionally important. The gap this paper fills is mechanistic: it identifies the tether, shows what chromatin state makes peripheral activity possible, and tests whether breaking the tether changes oncogene output.
reading.study_design: Cell line panel of ecDNA positive lines from several tumor types: COLO320DM and H716 (colorectal), SNU16m1 (gastric, carrying two separate ecDNA species, one with FGFR2 and one with MYC), STA-NB-10DM and SMS-KAN (neuroblastoma), PC3DM (prostate). Two isogenic comparison lines in which the same amplicon is integrated into a chromosome as a homogeneously staining region rather than carried as ecDNA, COLO320HSR and PC3HSR, give the critical internal control. Patient tissue from colorectal, prostate, gastric, neuroblastoma and glioblastoma tumors was imaged by DNA FISH, but the number of patients is not stated in the text available to me. COLO320DM is the main workhorse for mechanism: the imaging based CRISPR knockout screen, the chaetocin experiment, the replication timing assay, the Hi-C hub analysis and the LBR knockout RNA sequencing are all done in it, with SNU16m1 and PC3DM used to replicate selected single molecule results. Data types: DNA FISH and nascent RNA FISH imaging, lamin B1 and H3K9me3 single molecule long read assays, ATAC sequencing normalized for copy number, CUT and RUN and ChIP sequencing for H3K9me3, H3K27ac, HP1 and lamin B1, whole genome sequencing, Pore-C, Hi-C, RNA sequencing, an in silico polymer style simulation of hub formation, and a correlative analysis of TCGA tumors split by ecDNA status.

key_methods.name: DNA FISH with radial distribution analysis
key_methods.plain_explanation: Fluorescence in situ hybridization uses a fluorescent DNA probe that sticks only to a chosen stretch of the genome, so that stretch lights up as a dot under the microscope. Here the probes target amplified oncogene regions such as MYC, so every ecDNA molecule or cluster appears as a spot inside a DAPI stained nucleus. The analysis then measures, for every spot, how far it sits from the nuclear edge, and compares the whole distribution against what you would get if the spots were scattered at random through the same nuclear shape. Centromere probes for chromosomes 2 and 7 serve as chromosomal reference points.
key_methods.how_used: Applied to six ecDNA positive cell lines and to patient tissue from five tumor types, imaged at the mid nuclear plane for cells and as maximum intensity projections for tissue. The key control was the comparison of COLO320DM against COLO320HSR and PC3DM against PC3HSR, where the same amplicon is chromosomally integrated, so any difference is attributable to being extrachromosomal rather than to the DNA sequence itself. Significance was assessed by two sided permutation tests, 5,000 permutations for the radial distributions and 2,000 for the FISH over random enrichment curves. Pixel size was 0.11 micrometres.
key_methods.why_it_matters: It establishes the central observation, that ecDNA sits closer to the nuclear edge than chance and closer than the same amplicon when integrated into a chromosome, which is what makes the rest of the paper worth doing. The caveat is that FISH spots are optical objects, so one bright spot can be a single circle or a cluster of many, and the paper only resolves this later with intensity based object analysis.

key_methods.name: Lamin B1 DINO-seq
key_methods.plain_explanation: This is a new assay for reading two things off the very same DNA molecule: where that molecule was sitting in the nucleus, and how open its chromatin was. An antibody against lamin B1, the protein mesh lining the nuclear envelope, is used to bring an enzyme called Hia5 to the lamina. Hia5 writes methyl groups onto adenine bases, a tag that human DNA does not normally carry, so any DNA within reach of the lamina gets stamped. Separately, a second enzyme, M.CviPI, methylates cytosines in GpC contexts only where the DNA is not wrapped by a nucleosome or bound by protein, which marks accessible regions. Long read sequencing then reads the native DNA directly and can tell apart the adenine tag (position at the lamina), the GpC tag (accessibility) and the cell's own CpG methylation, all along one single molecule tens of kilobases long.
key_methods.how_used: Run in PC3DM, COLO320DM and SNU16m1. Reads were classified as lamina associated or not, and this classification was validated against bulk lamin B1 ChIP sequencing, showing enrichment at constitutive lamina associated domains and depletion at constitutive interior domains. Accessibility was then compared between lamina associated ecDNA reads and lamina associated chromosomal reads, with three replicates and a two sided Student t test, and reads were aligned on transcription start sites to look for nucleosome footprints. GCG sequence contexts were excluded because the two tags would be ambiguous there, and a DBSCAN clustering step was used to strip signal coming from linker DNA.
key_methods.why_it_matters: Bulk assays average over the whole cell population, so they cannot say whether the open ecDNA and the peripheral ecDNA are the same molecules. This assay answers that directly, and it is the strongest evidence in the paper that peripheral ecDNA is itself accessible rather than there being two separate pools. The caveat is that lamina association is inferred from an enzymatic reach rather than observed in an image, so the distance threshold is a defined cutoff rather than a physical measurement.

key_methods.name: H3K9me3 DINO-seq
key_methods.plain_explanation: The same single molecule idea applied to a histone mark instead of to nuclear position. An antibody against trimethylated lysine 9 of histone H3, the classic mark of silenced heterochromatin, is paired with protein A fused Hia5, so the adenine methylation stamp is written wherever that mark sits. Together with the accessibility stamp, each sequencing read reports both where H3K9me3 is and where the DNA is open along one continuous molecule.
key_methods.how_used: Used in COLO320DM, PC3DM and SNU16m1 to ask whether an open regulatory element and a repressive H3K9me3 patch can coexist on one molecule. Reads at an ecDNA locus were sorted into four classes according to whether they carried H3K9me3, accessibility, both or neither at the ATAC peak, and reads were also ranked by the distance between an accessible element and the nearest H3K9me3 signal. Chromosomal reads were randomly subsampled so that ecDNA and chromosomal read counts matched, which is important because ecDNA is present at high copy number and would otherwise dominate.
key_methods.why_it_matters: This is what turns a correlation into a claim about single molecules. Bulk ChIP data showing both marks on the ecDNA amplicon could simply mean some copies are silent and others are active. Finding 15.5 percent of molecules with an accessible element directly adjacent to H3K9me3 argues instead for a genuinely mixed state on individual circles. The caveat is that 15.5 percent is a minority of molecules, so most ecDNA copies at that locus are not in that mixed state.

key_methods.name: Imaging based (optical) CRISPR knockout screen
key_methods.plain_explanation: A CRISPR screen knocks out many genes one at a time and looks for the knockout that changes a phenotype. Normally the readout is cell growth or sequencing, which cannot see nuclear position. Here the readout is a microscope image. Cells in which a gene was knocked out are labelled with mCherry, control cells are labelled with GFP, the two are mixed one to one and grown in the same well of a 96 well plate, then fixed and probed with DNA FISH. Because both populations sit side by side in the same well and are imaged together, the knockout and control cells experience identical staining and imaging conditions, and the analysis re-identifies which cell was which after imaging. The output for each gene is how far ecDNA has moved relative to the nuclear edge.
key_methods.how_used: Run in COLO320DM with a pool of three guide RNAs per gene delivered by nucleofection, scoring each knockout both by the mean FISH weighted distance of ecDNA to the nuclear edge and by the distance of the peak of the FISH enrichment profile to the edge. Loss of LBR, the lamin B receptor, gave the strongest inward shift of ecDNA, and the knockout was validated separately.
key_methods.why_it_matters: It converts a question about spatial organization into a screenable phenotype and yields the single named molecular tether in the paper. The important caveat, stated by the authors, is that the screen tested a predefined set of nuclear peripheral genes rather than the whole genome, so other tethers could exist, and the number of genes screened is not given in the text available to me.

key_methods.name: Pore-C based single molecule replication timing and localization assay
key_methods.plain_explanation: Pore-C is a way of asking which pieces of DNA were physically close together in the nucleus. The DNA is cut with a restriction enzyme, the cut ends that are near each other in space are ligated together, and the resulting chimeric molecule is sequenced on a nanopore, which reads long enough to recover many contacts from one molecule at once. Replication timing is measured by giving cells a short pulse of BrdU, a nucleotide analogue that is only incorporated into DNA that is actively being copied, then sorting cells by cell cycle stage with a FUCCI fluorescent reporter and asking which reads carry BrdU in early S phase versus late S phase.
key_methods.how_used: In COLO320DM, each ecDNA read was labelled peripheral or interior according to whether its Pore-C contacts were with constitutive lamina associated chromosomal DNA or with constitutive interior chromosomal DNA. Those same two classes of chromosomal DNA acted as built in late and early replicating controls. The BrdU positive fraction was then compared between peripheral ecDNA, interior ecDNA, constitutive lamina associated chromatin and constitutive interior chromatin, across replicates.
key_methods.why_it_matters: It lets the authors assign a replication time to ecDNA molecules sorted by where they were, which no bulk assay can do, and it is the basis for the claim that peripheral ecDNA replicates late. The caveat the authors themselves flag is that peripheral and interior are inferred from contacts with chromosomal reference regions rather than measured optically, so the two groups are defined indirectly.

key_methods.name: Hi-C and FISH object analysis of ecDNA hubs
key_methods.plain_explanation: Hi-C is the population scale version of the proximity ligation idea, producing a genome wide map of which regions contact which. FISH object analysis is simpler: each FISH spot is treated as an object, and its total fluorescence intensity is used as a proxy for how many ecDNA copies are in it, so a bright object is a large hub and a dim one is a single molecule or a small cluster. Plotting object intensity against distance to the nuclear edge therefore asks whether big hubs sit at the periphery.
key_methods.how_used: In COLO320DM, hub intensity was plotted against distance from the nuclear edge, and the same analysis was repeated in SNU16m1 for both of its ecDNA species and in a glioblastoma patient sample. Hi-C contacts were split into ecDNA to ecDNA and ecDNA to lamina associated chromosomal DNA, with lamina associated domains called from lamin B1 ChIP sequencing at a log2 treated over input threshold above zero, and the contact counts were then normalized for how much DNA each class contributes. An in silico simulation varied two parameters, the probability of being at the periphery and the affinity between ecDNA molecules, to see what would be needed to produce the observed hub sizes.
key_methods.why_it_matters: It connects position to the functional output, because hubs are the proposed unit in which ecDNA molecules share enhancers. The headline numbers are a 6.4 fold excess of ecDNA to ecDNA contacts over ecDNA to lamina associated chromosomal contacts, which becomes a close to 40 fold preference once the roughly sixfold greater DNA content of lamina associated chromatin is accounted for. The caveat is that intensity is an indirect measure of copies per hub and that the simulation is a plausibility argument rather than a test.

key_methods.name: TCGA stratification by ecDNA status with AmpliconArchitect
key_methods.plain_explanation: AmpliconArchitect is a computational tool that reconstructs the structure of amplified regions from whole genome sequencing and infers whether an amplification is circular and extrachromosomal rather than integrated in a chromosome. Using it to split a large public tumor cohort into ecDNA positive and ecDNA negative lets the authors ask whether the genes they implicated mechanistically are differently expressed in real tumors.
key_methods.how_used: TCGA tumors were split by inferred ecDNA status and compared for expression of LBR and of several H3K9me3 methyltransferases and HP1 family genes. LBR was reported as significantly higher in ecDNA positive tumors, as were several of the H3K9me3 pathway genes. Cohort sizes and the statistical test are not given in the text available to me.
key_methods.why_it_matters: It is the only evidence in the paper that the proposed machinery is relevant in patient tumors rather than only in cell lines, and it is what motivates calling LBR a candidate drug target. It is purely correlative: higher LBR expression in ecDNA positive tumors does not show that ecDNA requires LBR in those tumors, and the direction of causality is not addressed.

key_concepts.plain_definition: ecDNA is DNA that has broken away from a chromosome and circularized, so it exists as a free circular element of roughly hundreds of kilobases to a few megabases inside the nucleus, separate from the chromosomes. Because it has no centromere, the structure that the mitotic spindle grabs to divide chromosomes evenly, it is handed out unequally when a cell divides. Daughter cells can therefore end up with very different copy numbers, which lets a tumor rapidly amplify or shed an oncogene under selection. In this paper ecDNA is the object whose nuclear position, chromatin state, replication timing and transcription are all being measured, and the amplified oncogenes it carries are MYC in the colorectal and prostate lines and both FGFR2 and MYC in the gastric line.

key_concepts.term: Nuclear periphery and lamina associated domains
key_concepts.plain_definition: The inside face of the nuclear envelope is lined by a protein mesh called the nuclear lamina, built mainly from lamin A, lamin B1 and lamin B2. Large stretches of the genome, typically hundreds of kilobases to megabases long, press up against this mesh and are called lamina associated domains. In almost every cell type studied these domains are gene poor, marked by H3K9me3, replicate late in S phase, and are transcriptionally repressed, while active genes tend to loop away into the nuclear interior. This radial rule is exactly the logic the title says ecDNA inverts, since ecDNA is found at that normally repressive periphery while remaining highly transcribed.

H3K9me3 means that lysine 9 on histone H3 carries three methyl groups. It is deposited by a small set of methyltransferase enzymes and is the defining chemical mark of constitutive heterochromatin, the compacted, silenced fraction of the genome.
