The mark works largely by being read: heterochromatin protein 1 (HP1) binds H3K9me3 directly and then bridges to other proteins, which both compacts the chromatin and can tether it to the nuclear envelope. In this paper H3K9me3 is unexpectedly enriched on ecDNA, HP1 is found on that H3K9me3 decorated ecDNA, and the mark is required for peripheral anchoring, since blocking its deposition with chaetocin releases ecDNA inward.

LBR is a protein embedded in the inner membrane of the nuclear envelope. It has two jobs: an enzymatic role in sterol metabolism, and a structural role as an adaptor that grips both lamin B and heterochromatin, including through HP1. It is one of the main ways cells physically hold silenced chromatin against the nuclear envelope. Here it is identified as the dominant tether for ecDNA: of all the peripheral genes screened, its knockout caused the largest inward relocalization of ecDNA, and knocking it out also shrinks ecDNA hubs and lowers expression of ecDNA encoded genes without changing ecDNA copy number.

An HSR is the other way a tumor can amplify an oncogene. Instead of circularizing into ecDNA, the amplified copies are strung out in tandem and remain inserted inside a chromosome, which under cytogenetic staining looks like a uniform block without the normal banding pattern. HSR amplifications therefore carry essentially the same DNA sequence and the same oncogene as the matched ecDNA, but inherit it normally through the centromere. COLO320HSR and PC3HSR are isogenic HSR counterparts of COLO320DM and PC3DM, and they are the control that makes the paper's argument specific: the peripheral enrichment and the extra transcription track with being extrachromosomal, not with the sequence.

An ecDNA hub is a cluster in which many separate ecDNA circles are held together in one spot in the nucleus rather than diffusing independently. Because the circles are physically adjacent, an enhancer sitting on one circle can act on a promoter sitting on a different circle, so the cluster behaves like a shared pool of regulatory elements and produces far more transcript than the same number of isolated circles would. In this paper hubs are the functional output of peripheral positioning: the brightest, and therefore largest, FISH objects are the peripheral ones, Hi-C shows a strong preference for ecDNA to ecDNA over ecDNA to chromosomal contacts, and removing the LBR tether reduces the frequency of large hubs.

key_concepts.term: Chromatin accessibility and the plus one nucleosome
key_concepts.plain_definition: Chromatin accessibility is how exposed a stretch of DNA is to proteins, as opposed to being wrapped around histones or coated by other factors. Active promoters and enhancers are accessible, which is what assays such as ATAC sequencing detect. The plus one nucleosome is the first histone particle immediately downstream of a transcription start site. When a promoter is poised or active, that nucleosome sits in a sharply defined position, so a crisp plus one footprint in the sequencing signal is read as a sign of transcriptional readiness rather than of random packaging. The paper finds these well positioned footprints on lamina associated ecDNA but not on lamina associated chromosomal DNA, which is the single molecule argument that peripheral ecDNA is primed to transcribe.

A cell copies its genome over several hours of S phase, and different regions are copied at reproducibly different times. Gene rich, active, interior regions tend to be copied early, while gene poor, heterochromatic, lamina associated regions tend to be copied late. Late replication matters because a region still being copied late, while also being transcribed, is more exposed to collisions between the replication machinery and the transcription machinery, which are a known source of DNA damage and mutation. Here peripheral ecDNA is shown to replicate late, and the authors use this to propose both a source of extra mutation, citing enrichment of the SBS8 mutational signature, and a possible vulnerability to drugs that increase replication stress.

key_concepts.term: CpG methylation and long range hypomethylation
key_concepts.plain_definition: CpG methylation is the cell's own addition of a methyl group to cytosine where a cytosine is followed by a guanine. At promoters it is usually associated with silencing, while across gene bodies and large domains it forms broad patterns that track with replication timing and nuclear compartment. Long range hypomethylation means an unusually large stretch has lost that methylation relative to a comparison. In this paper the single molecule long reads show that lamina associated ecDNA molecules are CpG hypomethylated over long distances compared with non lamina associated ecDNA molecules from the same cells, which ties position to an epigenetic state that is normally coupled to late replication.

Chaetocin is a small molecule inhibitor of H3K9 methyltransferases, the enzymes that write the H3K9me3 mark, so treating cells with it lowers the amount of that mark. It is a tool compound rather than a clinical drug and is known to have additional activities, so results with it need confirmation by genetic means. Here a one day treatment at 100 nanomolar reduced H3K9me3 on ecDNA and shifted ecDNA away from the nuclear edge, which is the pharmacological half of the argument that the mark is what anchors ecDNA.

figures.label: Fig. 1
figures.title: ecDNA preferentially localizes to the nuclear periphery across cancer cell lines and patient samples
figures.question: Is peripheral positioning of ecDNA a general feature across cancer types, and is it a property of being extrachromosomal rather than of the amplified sequence itself?
figures.how_to_read: Panel A is the study roadmap, pairing single molecule multi omic sequencing with high content imaging and genetic perturbation. Panel B shows representative DNA FISH images, with the oncogene amplicon in one color and DAPI stained nuclei in another, for COLO320DM and H716 (colorectal), SNU16m1 (gastric), STA NB 10DM and SMS KAN (neuroblastoma) and PC3DM (prostate); cell lines are shown as a mid nuclear optical plane and tissue as a maximum intensity projection, scale bar 10 micrometres, with CEN2 and CEN7 centromere probes as chromosomal reference. Panel C plots the radial distribution of ecDNA distance to the nuclear edge against a uniform random distribution, with dashed lines at the medians and error bars giving 95 percent confidence intervals. Panel D is the key control: MYC FISH enrichment expressed as observed over random, for COLO320DM versus COLO320HSR and PC3DM versus PC3HSR, with shaded 95 percent confidence intervals.
figures.key_result: ecDNA sits closer to the nuclear edge than expected by chance in every line and tumor type tested, with p below 0.001 by two sided permutation test over 5,000 permutations. In the isogenic comparison the ecDNA lines show stronger peripheral enrichment than their HSR counterparts, tested by two sided permutation over 2,000 permutations, so the effect tracks with the DNA being extrachromosomal rather than with the amplicon sequence. Numerical median distances are not given in the text available to me.

figures.label: Fig. 2
figures.title: Peripheral ecDNA remains accessible and transcriptionally active
figures.question: Is the ecDNA that sits at the lamina the same ecDNA that is open and transcribed, or are the active and the peripheral molecules separate populations?
figures.how_to_read: Panel A is the schematic of lamin B1 DINO-seq: a lamin B1 antibody brings nanobody fused Hia5, which uses the methyl donor SAM to write adenine methylation at the lamina, while M.CviPI writes GpC methylation wherever the DNA is accessible, and long read sequencing reads both tags plus endogenous CpG methylation; GCG contexts are excluded as ambiguous. Panel B shows one example read with the three signals side by side. Panel C overlays ATAC sequencing tracks with pseudo bulk accessibility of lamina associated reads at oncogene promoters in PC3DM, COLO320DM and SNU16m1. Panel D is nascent RNA FISH against MYC intronic sequence in COLO320DM, with the radial distribution of RNA signal compared against all nuclear pixels as the random reference, dashed lines at medians, scale bar 10 micrometres. Panel E averages total accessibility of lamina associated ecDNA reads around transcription start sites, with red arrows marking plus one nucleosome footprints. Panel F compares the density of accessible regulatory elements per kilobase of read between lamina associated ecDNA and lamina associated chromosomal reads, with one dot per replicate. Panel G is the interpretive model.
figures.key_result: Lamina associated ecDNA reads retain accessibility peaks at oncogene promoters and enhancers, nascent MYC transcription is detected preferentially near the periphery by two sided permutation test over 5,000 permutations, and crisp plus one nucleosome footprints are present on both lamina associated and non lamina associated ecDNA but absent from lamina associated chromosomal DNA. Accessible regulatory element density is higher on lamina associated ecDNA than on lamina associated chromosomal DNA across three replicates by two sided Student t test. The exact densities and the p value are not given in the text available to me.

figures.label: Fig. 3
figures.title: ecDNA is simultaneously enriched for the repressive mark H3K9me3 and the active mark H3K27ac
figures.question: Does ecDNA carry a repressive heterochromatin mark, and if so, does the repressive and the active state coexist on the same single molecules rather than in separate silent and active copies?
figures.how_to_read: Panel A combines MYC DNA FISH with H3K9me3 immunofluorescence in COLO320DM, with line intensity profiles drawn across a region where the two signals overlap, scale bar 10 micrometres. Panel B stacks whole genome sequencing coverage, H3K9me3 CUT and RUN and copy number normalized ATAC sequencing over the amplicon, with called peaks shown as bars; copy number normalization matters because ecDNA is present at high copy and would otherwise look artificially accessible. Panel C quantifies the fraction of ATAC peaks lying within 1 kilobase of an H3K9me3 peak, ecDNA amplicon versus chromosomal. Panel D is the H3K9me3 DINO-seq schematic. Panel E shows example single reads at one ecDNA locus sorted into four classes by whether they carry H3K9me3 and whether they are accessible at the ATAC peak. Panel F shows reads centered on ATAC peaks and ranked by the distance between the accessible element and the nearest H3K9me3 signal, displaying the top 5 percent for COLO320DM, 5 percent for PC3DM and 2 percent for SNU16m1, with chromosomal reads randomly subsampled to match ecDNA read counts. Panels G and H compare H3K27ac and H3K9me3 ChIP signal, panel H restricting the comparison to genomic regions where ecDNA and chromosomal DNA have matched H3K9me3 levels, split into high, mid and low H3K9me3 bins, shown as kernel density curves with dashed medians.
figures.key_result: More than one quarter of ecDNA ATAC peaks lie within 1 kilobase of an H3K9me3 peak, over fourfold higher than for chromosomal DNA. At the single molecule level 15.5 percent of molecules at the examined ecDNA locus are accessible at the ATAC peak immediately adjacent to H3K9me3 signal. With H3K9me3 held matched, ecDNA still shows higher H3K27ac than chromosomal DNA, p below 0.0001 by two sided Mann Whitney U test.

figures.label: Fig. 4
figures.title: ecDNA is tethered to the nuclear periphery by H3K9me3 dependent, LBR mediated interactions
figures.question: Which nuclear envelope protein physically holds ecDNA at the periphery, and is the H3K9me3 mark required for that anchoring?
figures.how_to_read: Panel A is the design of the optical screen: mCherry positive knockout cells and GFP positive mock nucleofected control cells are mixed and co seeded in the same well, then fixed, FISH stained and imaged, with computational re alignment to recover which cell belonged to which population. Panel B is the screen heatmap, scoring each knockout by two readouts, the mean FISH weighted distance of ecDNA to the nuclear edge and the distance from the edge to the peak of the FISH enrichment profile; the bottom panels show the full FISH enrichment heatmaps for LBR knockout versus wild type, with green arrows at the enrichment peaks, pixel size 0.11 micrometres, three pooled single guide RNAs per gene. Panel C stacks whole genome sequencing, H3K9me3 ChIP sequencing and HP1 ChIP sequencing over the COLO320DM ecDNA amplicon. Panel D shows the per cell mean ecDNA distance to the nuclear edge after 100 nanomolar chaetocin for one day, as boxplots with interquartile range boxes and whiskers at 1.5 times the interquartile range. Panel E is the mechanistic model.
figures.key_result: LBR loss produced the strongest inward relocalization of ecDNA among the genes screened. HP1 ChIP signal is enriched over the H3K9me3 decorated ecDNA amplicon, consistent with the proposed H3K9me3 to HP1 to LBR chain. Chaetocin treatment significantly displaced ecDNA from the nuclear edge by two sided Kolmogorov Smirnov test, with the exact p value shown only in the figure. The number of genes screened is not stated in the text available to me.

figures.label: Fig. 5
figures.title: Peripheral ecDNA shows long range CpG hypomethylation and delayed replication
figures.question: Does peripheral positioning come with the other hallmarks of lamina associated chromatin, namely altered CpG methylation and late replication?
figures.how_to_read: Panel A shows endogenous CpG methylation as HmCG over HCG tracks for lamina associated versus non lamina associated ecDNA reads in COLO320DM and SNU16m1, plus a differential track computed as lamina associated minus non lamina associated, so values below zero mean the peripheral molecules are hypomethylated. Panel B is the schematic of the combined replication timing and localization assay. Panel C explains the classification step: Pore-C reads from the ecDNA amplicon are called peripheral or interior depending on whether their contacts are with constitutive lamina associated or constitutive interior chromosomal DNA. Panel D plots the BrdU positive read fraction in early S versus late S sorted FUCCI cells for four classes, peripheral ecDNA, interior ecDNA, constitutive lamina associated chromosomal DNA as the late control and constitutive interior chromosomal DNA as the early control, with one dot per replicate. Panel E is the summary model.
figures.key_result: Lamina associated ecDNA reads are CpG hypomethylated over long ranges relative to non lamina associated ecDNA reads from the same cells, shown by a predominantly negative differential track. Peripheral ecDNA has a higher BrdU positive fraction in late S than in early S, so it replicates late, while interior ecDNA shows the opposite pattern. No numerical fractions or p values are given in the text available to me.

figures.label: Fig. 6
figures.title: Lamina anchoring promotes large ecDNA hubs and raises transcription of ecDNA encoded genes
figures.question: Does peripheral anchoring increase ecDNA clustering, and does breaking the tether reduce transcription of the oncogenes that ecDNA carries?
figures.how_to_read: Panel A shows representative MYC DNA FISH in COLO320DM with red dashed boxes marking a large peripheral hub and a small interior hub or single molecule, scale bar 10 micrometres. Panels B and C plot mean FISH intensity of each individual ecDNA object, which serves as a proxy for how many copies are in it, against that object's distance to the nuclear edge, shown as mean plus or minus standard error of the mean, in COLO320DM and then separately for the FGFR2 and MYC ecDNA species of SNU16m1. Panel D gives total Hi-C contacts split into ecDNA to ecDNA and ecDNA to lamina associated chromosomal DNA, with lamina associated domains called from lamin B1 ChIP sequencing where log2 of treated over input exceeds zero. Panel E converts those counts into a contact preference by normalizing for the DNA content each class contributes. Panel G is a heatmap of mean ecDNA object area in simulated nuclei as a function of two parameters, intermolecular affinity and peripheral probability. Panel H is gene set enrichment analysis of ecDNA encoded genes after LBR knockout, with normalized enrichment score and nominal p value printed in the panel. Panel I compares differential expression of ecDNA encoded genes against chromosomal genes after LBR knockout, as boxplots with interquartile range boxes and 1.5 times interquartile range whiskers. Panels F and J are models.
figures.key_result: Brighter and therefore larger ecDNA objects are found closer to the nuclear edge, in COLO320DM, in both ecDNA species of SNU16m1 and in a glioblastoma patient sample. Hi-C shows 6.4 fold more ecDNA to ecDNA than ecDNA to lamina associated chromosomal contacts, and because lamina associated chromatin contributes roughly sixfold more DNA content, the normalized intra hub preference is close to 40 fold. In silico, raising peripheral probability or intermolecular affinity, or both, increases mean hub size. LBR knockout reduces the frequency of large hubs and selectively lowers expression of ecDNA encoded genes relative to chromosomal genes by two sided Mann Whitney U test, with no change in average ecDNA copy number. The normalized enrichment score and p value for the gene set enrichment are shown only in the figure.

key_findings.statement: ecDNA is enriched at the nuclear periphery across six cancer cell lines and five patient tumor types, and this enrichment is stronger than for the same amplicon integrated chromosomally as an HSR.
key_findings.evidence: Fig. 1C radial distributions versus a uniform random reference, p below 0.001 by permutation over 5,000 permutations; Fig. 1D isogenic comparison of COLO320DM versus COLO320HSR and PC3DM versus PC3HSR.

key_findings.statement: Peripheral ecDNA stays accessible and transcriptionally primed, in contrast to peripheral chromosomal DNA which is repressed.
key_findings.evidence: Fig. 2C accessibility peaks at oncogene promoters on lamina associated reads in three lines; Fig. 2E well positioned plus one nucleosome footprints on lamina associated ecDNA but not on lamina associated chromosomal DNA; Fig. 2F higher accessible element density on lamina associated ecDNA across three replicates; Fig. 2D nascent MYC intron RNA FISH detected preferentially near the periphery.

key_findings.statement: ecDNA carries the repressive mark H3K9me3 and the active mark H3K27ac at the same time, and in a minority of molecules the two states sit immediately adjacent on the same single molecule.
key_findings.evidence: Fig. 3C, more than a quarter of ecDNA ATAC peaks within 1 kilobase of an H3K9me3 peak, over fourfold above chromosomal; Fig. 3E, 15.5 percent of single molecules accessible at the ATAC peak adjacent to H3K9me3; Fig. 3H, higher H3K27ac on ecDNA than chromosomal DNA at matched H3K9me3 levels, p below 0.0001.

key_findings.statement: LBR is the dominant tether holding ecDNA at the nuclear periphery, acting downstream of H3K9me3 and HP1.
key_findings.evidence: Fig. 4B optical CRISPR screen, LBR knockout gives the largest inward shift of ecDNA; Fig. 4C HP1 ChIP enrichment over the H3K9me3 decorated ecDNA amplicon; Fig. 4D chaetocin at 100 nanomolar for one day displaces ecDNA from the edge.

key_findings.statement: Peripheral ecDNA replicates late in S phase and is CpG hypomethylated over long stretches, whereas interior ecDNA replicates early.
key_findings.evidence: Fig. 5A differential HmCG tracks for lamina associated versus non lamina associated ecDNA reads in COLO320DM and SNU16m1; Fig. 5D BrdU positive read fraction in early S versus late S sorted FUCCI cells, with constitutive lamina associated and constitutive interior chromatin as internal late and early controls.

key_findings.statement: Peripheral positioning favours ecDNA to ecDNA contacts and produces the largest ecDNA hubs.
key_findings.evidence: Fig. 6B and 6C, object intensity rises with proximity to the nuclear edge in COLO320DM and in both ecDNA species of SNU16m1, replicated in a glioblastoma patient sample in Fig. S7; Fig. 6D and 6E, 6.4 fold excess of ecDNA to ecDNA over ecDNA to lamina associated chromosomal Hi-C contacts, close to 40 fold after normalizing for DNA content; Fig. S7 Pore-C showing higher ecDNA to ecDNA contacts for peripheral than interior ecDNA.

key_findings.statement: Breaking the tether lowers oncogene output: LBR knockout reduces large hub frequency and selectively decreases expression of ecDNA encoded genes without changing ecDNA copy number.
key_findings.evidence: Fig. 6H gene set enrichment of ecDNA encoded genes after LBR knockout; Fig. 6I differential expression of ecDNA encoded versus chromosomal genes by two sided Mann Whitney U test; Fig. S7F reduced large hub frequency and Fig. S7G unchanged average copy number.

key_findings.statement: LBR and several H3K9me3 methyltransferase and HP1 family genes are expressed more highly in ecDNA positive than ecDNA negative TCGA tumors.
key_findings.evidence: Fig. S7H and S7I, TCGA tumors stratified by ecDNA status called with AmpliconArchitect. Cohort sizes and statistics are not given in the text available to me.

limitations: This is a bioRxiv preprint and has not been peer reviewed.

The optical CRISPR screen interrogated a predefined list of nuclear peripheral genes rather than the genome, so LBR is the strongest hit within a restricted search space and other tethers may exist. The number of genes screened is not stated in the text available to me.

The core mechanistic experiments, that is the screen, the chaetocin treatment, the replication timing assay, the Hi-C hub analysis and the LBR knockout RNA sequencing, were all done in a single colorectal line, COLO320DM, with only selected single molecule results replicated in SNU16m1 and PC3DM.

Peripheral versus interior ecDNA in the replication timing analysis is inferred from Pore-C contacts with reference chromosomal regions rather than measured optically, so the two groups are defined indirectly and the authors acknowledge this.
Chaetocin is a tool inhibitor with known off target activity, so the H3K9me3 dependence of anchoring rests on pharmacology plus a correlative HP1 ChIP rather than on genetic removal of the writers.
FISH object intensity is an indirect proxy for the number of ecDNA copies in a hub, so hub size is estimated optically rather than counted.

The in silico simulation shows that peripheral probability and intermolecular affinity can together produce the observed hub sizes, but it is a plausibility argument rather than a test of the mechanism.

The TCGA analysis is correlative: higher LBR expression in ecDNA positive tumors does not show that those tumors depend on LBR, and the cohort sizes and statistical tests are not given in the text available to me.
No breast cancer model is included anywhere in the panel, which spans colorectal, gastric, neuroblastoma, prostate and glioblastoma, so whether the mechanism generalizes to breast ecDNA is untested.

The authors do not present a formal limitations section, and most mechanistic and therapeutic statements in the discussion are explicitly hedged, with the heritability of nuclear position called speculative.
The paper offers no functional cancer phenotype: LBR knockout is assayed for ecDNA position, hub size and transcription, but not for proliferation, drug response or tumor growth.
open_questions: Does the H3K9me3 to HP1 to LBR tether operate on breast cancer ecDNA, including the ER positive setting, where no model was tested here?
Is LBR dependence a real vulnerability, that is does LBR loss slow growth, reduce ecDNA retention over passages, or sensitize ecDNA positive cells to therapy, rather than only lowering transcription?
What writes H3K9me3 onto ecDNA in the first place, and why do these circles acquire a heterochromatin mark that chromosomal copies of the same sequence do not acquire to the same extent?

How is a minority state, 15.5 percent of molecules with an accessible element next to H3K9me3, enough to account for the very high transcription of ecDNA encoded genes, and what distinguishes the molecules that are in that state?

If peripheral ecDNA replicates late while being transcribed, can transcription replication conflicts on ecDNA be measured directly, and do they generate the DNA damage, micronucleation and cytosolic DNA that other work links to ecDNA under replication stress?

Does nuclear position influence how ecDNA is passed on at mitosis, and could peripheral anchoring be how combinations of distinct ecDNA species, such as the FGFR2 and MYC circles in SNU16m1, are co inherited?
reading.relevance_to_lab: For the ecDNA arm of the lab this is directly usable. It supplies the first named molecular tether for ecDNA, LBR acting downstream of H3K9me3 and HP1, and a clean separation of position from copy number: LBR knockout moves ecDNA inward, shrinks hubs and lowers ecDNA encoded gene expression while average ecDNA copy number stays the same (Fig. 6I, Fig. S7F, Fig. S7G). That is exactly the kind of handle the lab needs if it wants to ask whether ecDNA position, as opposed to ecDNA dose, matters in ER positive breast cancer. Three things are directly borrowable. First, the isogenic DM versus HSR design: COLO320DM against COLO320HSR and PC3DM against PC3HSR is the control that makes every claim specific to being extrachromosomal, and an ER positive breast equivalent would strengthen any ecDNA claim the lab makes. Second, the two DINO-seq assays, which read nuclear position or a histone mark and chromatin accessibility off the same single long molecule, would let the lab ask whether a breast ecDNA amplicon is peripheral and open on the same circles. Third, the TCGA analysis of LBR and the H3K9me3 methyltransferase and HP1 genes stratified by AmpliconArchitect ecDNA calls (Fig. S7H, S7I) is a cheap reanalysis the lab could immediately repeat restricted to the breast cohort, split by ER status, which this paper does not do. The important caution is about the bridge to the BRCA1 immune work. This paper does not touch micronuclei, cytosolic DNA, cGAS, STING, NF-kB, IRF3, type I interferon, MHC class I, NK cells or T cells at any point. It is entirely about interphase nuclear positioning in cell lines and fixed tumor sections, with transcription as the only functional readout. So it establishes nothing about immune sensing. What it does contribute to that bridge is upstream and indirect, and should be presented as hypothesis generating only. Peripheral ecDNA replicates late (Fig. 5D) while still being transcribed (Fig. 2D), and the authors propose on that basis that transcription replication conflicts raise the mutation rate, citing enrichment of the SBS8 signature, and that ecDNA positive tumors may be sensitive to replication stress targeting therapy. Replication stress is the condition under which ecDNA is reported elsewhere to mis-segregate into micronuclei, and micronuclear rupture is the canonical route by which DNA reaches cGAS, so this paper names a structural reason why ecDNA might be an unusually good substrate for that route, without testing it. The discussion also proposes that ecDNA positive tumors may lean on classical or alternative non homologous end joining, given that the lamina is a site of double strand break repair. That intersects the lab's BRCA1 deficient models, which depend on end joining rather than homologous recombination, and suggests a concrete test of whether BRCA1 status changes ecDNA retention or ecDNA position. Finally the H3K9me3 and HP1 loading on ecDNA is worth noting because heterochromatin binding is one of the ways cGAS activity is tuned on chromatin, but the paper does not test cGAS, so that connection is the lab's to make rather than a result to cite. Practical caveat for the lab: no breast model appears anywhere in the panel, the mechanism rests mainly on one colorectal line, and the paper is a preprint.
discussion_questions: LBR knockout lowers ecDNA encoded gene expression without changing ecDNA copy number. If we could do the same in an ER positive breast ecDNA model, what would we measure as the phenotype that actually matters: proliferation, estrogen response, or the amount of cytosolic DNA and interferon output?

This paper says peripheral ecDNA replicates late while being transcribed, and proposes transcription replication conflicts as a consequence. Is that the mechanistic link we have been missing between ecDNA and the micronuclei and cytosolic DNA in our BRCA1 model, and what is the minimum experiment that would test it rather than assume it?

ecDNA here carries H3K9me3 and loads HP1. Given that heterochromatin and HP1 binding modulate how cGAS behaves on chromatin, does the H3K9me3 coat on ecDNA make ruptured ecDNA micronuclei better or worse at triggering cGAS-STING, and how would we tell those two possibilities apart?

The discussion argues that ecDNA positive tumors may depend on classical or alternative end joining because the lamina is a site of double strand break repair. Our BRCA1 deficient models already depend on end joining. Does BRCA1 loss change ecDNA retention, position or hub size, and is that worth a focused FISH experiment in the models we already have?

Every mechanistic step here rests on COLO320DM, with no breast model in the panel at all. Before we build on the LBR tether, should we first reproduce the basic peripheral enrichment and the isogenic DM versus HSR comparison in an ER positive breast ecDNA line, and which line would we use?

nodes.label: How is ecDNA organized in the nucleus and does it matter?
nodes.detail: The paper asks three linked questions: where ecDNA sits in the nucleus, what mechanism puts it there, and whether that position changes oncogene transcription.

nodes.label: Nuclear periphery is normally silenced, late replicating heterochromatin
nodes.detail: Lamina associated domains press against the nuclear lamina and are gene poor, H3K9me3 marked, late replicating and transcriptionally repressed, while active genes sit in the interior.

nodes.label: ecDNA is centromere free, highly transcribed and clusters into hubs
nodes.detail: ecDNA circles carry amplified oncogenes, segregate unequally because they lack centromeres, are unusually highly transcribed, and are known to cluster so that enhancers on one circle can act on promoters on another.

nodes.label: ecDNA has features that sustain transcription at the periphery
nodes.detail: The authors propose that ecDNA carries a distinct epigenomic and structural state that keeps it active in a normally repressive compartment, and that peripheral position confers a functional advantage rather than being incidental.

nodes.label: DNA FISH with radial analysis, ecDNA lines versus isogenic HSR lines
nodes.detail: Oncogene FISH in six ecDNA positive lines and five patient tumor types, with distance to the nuclear edge compared against a uniform random distribution, and the same amplicon integrated chromosomally in COLO320HSR and PC3HSR as the internal control.

nodes.label: ecDNA is peripheral across cancers, more than matched HSR
nodes.detail: Peripheral enrichment of ecDNA holds in every line and tumor type at p below 0.001 by permutation, and is stronger than for the isogenic HSR counterparts, so the effect follows from being extrachromosomal.

nodes.label: Single molecule lamin B1 DINO-seq links position to accessibility
nodes.detail: A lamin B1 antibody directs Hia5 to write adenine methylation on lamina proximal DNA while M.CviPI marks accessible DNA, and long read sequencing reads both tags plus endogenous CpG methylation on the same molecule.

nodes.label: Peripheral ecDNA is accessible, nucleosome primed and transcribed
nodes.detail: Lamina associated ecDNA reads keep accessibility at oncogene promoters, show crisp plus one nucleosome footprints that lamina associated chromosomal DNA lacks, and nascent MYC transcription is detected preferentially near the periphery.

nodes.label: ecDNA carries H3K9me3 and H3K27ac together, partly on one molecule
nodes.detail: Over a quarter of ecDNA ATAC peaks lie within 1 kilobase of an H3K9me3 peak, fourfold above chromosomal; 15.5 percent of single molecules are accessible adjacent to H3K9me3; and at matched H3K9me3 ecDNA still has higher H3K27ac, p below 0.0001.

nodes.label: Imaging based CRISPR screen of nuclear peripheral genes
nodes.detail: mCherry labelled knockout cells and GFP labelled controls are co seeded in the same well, FISH stained and imaged together, scoring each knockout by how far ecDNA moved from the nuclear edge, with three guides pooled per gene.

nodes.label: LBR tethers ecDNA, downstream of H3K9me3 and HP1
nodes.detail: LBR knockout caused the largest inward relocalization of ecDNA, HP1 is enriched on the H3K9me3 decorated amplicon, and chaetocin treatment that lowers H3K9me3 displaces ecDNA from the edge.

nodes.label: Peripheral ecDNA replicates late and is CpG hypomethylated
nodes.detail: Lamina associated ecDNA reads are hypomethylated over long ranges, and BrdU labelling with FUCCI sorting shows peripheral ecDNA replicating in late S while interior ecDNA replicates early.

nodes.label: Peripheral ecDNA forms the largest hubs and prefers ecDNA contacts
nodes.detail: Brighter, larger FISH objects lie nearer the nuclear edge in three systems, and Hi-C shows 6.4 fold more ecDNA to ecDNA than ecDNA to lamina associated chromosomal contacts, close to 40 fold after normalizing for DNA content.

nodes.label: LBR loss shrinks hubs and lowers ecGene expression at constant copy number
nodes.detail: Knocking out LBR reduces the frequency of large hubs and selectively lowers expression of ecDNA encoded genes relative to chromosomal genes, while average ecDNA copy number is unchanged, and LBR is also higher in ecDNA positive TCGA tumors.

nodes.label: H3K9me3-HP1-LBR docking converts the periphery into a transcription hub
nodes.detail: The authors conclude that ecDNA inverts the usual radial logic: the repressive mark recruits HP1 and LBR to anchor it at the lamina, and anchoring turns a three dimensional search into a two dimensional one so circles find each other and amplify each other's transcription.

nodes.label: LBR, H3K9me3 and replication stress as candidate vulnerabilities
nodes.detail: The discussion proposes LBR and the H3K9me3 and H3K27ac programs as targets, suggests that late replication plus ongoing transcription raises mutation rate consistent with SBS8 and may create replication stress sensitivity, and speculates about end joining dependence and heritable positioning. None of these is tested here.

entities.name: extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA)
entities.description: Centromere free circular DNA carrying amplified oncogenes, the object whose nuclear position, chromatin state, replication timing and transcription this paper measures.

entities.name: LBR
entities.description: Lamin B receptor, an inner nuclear membrane protein identified here as the dominant tether anchoring ecDNA to the nuclear periphery.

entities.name: HP1
entities.description: Heterochromatin protein 1 family, the reader that binds H3K9me3 and bridges to LBR, found enriched on the ecDNA amplicon by ChIP sequencing.

entities.name: H3K9me3
entities.description: Trimethylation of histone H3 lysine 9, the canonical repressive heterochromatin mark, unexpectedly enriched on ecDNA and required for its peripheral anchoring.

entities.name: H3K27ac
entities.description: Acetylation of histone H3 lysine 27, an active enhancer and promoter mark, enriched on ecDNA even at regions with H3K9me3 levels matched to chromosomal DNA.

entities.name: LMNB1
entities.description: Lamin B1, a structural component of the nuclear lamina, used here both as the antibody target that defines lamina proximity in DINO-seq and to call lamina associated domains by ChIP sequencing.

entities.name: nuclear lamina and periphery
entities.description: The protein mesh lining the inner nuclear envelope and the shell of chromatin against it, normally a repressive compartment, which this paper shows ecDNA occupies while staying active.

entities.name: lamina associated domain (LAD)
entities.description: Large genomic stretch in contact with the nuclear lamina, usually gene poor, H3K9me3 marked and late replicating, used here as the reference compartment for ecDNA reads.

entities.name: MYC
entities.description: Oncogene carried on the ecDNA of COLO320DM, PC3DM and one of the two SNU16m1 ecDNA species, and the main FISH and nascent RNA target in this paper.

entities.name: FGFR2
entities.description: Oncogene carried on the second, distinct ecDNA species in the gastric line SNU16m1, used to show that the hub and position findings hold for more than one ecDNA species in the same nucleus.

entities.name: ecDNA hub
entities.description: Cluster of many ecDNA circles held together in one nuclear spot so that enhancers on one circle can act on promoters on another; the largest hubs are found at the periphery.

entities.name: homogeneously staining region (HSR)
entities.description: Tandem amplification of the same oncogene amplicon integrated inside a chromosome, the isogenic control state that shows less peripheral enrichment than ecDNA.

entities.name: accessible regulatory elements
entities.description: Open promoters and enhancers detected by GpC methylation footprinting and ATAC sequencing, present on lamina associated ecDNA but not on lamina associated chromosomal DNA.

entities.name: plus one nucleosome positioning
entities.description: Sharply positioned first nucleosome downstream of a transcription start site, read as a sign of transcriptional readiness and observed on ecDNA including its lamina associated molecules.

entities.name: ecDNA encoded gene transcription
entities.description: Transcriptional output of the oncogenes carried on ecDNA, the functional readout that drops selectively after LBR knockout while copy number stays constant.

entities.name: late DNA replication timing
entities.description: Copying of a genomic region in late rather than early S phase, measured here by BrdU incorporation in FUCCI sorted cells and found for peripheral but not interior ecDNA.

entities.name: long range CpG hypomethylation
entities.description: Loss of endogenous cytosine methylation across long stretches, observed on lamina associated ecDNA molecules relative to non lamina associated ecDNA molecules from the same cells.

entities.name: ecDNA peripheral localization
entities.description: The positional phenotype at the centre of the paper: ecDNA sitting closer to the nuclear edge than chance, scored by FISH radial distribution and by lamina associated read fraction.

entities.name: chaetocin
entities.description: Tool inhibitor of H3K9 methyltransferases, used at 100 nanomolar for one day to lower H3K9me3 and test whether the mark is needed to hold ecDNA at the periphery.

entities.name: H3K9me3 methyltransferases
entities.description: The enzymes that deposit H3K9me3; the paper reports several of them as more highly expressed in ecDNA positive TCGA tumors but does not name which ones in the text available here.

entities.name: JQ1
entities.description: BET bromodomain inhibitor named only in the discussion as a possible way to attack the active, H3K27ac dependent arm of the ecDNA chromatin program; not tested in this paper.

entities.name: SBS8 mutational signature
entities.description: A single base substitution signature cited as background and linked to replication associated processes, invoked in the discussion to argue that late replicating, transcribed ecDNA accumulates extra mutation.

entities.name: COLO320DM
entities.description: Colorectal cancer line carrying MYC ecDNA, the main model in which the CRISPR screen, chaetocin treatment, replication timing, Hi-C hub analysis and LBR knockout RNA sequencing were done.

entities.name: COLO320HSR
entities.description: Isogenic counterpart of COLO320DM in which the same amplicon is chromosomally integrated as an HSR, the control that separates being extrachromosomal from the amplicon sequence.

entities.name: SNU16m1
entities.description: Gastric cancer line carrying two distinct ecDNA species, one with FGFR2 and one with MYC, used to replicate the single molecule, methylation and hub findings.

entities.name: PC3DM
entities.description: Prostate cancer line with MYC ecDNA, paired with the isogenic PC3HSR line and used to replicate the peripheral localization and single molecule chromatin findings.

entities.name: lamin B1 DINO-seq
entities.description: New single molecule long read assay that writes adenine methylation at the lamina and GpC methylation at accessible DNA, so nuclear position and chromatin accessibility are read off the same molecule.

entities.name: H3K9me3 DINO-seq
entities.description: The same single molecule approach retargeted with an H3K9me3 antibody and protein A fused Hia5, used to test whether a repressive mark and an accessible element coexist on one molecule.

entities.name: optical CRISPR knockout screen
entities.description: Imaging based screen in which mCherry labelled knockout cells and GFP labelled controls are co seeded, FISH stained and imaged together, scoring each knockout for ecDNA distance to the nuclear edge.

entities.name: Pore-C
entities.description: Nanopore based proximity ligation assay that recovers many contacts per molecule, used here to classify ecDNA reads as peripheral or interior and to combine that with BrdU replication timing.

entities.name: Hi-C
entities.description: Genome wide proximity ligation assay, used to compare ecDNA to ecDNA against ecDNA to lamina associated chromosomal contact frequencies.

entities.name: DNA FISH
entities.description: Fluorescence in situ hybridization against oncogene amplicons, used for radial distribution analysis, for the screen readout, and for the object intensity analysis of hub size.

entities.name: TCGA pan-cancer cohort
entities.description: Public tumor dataset stratified by ecDNA status called with AmpliconArchitect, used to compare LBR and H3K9me3 pathway gene expression between ecDNA positive and negative tumors.

entities.name: ecDNA positive tumors
entities.description: Tumors in which an amplification is inferred to be extrachromosomal, the clinical group in which LBR and H3K9me3 pathway genes are reported as more highly expressed.

entities.name: glioblastoma
entities.description: One of the patient tumor types imaged by FISH, and the sample in which the peripheral hub size relationship was reproduced in tissue.

relations.evidence: ecDNA sits closer to the nuclear edge than a uniform random distribution in six cell lines and five patient tumor types
MYC FISH enrichment at the nuclear edge is lower in isogenic COLO320HSR and PC3HSR than in the matched ecDNA lines
a substantial fraction of ecDNA long reads carry the lamina proximity tag, validated against lamin B1 ChIP sequencing and against constitutive lamina associated and interior domains
cited background that lamina associated domains are H3K9me3 marked, gene poor and repressed
accessible regulatory element density is higher on lamina associated ecDNA reads than on lamina associated chromosomal reads across three replicates
well positioned plus one nucleosome footprints appear on lamina associated and non lamina associated ecDNA but not on lamina associated chromosomal DNA
MYC is the amplified oncogene carried on the ecDNA of COLO320DM and PC3DM and on one of the two SNU16m1 ecDNA species
FGFR2 is carried on the second distinct ecDNA species of SNU16m1
COLO320DM carries MYC ecDNA and is the main model for the mechanistic experiments
H3K9me3 immunofluorescence overlaps MYC FISH, and CUT and RUN plus ChIP sequencing show H3K9me3 enrichment across the ecDNA amplicon
at regions with H3K9me3 matched between ecDNA and chromosomal DNA, ecDNA still shows higher H3K27ac, p below 0.0001 by Mann Whitney U test

more than a quarter of ecDNA ATAC peaks lie within 1 kilobase of an H3K9me3 peak, over fourfold higher than on chromosomal DNA, and 15.5 percent of single molecules are accessible immediately adjacent to H3K9me3
cited background that HP1 reads H3K9me3 directly
cited background that LBR grips heterochromatin through HP1 at the inner nuclear membrane, invoked as the chain linking the ecDNA mark to the tether
HP1 ChIP sequencing signal is enriched over the H3K9me3 decorated ecDNA amplicon in COLO320DM
in the imaging based CRISPR screen LBR knockout produced the strongest inward relocalization of ecDNA among the peripheral genes tested
chaetocin at 100 nanomolar for one day lowered ecDNA H3K9me3 and significantly displaced ecDNA from the nuclear edge by Kolmogorov Smirnov test
cited background that chaetocin inhibits H3K9 methyltransferases, which is why it was used to lower the mark
chaetocin treatment reduced H3K9me3 on the ecDNA amplicon
peripheral ecDNA reads, classified by Pore-C contacts, show a higher BrdU positive fraction in late S than early S, while interior ecDNA shows the reverse
the differential CpG methylation track of lamina associated minus non lamina associated ecDNA reads is predominantly negative in COLO320DM and SNU16m1
FISH object intensity, a proxy for copies per cluster, rises with proximity to the nuclear edge, and simulations show that raising peripheral probability increases mean hub size

Hi-C shows 6.4 fold more ecDNA to ecDNA than ecDNA to lamina associated chromosomal contacts, close to 40 fold once DNA content is normalized, so ecDNA circles preferentially contact each other and assemble into hubs
LBR knockout reduced the frequency of large ecDNA hubs
hubs are proposed as the unit in which enhancers on one circle act on promoters on another, and disrupting hub formation by LBR knockout lowers ecDNA encoded gene expression
LBR knockout selectively lowered expression of ecDNA encoded genes relative to chromosomal genes with no change in average ecDNA copy number
LBR expression is significantly higher in ecDNA positive than ecDNA negative TCGA tumors; cohort size and test are not stated in the text available here
several H3K9me3 methyltransferase and HP1 family genes are more highly expressed in ecDNA positive TCGA tumors
ecDNA status was assigned to TCGA tumors computationally with AmpliconArchitect from whole genome sequencing
radial distribution of FISH spot distance to the nuclear edge, compared against a uniform random distribution over 5,000 permutations
lamina proximity is recorded as adenine methylation written by lamin B1 directed Hia5 and read on single long molecules
H3K9me3 position and chromatin accessibility were read on the same single molecules using an H3K9me3 antibody with protein A fused Hia5
LBR was identified as the dominant tether in an imaging based CRISPR knockout screen scored on ecDNA distance to the nuclear edge
BrdU pulse labelling with FUCCI sorting into early and late S, combined with Pore-C classification of ecDNA reads as peripheral or interior
hub contacts were quantified as ecDNA to ecDNA versus ecDNA to lamina associated chromosomal Hi-C contacts, normalized for DNA content
lamin B1 is a structural component of the nuclear lamina and is the antibody target used to define lamina proximity
cited in the discussion to argue that late replication combined with ongoing transcription raises mutation rate on ecDNA; not tested in this paper
proposed in the discussion, alongside chaetocin, as a way to attack the active H3K27ac dependent arm of the ecDNA program; the paper does not test it
the relationship between larger ecDNA objects and proximity to the nuclear edge was reproduced in a glioblastoma patient sample

papers.source_note: Read the bioRxiv full text HTML of the fallback preprint at https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.09.11.751063v1.full, which supplied the abstract, introduction, full results narrative, discussion and the complete legends of main figures 1 to 6; the first choice paper (Nature Genetics, doi 10.1038/s41588-026-02782-w) could not be deep read because Europe PMC lists it as subscription required with no PMC deposit, PubTator returned only title and abstract, and the nature.com article page returned a client error on two attempts. Missing from this reading: the preprint page carries no Methods section at all, so all protocol detail (reagents, antibodies, concentrations, incubation times, sequencing depths, analysis parameters, the gene list and gene count of the CRISPR screen, the number of patient samples, and the TCGA cohort sizes and statistical tests) was unavailable; supplementary figure legends S1 to S7 were also not present, so supplementary figures are referenced only by what the main text says about them; and several exact values shown only inside figure panels (median radial distances, the Student t test and Kolmogorov Smirnov p values, the gene set enrichment normalized enrichment score and nominal p value, and the BrdU positive read fractions) are not stated anywhere in the available text.
